title: Senior Advisor, SSE
description:
Metrolinx is connecting communities across the Greater Golden Horseshoe. Metrolinx operates GO Transit and UP Express, as well as the PRESTO fare payment system. We are also building new and improved rapid transit, including GO Expansion, Light Rail Transit routes, and major expansions to Toronto’s subway system, to get people where they need to go, better, faster and easier. Metrolinx is an agency of the Government of Ontario.

At Metrolinx, equity, diversity and inclusion are essential to living our values of serving with passion, thinking forward and playing as a team.

This role is primarily an in‑office position based at our 100 Consilium Place location in Scarborough. Our team is highly collaborative, and much of our work benefits from in‑person co‑creation, relationship‑building, and hands‑on partnership with leaders across the organization.

Our Capital Projects Group workforce is made up of driven and dedicated professionals who care deeply about working together to deliver infrastructure and make a positive impact in our communities. Join us as we build a knowledgeable and collaborative team that courageously changes how transit projects will be delivered.

This role supports project delivery in the Scarborough Subway Extension’s Vice President’s Office by providing infrastructure delivery advice and project management expertise that impacts and supports the successful delivery of the Scarborough Subway Extension project. A core function of this role is to provide solutions that meet corporate needs, stakeholder and customer expectations - all in a timely, safe, and cost-effective manner.

What will I be doing?

  • Supports project delivery by initiating and facilitating productive relationships across the organization to engage stakeholders and enable an integrated and inclusive approach. Coordinates internal and external consultation processes to identify key issues, conduct options analysis, and support project delivery with minimal adverse impact to cost and schedule.

  • Supports the development of memos, reports, and submissions to the Metrolinx Board of Directors and its committees, contributes to provincial government submissions (e.g., Cabinet/Treasury Board Submissions), and coordinates corporate reporting and information-sharing requirements (e.g., briefing/information notes, slide decks).

  • Provides strategic project delivery and issue management support.

  • Assemble and package, stakeholder engagement, current status, and technical information to internal communications and community relations experts to ensure a strong and positive public presence for the project.

  • Collaborates with all levels of management and works cross-functionally across the organization to support internal alignment for matters related to project delivery.

  • Supports and coordinates with all levels within the project team and broader organization on the development, implementation and outcome tracking of continuous improvement initiatives.

  • Disseminates information and communicates ideas on behalf of management to align the primary focus with overall project objectives and ensure accurate resource allocation has been approved.

  • Handles simultaneous complex situations and multiple responsibilities across ongoing activities and identifies the urgency of immediate demands.

What Skills and Qualifications Do I Need?

  • Communication, interpersonal, consultative, and negotiation skills to establish and maintain business relationships and partnerships within the organization, with relevant provincial ministries, other jurisdictions, service providers, and stakeholders to provide expertise and advice, influence decisions, address complex and/or sensitive issues, and present solutions.

  • Written and verbal communication skills to prepare a range of reports and briefings, participate in building and negotiating agreements, and represent the organization on internal and external committees and working groups.

  • Project management skills, including planning, organization, and coordination, determine priorities and meet strict deadlines in a publicly sensitive environment.

  • Strong issues analysis, risk mitigation, and issues management skills to identify complex and contentious project and/or contract issues and make recommendations.

  • Political acuity to anticipate and recognize sensitive situations and respond to issues that may impact Metrolinx with sound recommendations, guidance, advice, and strategies.

  • Knowledge of public sector decision-making structures and processes in Canadian provincial, federal, municipal, and regional governments is an asset.

Don’t Meet Every Requirement?

If you’re excited about working with Metrolinx but your past experience doesn’t quite align with every qualification of this posting, we encourage you to apply. You just might be the right candidate for this or other roles. We are always looking for great talent to join our team.

We invite all interested individuals to apply and encourage applications from members of equity-deserving communities, including those who identify as Indigenous, Black, racialized, women, people with disabilities, and people with diverse gender identities, expressions and sexual orientations.

Accommodation:

We value the unique skills and experiences each person brings to Metrolinx and are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment. We are committed to the requirements of the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act and other applicable legislation so if you require accommodation during the hiring process, please let our Recruitment team know by contacting us at: 416-202-5601 or email hr.recruitment@metrolinx.com.

Application Process:

All applicants must be legally entitled to work in Canada. Metrolinx will be using email to communicate with you for all job competitions. It is your responsibility to include an updated email address that is checked daily and accepts emails from unknown users. As we send time sensitive correspondence, we recommend that you check your email regularly. If no response is received, we will assume you are no longer interested in pursuing the opportunity. Please be advised that a Criminal Record Check may be required of the successful candidate.

For Internal applicants, with the recent implementation of the Internal Mobility Policy, the internal recruitment process has changed for non-union roles. Candidates must be in their current role for 12 months prior to applying for another role and each applicant must be in good standing (not participating in a Performance Improvement Plan). Please review all provisions of the policy before submitting your application.

Should it be determined that any background information provided be misleading, inaccurate or incorrect, Metrolinx reserves the right to discontinue with the consideration of your application.

We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.

WE ARE AN EQUITABLE AND INCLUSIVE EMPLOYER.

title: Senior Manager, Software Development
description:
IMPROVE THE HEALTH OF YOUR CAREER AT ZYNX HEALTH


Zynx Health, part of the Hearst Health Network, is seeking a Senior Manager, Software Development to lead software engineering execution across multiple development teams. This role directly manages Software Development Leads and is accountable for software delivery, engineering quality, release readiness, development practices, resource planning, and cross-team coordination.

This leader provides organizational leadership, standards, governance, coaching, and delivery oversight across teams. DevOps resources are embedded within individual development teams and managed by the respective Software Development Leads; this role provides the cross-team standards, governance, and oversight that keep engineering practices aligned.

This is an opportunity for a people-focused, delivery-oriented engineering leader to strengthen engineering consistency, improve development practices, mature release readiness, reduce technical debt, and support responsible adoption of AI-assisted engineering tools.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Software Engineering Leadership

  • Lead the overall software engineering organization through Software Development Leads.
  • Manage, coach, and develop Software Development Leads, setting clear priorities, ownership, delivery expectations, and accountability.
  • Provide leadership across multiple software development teams, workstreams, and technology platforms.
  • Support team maturity, leadership development, performance management, onboarding, retention, and succession planning.


Delivery Execution and Cross-Team Coordination

  • Own software delivery execution, sprint and release readiness, quality practices, resource planning, and cross-team dependency management.
  • Translate product and technology priorities into clear team plans, delivery expectations, milestones, and execution priorities.
  • Identify and communicate delivery risks, blockers, dependencies, staffing needs, operational concerns, and recommended actions.
  • Partner with product management, architecture, data platforms, security, compliance, QA, and business stakeholders to align delivery execution with business and technology priorities.


Engineering Standards and Development Practices

  • Establish and reinforce consistent engineering standards across teams, including maintainable design, code quality, documentation, testing, code review, release readiness, and operational readiness.
  • Ensure Software Development Leads apply consistent development, CI/CD, operational support, and team-level DevOps practices within their teams.
  • Promote reusable patterns, responsible modernization, automation, and technical-debt reduction while balancing speed, quality, security, and reliability.
  • Define and monitor engineering metrics related to delivery predictability, quality, release readiness, operational health, and team effectiveness.


Embedded DevOps and Operational Readiness

  • Provide governance and oversight for embedded DevOps practices across development teams.
  • Ensure team-level DevOps execution aligns with organization-wide standards for CI/CD, deployment automation, observability, incident response, and operational support.
  • Partner closely with the Senior Manager, Data Platforms & Architecture and the Senior Manager, Security & Compliance on platform, infrastructure, architecture, security, compliance, and operational initiatives.
  • Support continuous improvement in release processes, deployment reliability, observability, and production support practices.


AI-Assisted Engineering and Continuous Improvement

  • Establish expectations for responsible use of AI-assisted coding and engineering tools.
  • Ensure AI-generated code, scripts, documentation, tests, automation, and technical recommendations are reviewed for quality, security, maintainability, and appropriateness.
  • Encourage practical use of AI-assisted tools to improve productivity, troubleshooting, documentation, testing, refactoring, and delivery efficiency.
  • Promote a culture of continuous improvement, engineering accountability, and thoughtful innovation.


REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • 8+ years of experience in software development, software engineering leadership, application development, DevOps, platform engineering, or related technology roles.
  • 3+ years of experience leading or managing software development teams, technical leads, engineering leads, or cross-functional engineering teams.
  • Experience managing software delivery across multiple teams, workstreams, or product delivery areas.
  • Experience leading through technical leads, team leads, or first-line engineering leaders.
  • Strong people leadership, coaching, mentoring, performance management, communication, and team-development skills.
  • Strong understanding of modern software development lifecycle practices, CI/CD, DevOps principles, cloud-native platforms, secure software delivery, and operational readiness.
  • Ability to translate product and technology priorities into clear team plans, execution priorities, and measurable delivery outcomes.
  • Experience partnering with architecture, security, compliance, QA, product management, data platforms, and business stakeholders.
  • Working knowledge of relevant technologies such as Java, Groovy, Spring Boot, Svelte, SvelteKit, TypeScript, Vite, React, .NET Core, C#, MarkLogic, Redis, OpenShift, Kubernetes, Docker, GitLab CI/CD, Tekton, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Keycloak, OAuth2/OIDC, JWT, or related tools.
  • Bachelor's degree preferred, or equivalent practical experience.


PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • Experience in healthcare, clinical content, regulated software, compliance-driven environments, or enterprise SaaS.
  • Experience leading distributed or remote software engineering teams.
  • Experience improving engineering standards, release-readiness practices, CI/CD consistency, or operational support models across multiple teams.
  • Experience guiding responsible adoption of AI-assisted coding or engineering productivity tools.
  • Familiarity with embedded DevOps models, platform engineering partnerships, or shared engineering-practice governance.


About Zynx Health

Zynx Health, a part of Hearst Health, is a market leader in providing evidence-based clinical decision support solutions that help healthcare organizations measurably improve patient outcomes, enhance safety, and lower costs.

Thousands of hospital organizations and providers rely on Zynx Health's rigorously developed and maintained evidence-based clinical content, patented technology, and tailored services to drive clinical improvements at the point of care. Zynx Health partners with healthcare organizations to continuously and measurably improve care every day, for every patient, every time.

Zynx Health seeks to hire and train employees who uphold and mirror our core values of Bold Innovation, Passion, Integrity, Respect, and Excellence. To learn more, visit www.zynxhealth.com.

Zynx Health offers competitive salary and extensive benefits - including medical, dental, vision, short and long term disability, life insurance, and matching 401k.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or protected military and veteran status.

In accordance with applicable law, Zynx is required to include a reasonable estimate of the compensation for this role where required. The reasonable estimate for this role in Dallas, Texas is $160,000 - $180,000. If this role is open to candidates outside of that location, the salary range would be aligned to that specific location. A final decision on the successful candidate’s starting salary will be based on a number of permissible, non-discriminatory factors, including but not limited to skills and experience, training, certifications, and education.

This role is also eligible for a competitive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance; 401(k) retirement plan; flexible spending savings account; paid holidays; paid time off; employee assistance program; and other company benefits.

title: Senior Director of US Product Line
description:
Senior Director of US Product Line

Location: Singapore

Employment type: Full-time

Vacancies: 1

About the Role

This role owns product strategy and lifecycle management for residential energy storage products in the US market and converts market, customer, and certification requirements into executable product roadmaps and release plans.

Key Responsibilities

1. Own the planning, definition, iteration, and full lifecycle management of the residential energy storage product line for the US market. Develop product plans and release strategies based on market trends, user needs, and technical capabilities.

2. Conduct market research, competitive analysis, and user-needs assessment. Produce standardized product requirements documents, specifications, feature plans, and product roadmaps.

3. Coordinate research and development, testing, supply chain, and marketing teams throughout requirements, design, development, validation, launch, and post-launch iteration. Maintain project pace and delivery quality.

4. Lead technical solution reviews, feature definition, performance improvement, and cost optimization to improve competitiveness, stability, and user experience.

5. Collect product operating feedback, market issues, and enhancement requests, and drive continuous product improvement and release upgrades.

6. Establish product requirement baselines, release plans, and requirement-change controls so that sources, priorities, acceptance criteria, and owners remain traceable.

7. Monitor US market policy, certification requirements, competitor activity, and feedback from channels and installers. Produce regular market insights and update product plans accordingly.

8. Define launch criteria and release acceptance standards, lead pre-launch reviews, and track post-launch quality, usage, and customer feedback.

Requirements

9. Bachelor's degree or above in new energy, electrical engineering, power electronics, product management, or a related discipline. At least 15 years of energy storage product experience focused on residential applications. Experience launching products in the North American market is preferred.

10. Deep understanding of integrated residential solar-plus-storage systems and grid-connected and off-grid applications. Familiarity with the product logic and technical architecture of BMS, EMS, and PCS inverter systems.

11. Ability to independently plan a product line, break down requirements, lead delivery, and coordinate across teams. Experience taking a product from concept to launch.

12. Familiarity with product certification, safety, and grid-connection standards applicable to the North American market. Able to write product requirements and specifications in English and communicate with North American customers, partners, and international teams.

13. Familiarity with US residential energy storage use cases, installation processes, channel models, and after-sales issue-closure practices.

14. Ability to use data and customer evidence to support product trade-offs, cost targets, and release-priority decisions.

title: Manufacturing Plant Senior Quality Leader - Dairy

Support plant safety and environmental sustainability initiatives, as well capital projects and Total Productive Maintenance activities. Desired

  • Dairy experience
  • Thorough knowledge of food safety & microbiological concepts
  • Plant QA Assistant Manager or QA Supervisory experience

title: Founding Engineer, Computer Vision & Robotics
description:
About the Role

Join an early engineering team at an industrial automation startup building computer vision systems for quality inspection in manufacturing. You will take perception from experimentation to reliable factory deployments, helping detect process issues early and laying groundwork for future robotic automation.

What You'll Do

  • Build perception systems for detection, classification, tracking, temporal understanding, and 3D vision.

  • Address first-person vision challenges such as camera motion, changing viewpoints, occlusion, motion blur, and variable lighting.

  • Work with the technical team to turn field failures into improvements to models, data, and evaluation.

  • Develop geometric vision capabilities including calibration, localization, pose estimation, and coordinate transformations.

  • Train and debug PyTorch models on synthetic and real-world data.

  • Optimize low-latency inference and deploy systems on edge hardware in factory environments.

What We're Looking For

  • At least 3 years building and deploying computer vision, robotics perception, or applied ML systems outside notebooks or lab settings.

  • Experience shipping real-time perception systems that perform reliably in changing real-world conditions.

  • Strong Python, PyTorch, and OpenCV skills, with experience developing and debugging detection, classification, or tracking models.

  • Experience with geometric vision and edge deployment or production inference optimization.

  • Technical ownership and judgment to lead an underspecified problem end to end, including working directly with users or in field deployments.

  • Experience with synthetic data, Sim2Real, SLAM or VIO, depth or 3D reconstruction, CUDA or TensorRT, ROS2, or robot learning is a plus.

Compensation & Benefits

Annual salary range: $150,000 to $200,000 USD. Visa sponsorship is available.

Location

On-site in San Francisco, California.

title: Souschef - Brøndby Strand
description:
Souschef med ambitioner – er det dig?

I Netto vil vi være kendt for at levere gode kundeoplevelser – og vil du også være med til det, så er denne stilling måske noget for dig?

Som souschef kan du se frem til en masse selvudvikling, karrieremuligheder og ikke mindst fællesskab. Som souschef har du flere ansvarsområder. Til daglig fungerer du både som butikschefens højre hånd og sparringspartner. Og er butikschefen ude af huset, syg eller på ferie, så er det altså dig, der har det overordnede ansvar.

Helt kort så skal du

  • udvikle og træne medarbejdere, og sikre at de er glade og motiverede
  • gå forrest ude i butikken og vise det gode eksempel for dine kolleger
  • løse forskellige administrative opgaver
  • supportere butikschefen i alle typer af opgaver
  • være med til at sikre, at butikken opnår de ønskede driftsresultater
  • være rollemodel for Nettos værdisæt og medarbejderoplevelse, vi kalder det NEX: Netto Employee Experience

Alle de gode grunde
Stillingen er en rigtig god mulighed for at være med i et dagligvareeventyr. Du bliver del af en stærk kultur præget af god energi, engagement og Netto-ånd. Vi har fokus på din personlige udvikling som leder. Du kan også glæde dig til

  • konkurrencedygtig løn, pension og bonusordning
  • sundhedsforsikring
  • masser af gode personaleordninger fx rabatter i Bilka, føtex, Netto, Carl’s Jr. og Starbucks og leje af vores feriehuse og lejligheder i ind- og udland

**Leder- og livserfaring
**I stillingen som souschef er det vigtigt, at du først og fremmest er et ordentligt menneske og har erfaring med at lede mennesker. Og du elsker at sprede trivsel og glæde omkring dig. Mere præcist så forestiller vi dig, at du

  • har ledererfaring
  • er åben over for Nettos holdning til ledelse ved at skabe resultater igennem høj medarbejdertrivsel
  • er nysgerrig og villig til at lære nye ting

**Souschef – blot en begyndelse?
**Du får selvfølgelig en masse god erfaring fra din dagligdag som souschef, men der er også mulighed for at komme på uddannelse og kurser. Måske kan du blive butikscheftrainee, hvor du får helt styr på teorien bag god ledelse. Netto er en del af Danmarks førende retail-koncern, så det kan også være, du på sigt ønsker en stilling hos føtex, Bilka eller på hovedkontoret. Du kan også sigte mod en international karriere.

**Er du vores nye kollega?
**Send din ansøgning til os via linket nedenfor. Vi inviterer løbende til samtale, så søg allerede i dag.

Vi glæder os til at høre fra dig!

Netto – vi bærer vores logo med stolthed

Du kender måske allerede Netto som Danmarks største dagligvarekæde – men vidste du også, at vores medarbejdere er rigtig glade for at arbejde her?

Du bliver nemlig del af et helt specielt sammenhold med masser af opbakning, og hvor vi alle løfter i flok. For det vi laver er vigtigt, men dem, vi laver det med, er endnu vigtigere.

Vi håber, du er lige så begejstret for dyrevelfærd, reduktion af madspild og en bæredygtig fremtid, som vi er. Vi har bl.a. vores eget økologiske brand: ØGO. Og det er naturligvis til gode Netto-priser.

title: Starbucks Daily Operations Leader, Galleria - Full Time
description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Overview

The Starbucks Daily Operations Leader directs daily operations of the licensed Starbucks café inside Macy’s, ensuring an efficient, professional, safe, and profitable operation while upholding Starbucks brand standards and Macy’s Foods Division expectations. The Daily Operations Leader works alongside Baristas to deliver quality customer service and expertly crafted beverages, modeling the operational standards that define the Starbucks Experience.

The Daily Operations Leader coaches and develops team members, maintains an encouraging and energetic work environment, and partners with leadership to support sales, profitability, and compliance goals. In this role, the Daily Operations Leader positively influences others, strengthens leadership skills, and creates an uplifting experience for both customers and colleagues.

Full-time colleagues are typically scheduled to work 30 or more hours per week, while part-time colleagues are typically scheduled 12-24 hours per week. All schedules contain weekend shifts as part of the requirements. Hours are dependent on business needs and colleague availability. Information regarding hours per week needed for benefit eligibility purposes can be found here.

What You Will Do

  • Lead daily café operations, ensuring compliance with Starbucks, Macy’s Foods Division, and Health Department standards for safety, sanitation, and product quality.
  • Deliver an exceptional customer experience by modeling Starbucks’ customer connection standards and Macy’s Selling behaviors.
  • Train, coach, and motivate colleagues through ongoing feedback and role modeling to maximize team performance, customer satisfaction, and professional development.
  • Ensure consistent preparation, presentation, and merchandising of all food and beverages to Starbucks standards, making necessary recipe adjustments (e.g., temperature, ingredient quantities, or substitutions) to meet customer requests.
  • Monitor labor productivity to balance customer service needs with cost control.
  • Assist with ordering, receiving, inventory management, and invoice processing to maintain stock levels and achieve targeted food and beverage costs.
  • Monitor sales, expenses, and reports to achieve profit and loss goals, and communicate results and priorities to the team and leadership.
  • Oversee cash handling and point-of-sale operations in compliance with Macy’s and Starbucks policies.
  • Maintain a clean, professional, and welcoming café environment, serving as a role model for grooming, communication, and workplace conduct.
  • Partner with store leadership and Starbucks Division Managers to ensure operational excellence and promptly resolve customer concerns.
  • Foster an environment of acceptance and respect that strengthens relationships, and ensures authentic connections with colleagues, customers, and communities.
  • In addition to the essential duties mentioned above, other duties may be assigned.

Skills You Will Need

Leadership & Coaching – Demonstrates strong leadership, communication, and coaching skills to engage, develop, and motivate a high-performing team.

Customer Focus – Commits to delivering exceptional customer experiences and effectively resolves concerns to maintain satisfaction and loyalty.

Organizational & Problem-Solving Skills – Applies solid organizational and problem-solving abilities to manage multiple priorities and ensure smooth café operations.

Business Acumen – Understands basic business principles to support sales goals, control expenses, and ensure accurate cash handling.

Food Safety & Compliance – Knowledgeable in food safety, sanitation, and regulatory standards, maintaining a clean, safe, and compliant café environment.

Who You Are

  • Candidates with a High School diploma or equivalent are encouraged to apply. Retail, food service, or customer service experience preferred.
  • Must be ServSafe certified or have food handler permit as required by state or local health department.
  • This position requires heavy lifting, constant moving, remaining in a stationary position, and reaching with arms and hands. Involves remaining in a stationary position for at least two consecutive hours, lifting at least 30 lbs. stooping, kneeling, crouching, and climbing ladders. May involve reaching above eye level. Requires close vision, color vision, depth perception, and focus adjustment.
  • Able to work a flexible schedule, including days, evenings, weekends, and holidays, based on department and company needs.

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Merchandise discounts
  • Performance-based incentives
  • Annual merit review
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice
  • Tuition reimbursement

Access the full menu of benefits offerings here.

About Us

This is a great time to join Macy’s! Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

Join us and help write the next chapter in our story - Apply Today!

title: Senior Weld Engineer
description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.

Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

About the Team:

The Materials and NDE (Non-Destructive Evaluation) team plays a central role in enabling Terran R to fly, re-fly, and scale: developing, characterizing, and inspecting materials and processes across all parts of the vehicle. From welding and additive manufacturing to advanced composites, the team works at the intersection of innovation and execution, balancing performance and reliability with cost, quality, and schedule. As we move toward first flight and beyond, the challenges become more exciting, offering opportunities to shape how we design and develop for reuse. With ownership across products, systems, and disciplines, engineers gain broad exposure and drive key decisions across design, manufacturing, and operations.

About the Role:

  • Lead cross-functional collaboration with design, manufacturing, and quality teams to develop, qualify, and optimize advanced fusion welding processes and equipment/tools for the Terran-R launch vehicle
  • Own weld process development and qualification, including authoring and approving weld procedure specifications and qualifications (WPS/PQR) in accordance with AWS D17.1 and related aerospace standards
  • Provide expert technical support to manufacturing operations—troubleshoot complex welding challenges, perform root cause analysis, and drive sustainable corrective actions
  • Establish and maintain process controls, quality documentation, and inspection criteria to ensure compliance with aerospace standards and production goals
  • Mentor and guide junior weld engineers and technicians, supporting technical development and promoting best practices in welding process control and manufacturing efficiency
  • Identify and lead continuous improvement initiatives to advance welding automation, throughput, and reliability across production systems

About You:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Welding Engineering, Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, or related field (Master’s degree preferred)
  • 5+ years of experience in fusion welding process development, qualification, and production support within aerospace, space, or high-reliability manufacturing environments
  • Extensive knowledge of fusion welding processes (GTAW, GMAW, laser, and orbital tube welding) and related equipment setup, programming, and parameter optimization
  • Demonstrated experience with aerospace materials such as stainless steel, nickel, aluminum, and titanium alloys
  • Proven ability to lead cross-functional problem-solving, communicate and drive technical decision-making to implement robust welding solutions in fast-paced production settings

Nice to haves, but not required:

  • Welding Engineering B.S., M.S.
  • Hands-on experience with manual/semi-automatic GTAW, orbital tube welding, and laser welding systems
  • Deep familiarity with AWS D17.1 and related aerospace welding codes, standards, and inspection requirements
  • Experience with automation integration, robotic welding, or weld data analytics for process monitoring

title: Enterprise Business Architect
description:
The Enterprise Business Architect is responsible for translating enterprise strategy into repeatable EA processes, tools and technologies. The immediate focus will be on building actionable IT investment roadmaps, assessing business capabilities and creating EA models/artifacts that enable data-driven investment decisions. The role bridges business strategy and execution by analyzing current-state operations and designing future-state investment strategies that align business goals, processes, organizational structure and technology. The Business Architect collaborates cross-functionally with executive leadership, business unit stakeholders and EA teams to drive enterprise-wide transformation.

  • Partner with senior leadership to translate business strategy into actionable capability maps, value streams and target operating models.
  • Build and maintain enterprise capability models to uncover gaps, redundancies and investment opportunities.
  • Analyze current-state business processes and organizational structures to identify inefficiencies and drive improvements.
  • Provide input into the design of future-state business architectures including process redesign, organizational realignment and capability roadmaps.
  • Lead workshops and interviews with business unit leaders, subject matter experts and technology teams to gather requirements and build consensus on architectural direction.
  • Establish and maintain business architecture standards / frameworks and governance processes for enterprise-wide consistency.
  • Collaborate with Enterprise, Solution, Data and Technical Architects to align business architecture with IT architecture and solution design.
  • Support investment planning by linking business capabilities to strategic initiatives and identifying dependencies, risks and value drivers.
  • Drive adoption of new business models by communicating architectural vision and rationale to stakeholders across all levels.
  • Curate, organize and maintain learning content to support enterprise architecture learning pathways and employee development.
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Systems or related field.
  • 7+ years of experience in business/enterprise architecture, strategy or management consulting.
  • Experience with enterprise architecture tools (i.e. ServiceNow, YouDesign, etc.).
  • Strong knowledge of business architecture frameworks and methodologies (e.g. TOGAF, BIZBOK).
  • Proven experience developing capability models, value stream maps and target operating models.
  • Demonstrated ability to assess capabilities, analyze findings and deliver recommendations that drive informed decision-making.
  • Strong analytical skills to assess current-state processes and identify inefficiencies, gaps and redundancies.
  • Strategic thinking with the ability to translate business strategy into actionable roadmaps and investment priorities.
  • Excellent facilitation skills, with experience leading workshops and interviews to gather requirements and build stakeholder consensus.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, particularly with Enterprise, Solution, Data and Technical Architects.
  • Experience establishing governance processes and architecture standards across an enterprise.
  • Strong communication and change management skills, with the ability to influence and align stakeholders at all organizational levels.

  • Business acumen to link capabilities to strategic initiatives and evaluate risks, dependencies and value drivers.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Background in large-scale digital transformation or IT investment planning initiatives.
  • Familiarity with Agile and portfolio management practices.

title: Program Manager, Unmanned Surface Vehicle
description:
CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, and London. For more information, please visit .

Role Overview:

We are seeking an experienced Program Manager with a strong technical background to lead the planning, execution, and delivery of small Unmanned Surface Vehicle (sUSV). The successful candidate will own program cost, schedule, and technical performance (CSP) baselines from development, test, production, and sustainment, serving as the primary interface with potential customers (DoW, government agencies), internal engineering teams, operations teams, and supply chain partners. This role requires a rare blend of program management discipline and hands-on technical fluency in autonomous maritime domain.

Responsibilities:

  • Own full program P&L, including cost performance, schedule adherence (IMS/IMP), risk/opportunity management, and technical baseline control (EVMS-lite) across the program lifecycle.
  • Coordinate cross-functional Integrated Product Teams (IPTs) spanning systems engineering, airframe, aerodynamics, guidance, propulsion, warhead/payload integration, avionics, software, manufacturing, quality, test, and logistics.
  • Develop and maintain Integrated Master Schedules (IMS); manage critical path and resolve schedule conflicts.
  • Manage program risk and opportunity registers; drive mitigation plans for technical, schedule, cost, and supply chain risks.
  • Support proposal development, including Basis of Estimate (BOE) generation, technical volume input, pricing strategy, and capture activities for new business and follow-on contracts.
  • Serve as primary point of contact for customer program offices (e.g., PEO, PM offices), leading program reviews (PMR, technical interchange meetings, milestone reviews).
  • Provide informed oversight across the full system lifecycle: requirements decomposition, System Requirements Review (SRR), Preliminary/Critical Design Review (PDR/CDR), integration, flight/static test, Test Readiness Review (TRR), and Production Readiness Review (PRR).
  • Partner with Chief Engineer and systems engineering lead to assess technical trade studies, verify requirements traceability, and ensure design maturity gates are met.
  • Oversee airworthiness, flight safety, and range safety processes, and ensure compliance with applicable safety standards.
  • Coordinate developmental and operational test campaigns (DT&E/OT&E), including flight test, captive carry, HIL/SIL integration labs, and environmental/qualification testing.
  • Ensure configuration management (CM) rigor and technical data package integrity across engineering releases.
  • Manage contract performance against FAR/DFARS requirements, CDRLs, and contract line items (CLINs); support contract modifications and Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs).
  • Ensure compliance with ITAR/EAR export control regulations, DoW security requirements (NISPOM), and applicable airspace/range approvals (e.g., FAA COA, military range safety).
  • Manage supply chain and subcontractor performance for long-lead and critical components (seekers, guidance electronics, propulsion, warheads, airframes, avionics).
  • Report program status, financial performance, and risk posture to executive leadership and customer stakeholders.

Minimum Requirements:

  • Minimum 15 years of program/project management experience within the defense industry, with direct experience managing a complex development program
  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related technical field
  • Strong working knowledge of Earned Value Management Systems (EVMS), Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) development, and risk management processes.
  • Experience managing programs under FAR/DFARS contract types (CPFF, CPIF, FFP) and supporting government customer program offices.
  • Excellent leadership, negotiation, and executive-level communication skills; demonstrated ability to manage cross-functional IPTs and lead through influence.
  • Willingness to travel (typically 20–30%) to customer sites, test ranges, and manufacturing/integration facilities.

Preferred Requirements:

  • Master’s degree or MBA preferred.
  • PMP certification preferred
  • Experience supporting Foreign Military Sales (FMS) or international program execution.
  • Experience with digital engineering environments and model-based acquisition approaches.
  • Prior experience as a Chief Engineer, Deputy Program Manager, or Integration Lead prior to moving into Program Manager roles.
  • Ability to obtain/maintain Secret/Top Secret/SCI clearance

Why CHAOS?

  • Health Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision benefits 100% paid for by the company
  • Additional benefits: 401k (+ 50% company match up to 6% of pay), FSA, HSA, life insurance, and more
  • Our Perks: Free daily lunch while you're working onsite, fully-stocked kitchen, unlimited PTO, casual dress code
  • Compensation Components: Competitive base salaries, generous pre-IPO stock option grants, relocation assistance, and (coming soon!) annual bonuses
  • Team Growth: 500+ employees and counting across 5 global offices
Salary Range: $230,000 - $300,000

The stated compensation range reflects only the targeted base compensation range and excludes additional earnings such as bonus, equity, and benefits. Deloitte Technology Fast 500™ ranked AiDASH No. 12 in the San Francisco Bay Area, and No. 59 overall in their selection of the top 500 for 2024.

Join us in Securing Tomorrow Together!

The Role

Our satellite and AI-powered products are changing how utilities see and protect the grid, and we're gearing up for aggressive customer growth over the next two years. That growth runs on AI at scale. We're building a brand-new Data Inference AI Pipeline team to deliver it, and we're looking for a Staff MLOps Engineer to architect its operational backbone from the very first line of infrastructure code.

As the very first engineer on this team, you'll start with a blank canvas and a rare chance to build something that lasts. You'll shape how our models are deployed, how the pipeline scales and recovers under load, and what it costs to run. Just as importantly, you'll help define the culture, engineering standards, and ways of working that every future teammate inherits. This is a hands-on, high-leverage individual contributor role: your decisions will set the foundation the entire team builds on, and you'll be the go-to technical authority on MLOps as the team grows. You'll report to the Director of Engineering for the Data Inference AI Pipeline team.

Our pending acquisition by Schneider Electric will accelerate our mission as we bring our combined offering to our joint customer base, and the infrastructure you build will power outcomes at an even greater scale.

Location: This is a hybrid role based in Palo Alto, CA, requiring 2 days per week in the office.

How you'll make an impact:

Deployment

  • Own the model deployment pipeline end-to-end: packaging, versioning, rollout, and rollback for ML models moving from training to production
  • Build and maintain deployment infrastructure on SageMaker (endpoints, batch transform, multi-model/multi-container hosting), and evaluate where alternatives such as self-hosted serving or other managed options are a better fit
  • Set the CI/CD pattern for model releases, including automated testing, staged rollout, and canary/shadow deployments

Scalability & elasticity

  • Design inference infrastructure that scales seamlessly with real-time and batch demand
  • Right-size compute (CPU/GPU/Inferentia or equivalent) for each model and workload to balance latency and cost
  • Load-test the pipeline and build capacity plans that stay ahead of customer growth milestones

Cost

  • Own the cost-per-inference metric: instrument it, report on it, and drive it down as volume scales
  • Build cost-awareness into architecture decisions, including autoscaling policies, spot/on-demand mix, and model size/quantization trade-offs

Failover & resilience

  • Design for graceful degradation and failover across regions and availability zones for inference serving
  • Define and test disaster-recovery procedures, and run regular failure-injection and chaos exercises
  • Build monitoring, alerting, and on-call runbooks for model-serving infrastructure, covering drift, latency SLOs, error rates, and infra health

Cross-team leadership

  • Partner with Data Science to bring new models to production on a platform built to support them
  • Partner with the Web Application team where inference results power customer-facing features, keeping latency and reliability expectations aligned
  • Serve as the technical authority on MLOps practices as the Data Inference AI Pipeline team grows

What success looks like in your first 6 months:

  • Model deployment is a repeatable, automated process across models
  • Inference infrastructure has proven it scales up and down smoothly under real load
  • Cost-per-inference is measured, visible, and trending down as volume grows
  • A tested failover and disaster-recovery plan is in place for the inference pipeline, with at least one failure-injection exercise completed
  • Data Science can ship new models into production quickly and independently

What we’re looking for:

Minimum Qualifications

  • 7-10+ years in software/ML engineering, including 3+ years focused specifically on MLOps or ML infrastructure
  • Hands-on production experience with AWS SageMaker (or an equivalent managed ML platform) for model deployment and serving
  • A proven track record designing systems for elasticity/autoscaling, cost optimization, and failover/resilience at production scale
  • Strong expertise in containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes) and in CI/CD built for ML workloads, including model versioning and automated testing and rollout
  • Experience instrumenting and owning cost and performance metrics for the infrastructure you're responsible for
  • The ability to set technical direction as a Staff-level IC, building buy-in across Data Science and other engineering teams
  • High ownership mindset, low ego, and a collaborative spirit, with a passion for building platforms that help others ship faster

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with large imagery, video, or 3D sensor and point-cloud data pipelines or other high-volume unstructured data at scale
  • Experience with multimodal data (imagery, sensor/time-series, geospatial) beyond purely textual or tabular data
  • Experience building MLOps practices from scratch on a new team
  • Familiarity with model monitoring and drift-detection tooling, and GPU cost-optimization techniques (quantization, batching, Inferentia/Trainium or equivalent)
  • A background in a regulated or enterprise B2B domain such as utilities, energy, infrastructure, healthcare, or finance
  • Relevant AWS/Kubernetes certifications or open-source MLOps tooling contributions

What you'll love:

  • Comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage: 100% coverage for employees and 80% for their spouses and children
  • Health Reimbursement Account (HRA): 100% funded by AiDASH to cover medical deductibles
  • 401(k) Plan: Begin contributing after two months of employment to prepare for your future. Currently, no company match is offered
  • Parental Leave: Supportive parental leave with 16 weeks for primary caregivers and 4 weeks for secondary caregivers
  • Generous Vacation Policy: Accrue 20 vacation days per year, plus enjoy an additional flex holiday to celebrate whatever feels most important to you
  • Winter Break: From December 25th through January 1st, we give everyone time off to recharge and enjoy time with family and friends!

We are proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to embracing diversity and inclusion in our hiring practices, and we promote a work environment where everyone, from any race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin, can do their best work.

We offer a competitive annual pay range of $230,000 to $270,000 for this full-time position, which includes a base salary and bonus based on performance. This range reflects the anticipated annual pay range (base + bonus) for new hires. We strive to ensure our compensation packages are equitable and aligned with industry standards. Your recruiter can share more about compensation during the hiring process.

We are committed to providing an inclusive and accessible interview experience for all candidates. Please let us know if you require any accommodation during the interview process, and we will make every effort to meet your needs.

title: Investigative Impact Producer
description:
Investigative Impact Producer


An audience producer at NEWSWELL will help a new statewide investigative team maximize the reach and impact of our most significant journalism. This producer will help identify opportunities for impact, guide the processes to get there and build internal tracking and public-facing documentation about the effects of our work. This role will also help us promote and publicize the work itself.


In short, this job takes the journalism to the people.

This producer should come with a journalism background that may include reporting, editing or multimedia work, and should bring a deep familiarity with the ideas of impact and cross-platform outreach. More importantly, this staffer will bring fresh ideas about how our unique regional or statewide reporting can be of service to our local audiences.

This producer will collaborate with the team’s senior statewide reporter, other team members and NEWSWELL’s local newsrooms, and should bring the sensibility of an innovator, teacher and collaborator to the role.


The role may involve a variety of content creation and audience interaction work, such as:

  • Adding ideas for impact or suggesting additional reporting that could fuel impact
  • Writing stories directly related at solutions or outcomes from our reporting
  • Creating or managing graphics, databases, printed materials or other items that help connect audiences with our work
  • Seeking out stakeholders or potential new audiences and conducting outreach to connect them with our work
  • Brainstorming, organizing and executing community events, speaker forums, demonstrations or other public events


The role is part of a new standalone investigative team that serves the Western newsrooms in NEWSWELL’s nonprofit collective.


Every piece of our team’s work will focus on two equal priorities: impact and audience connection. This role lives at the intersection of both:


IMPACT: All our efforts should pursue righting a wrong and demonstrating the power of journalism to improve public life.


AUDIENCE CONNECTION: Everything we publish should also be in pursuit of strengthening audience ties to our newsroom, through two-way dialogue, public events, uses of new platforms or other methods to demonstrate public outreach.


NEWSWELL helps newsrooms become nonprofit and for-community, providing strategic guidance, innovative solutions and operational support so journalists can focus on what matters most: serving their communities. Through partnerships with Arizona State University — named the nation’s most innovative university for 11 years in a row — NEWSWELL brings cutting-edge ideas, research and tools to reinvent local news and strengthen democracy.


Our innovative model has earned us support from journalistic and philanthropic organizations nationwide. This new team’s work is designed to leverage and grow that support, so that we can grow and transform local journalism.

Submission Requirements

A cover letter explaining the key contributions you would bring to the role, and explaining how your clips shed light on the path to that role.


A resume explaining your professional skills and background.


A sampling of your audience connection experience, which might include things such as: a collection of social media posts with a document explaining strategy; a highlights reel or set of video samples; stories, blog posts, newsletters or other published material you wrote that supported audience engagement or promoted journalism impact.



This role pays $70,000-$80,000 annually.



What you’ll do

  • Support and amplify the process of conceiving, developing and producing investigative and accountability reporting.
  • Build systems to help deliver exclusive findings and measure or track civic impact.
  • Mentor and coach local newsrooms and collaborate on local reporting.
  • Integrate solutions journalism, audience interaction and other innovative techniques into the investigative workflow.
  • Collaborate with reporters and editors to present stories to a broad range of audiences.
  • Use multiple digital publishing formats when appropriate.
  • Support and help lead community forums and partner events; engage transparently with readers and stakeholders.
  • Pilot new tools, including responsible AI, to enhance research, document analysis and workflow efficiency.
  • Partner with ASU’s Walter Cronkite School and other academic institutions to create strong student engagement opportunities, including reporting, learning experiences and newsroom collaboration.
  • Contribute to an inclusive, collaborative newsroom culture that values transparency, fairness, equity and community impact.

What you'll need

  • Storytelling excellence: ability to distill complex information; strong organization and project management across multi‑month investigations and faster accountability hits.
  • Digital fluency: SEO‑aware writing, smart packaging, social and audience collaboration to maximize reach and comprehension.
  • Risk awareness: awareness of legal, safety and trauma‑informed practices, or intense focus on learning.
  • Teamwork: strong sense of collaboration with fellow reporters and other staffers.
  • Proficiency in Associated Press style; commitment to fairness, accuracy, inclusion and community‑centered journalism.


Relevant qualifications

  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in journalism or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Five years of journalism experience
  • Familiarity with accountability or investigative work, or an intense focus on learning.
  • Demonstrable experience in identifying journalism impact, connecting journalistic work with new audiences or engaging with audiences in new ways.
  • Deep familiarity with how to reach people across platforms – web, social, direct outreach, nontraditional forms.

Preferred education and experience

  • Experience in visual production, shooting or producing your own images, video, social media content or work on other platforms beyond written stories.
  • Experience reporting, editing or producing in California and the West.
  • Experience with cross‑newsroom or regional accountability collaborations.


Preferred skills and abilities

  • On-camera experience or video production
  • Events planning and management

Benefits

  • Comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) plan with matching employer contribution
  • 22 days of vacation time
  • 11 holidays, including your birthday
  • Parental leave
  • Significant tuition reductions
  • Professional development is highly valued at ASU Enterprise Partners, where employees are encouraged to look across the organization and nurture new areas of interest
  • $30 bi-weekly cell phone reimbursement

title: Call for CVs:SOP Review and Development Consultant for the IOM Ireland MHPSS Project
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Project Context and Scope

Established in 1951, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) is the leading intergovernmental organisation in the field of migration and is committed to the principle that humane and orderly migration benefits migrants and society. IOM is part of the United Nations system as a related organisation and supports migrants and governments to manage migration in a rights-based manner, with a focus on protecting and saving lives, driving solutions to displacement and facilitating pathways for regular migration.

IOM Ireland implements the Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) Project for International Protection Applicants residing in Ireland. The project provides counselling, case management, cultural mediation, psychosocial support, information and referral assistance, community-based activities, capacity building and follow-up through the MHPSS Infoline.

The project has developed a range of SOPs, guidelines, workflows, forms and operational tools. To strengthen consistency, accountability, safeguarding and service quality, IOM Ireland requires an external consultant to systematically review existing documentation, identify gaps and duplication, harmonise terminology and processes, and develop a practical SOP package for MHPSS project operations.

The objective of the consultancy is to develop a coherent, standardised and implementation-ready package of SOPs that reflects current MHPSS project operations and supports safe, ethical, consistent and accountable service delivery across International Protection Applicant centres.

The consultant will coordinate closely with designated MHPSS focal points while remaining accountable to the Hiring Manager for the timely submission, revision and finalisation of all deliverables. The SOP package will be aligned with relevant IOM standards, policies and principles, including safeguarding, PSEA, protection, accountability to affected populations, data protection and confidentiality requirements.

Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing
IOM Ireland, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Unit.
Tasks to be performed under this contract
Under the direct supervision of the Head of the MHPSS Unit at IOM Ireland, the consultant will:
  1. Review and revise the current draft and existing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), guidelines, workflows, templates and tools for the IOM Ireland MHPSS Project, ensuring they define the minimum procedures required for safe, ethical, consistent and accountable service delivery.
  2. Establish and facilitate consultations with the SOP Working Group, coordinated by the Head of the MHPSS Unit, and collect inputs from designated MHPSS focal points and relevant multidisciplinary team members to ensure that SOPs reflect operational realities, roles, responsibilities and service delivery requirements.
  3. Map, review and strengthen referral pathways and coordination mechanisms within Citywest and with external service providers, ensuring that referral procedures are practical, context-specific, client-centred and aligned with national systems and available services in Ireland.
  4. Ensure that SOPs clearly define the minimum actions and responsibilities required of MHPSS staff and focal points, including identification of needs and vulnerabilities, triage, immediate response, safeguarding measures, informed consent, confidentiality, data protection, referrals, follow-up, case documentation, escalation procedures and case closure.
  5. Coordinate with relevant internal IOM colleagues and external stakeholders, where appropriate, to ensure alignment with IOM policies, protection standards, existing referral mechanisms, interagency coordination processes and operational arrangements in Ireland.
  6. Validate draft SOPs through consultation with the SOP Working Group and key operational focal points, testing the feasibility, practicality and applicability of procedures within the Citywest context and incorporating feedback as required.
  7. Compile and present the revised SOP package, including SOPs, referral pathways, workflows, tools and templates, to IOM Ireland management and technical focal points for review, validation and final endorsement.
  8. Facilitate the finalisation of the SOP package, incorporating consolidated feedback and submitting editable final versions together with implementation recommendations and a practical roll-out plan.
  9. Develop and deliver capacity-building sessions and practical training workshops for MHPSS staff, focal points and relevant partner organizations on the finalised SOPs, referral pathways, roles and responsibilities, and key procedures to support consistent implementation.
  10. Provide post-training guidance and recommendations to support the operationalization, monitoring and continuous improvement of the SOPs and referral pathways.
Performance indicators for the evaluation of results
All deliverables are submitted by the agreed dates and accepted in writing by the Hiring Manager, or by a delegated IOM focal point where applicable. The document inventory and gap analysis comprehensively cover the materials made available by IOM. SOPs clearly define purpose, scope, responsibilities, procedures, documentation, escalation and quality-control requirements.
The final package uses consistent terminology, numbering, formatting, cross-references and document-control elements. Procedures are practical, accessible and aligned with current MHPSS operations. Relevant requirements on safeguarding, PSEA, confidentiality, informed consent, data protection, accountability to affected populations and protection principles are appropriately integrated. Stakeholder consultations and validation sessions are completed and documented, and all final documents are supplied in editable Microsoft Word format.


Deliverable 1. Inception, inventory and gap analysis

Due date: Fri 13 Nov 2026

Required outputs: Inception report; methodology and work plan; consultation schedule; inventory of existing SOPs; gap and duplication analysis; prioritised SOP list; proposed template and document-control framework.

Acceptance standard: Complete, evidence-based and approved in writing by IOM as sufficient to proceed to drafting.

Payment: First instalment: 20%

Deliverable 2. Draft harmonised SOP package

Due date: Fri 4 Dec 2026

Required outputs: First complete draft of agreed SOPs; process maps; associated forms, checklists and annexes; draft SOP register; consultation and validation summary; presentation to IOM..

Acceptance standard: Operationally accurate, internally consistent and sufficiently complete for structured validation by IOM.

Payment: Second instalment: 30%

Deliverable 3. Final SOP package and handover

Due date: Fri 18 Dec 2026

Required outputs: Final editable SOP suite; final workflows, forms and annexes; SOP register; feedback-response matrix; implementation and review plan; final report; staff handover session..

Acceptance standard: All consolidated comments addressed and final outputs accepted in writing by IOM.

Payment:Third Instalment: 30%

Deliverable 4.Capacity building, post-training guidance and final report (Tasks 9–10)

Due date: Training: 11–15 Jan 2027; report: Fri 22 Jan 2027

Required outputs: Training plan and materials; delivery of training workshops for MHPSS staff, focal points and relevant partners; attendance records and pre/post assessment; post-training guidance and recommendations for operationalisation, monitoring and continuous improvement; final consultancy report.

Acceptance standard: Training delivered as planned; materials and final report accepted in writing by IOM.

Payment:Final Instalment: 20%

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Advanced university degree in social work, psychology, public health, mental health, humanitarian affairs, international development, organisational development, quality management, public administration, law, policy development or a related field, with at least five years of relevant professional experience; or
  • A university degree in one of the above fields with at least seven years of relevant professional experience. Relevant certification in quality assurance, process mapping, safeguarding, project management, policy development or technical writing is an advantage.

Experience

  • Demonstrated experience developing, reviewing or implementing SOPs, operational manuals, policies, protocols or quality-assurance frameworks.
  • Experience translating complex operational processes into clear, practical and user-friendly procedures.
  • Relevant experience in MHPSS, protection, safeguarding, migration, social work, case management, public health or humanitarian programming.
  • Experience conducting document reviews, gap analyses, stakeholder consultations and process-mapping exercises.
  • Knowledge of confidentiality, informed consent, referral management, records management, incident reporting and risk-management principles.
  • Experience working with multidisciplinary and culturally diverse teams.
  • Experience with a UN agency, international organisation, NGO or government body is desirable.
  • Experience supporting services for refugees, migrants, asylum seekers or other populations in vulnerable situations is desirable.

Skills

  • Excellent analytical, drafting, editing and technical-writing skills in English.
  • Strong knowledge of SOP development methods, process mapping and document-control systems.
  • Ability to structure complex information into clear steps, roles, decision points and escalation pathways.
  • Strong consultation, facilitation, presentation and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail, consistency and quality assurance.
  • Ability to manage multiple documents and priorities within fixed contractual deadlines.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Word, including styles, tables of contents, tracked changes, cross-referencing and version control.
  • Ability to work independently while maintaining effective coordination with IOM.

Languages

For this consultancy, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Notes

IOM covers Consultants against occupational accidents and illnesses under the Compensation Plan (CP), free of charge, for the duration of the consultancy. IOM does not provide evacuation or medical insurance for reasons related to non-occupational accidents and illnesses. Consultants are responsible for their own medical insurance for non-occupational accident or illness and will be required to provide written proof of such coverage before commencing work.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

This post is subject to local recruitment. Only persons holding a valid residence and work permit in Ireland will be eligible for consideration.

As the right to live and work in Ireland is required, the contract issued may be shorter than the period mentioned in the advertisement, in order to align with expiry date of the work permit.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

title: Senior DevOps/Platform Engineer
description:
Part-Time Contract | Remote | Approximately 20 Hours per Week

About the Role

A mission-critical SaaS platform used by approximately 800 flooring businesses to manage leads, estimates, product selection, inventory, scheduling, installations, invoicing, and paymentsis being modernized from a legacy .NET/ASP, SQL Server, stored-procedure-heavy environment to React, Node.js, TypeScript, native PostgreSQL, REST APIs, and AWS. Much of the initial conversion has been completed using AI-assisted development. The immediate priority is to clean up, test, validate, and safely release the converted system while existing customers remain active.

We are looking for a hands-on Senior DevOps/Platform Engineer who can strengthen the delivery platform, observability, security, and production safeguards required for frequent, low-risk releases.

Responsibilities

  • Assess the current AWS infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, environments, deployment process, and production risks.
  • Improve automated build, test, security-scanning, deployment, and rollback workflows.
  • Support small, frequent releases through feature flags, staged rollouts, health checks, and automated validation.
  • Establish safe coexistence between legacy and modern services during the migration.
  • Build and maintain infrastructure as code for repeatable, auditable environment provisioning.
  • Strengthen monitoring, centralized logging, distributed tracing, alerting, dashboards, and incident-response procedures.
  • Define service-level indicators for availability, latency, error rates, database health, queues, and critical business workflows.
  • Help diagnose performance and stability issues involving AWS, Node.js services, APIs, PostgreSQL, Babelfish, and legacy .NET components.
  • Support the transition from Babelfish and SQL Server-oriented behavior to native PostgreSQL.
  • Review capacity, connection-pool, timeout, retry, queue, and load-shedding configurations.
  • Improve resilience for asynchronous and event-driven workloads using services such as Lambda, SQS, EventBridge, API Gateway, Redis, and dead-letter queues.
  • Implement secure secrets management, access controls, audit logging, vulnerability management, backup, and recovery procedures.
  • Verify that rollback remains safe after application or database writes, including backward-compatible schema changes.
  • Review AI-generated infrastructure and deployment changes for correctness, security, maintainability, and operational risk.
  • Document deployment standards, incident procedures, environment configuration, and operational ownership.
  • Partner closely with engineering and product teams, with meaningful overlap during US working hours.

Required Qualifications

  • At least 7 years of professional DevOps, SRE, platform engineering, or cloud infrastructure experience .
  • Strong hands-on experience operating production workloads in AWS.
  • Proven ownership of CI/CD architecture, automated deployments, monitoring, incident response, and rollback.
  • Experience supporting production systems built with Node.js, React, PostgreSQL, and .NET.
  • Strong understanding of:
    • Infrastructure as code
    • Networking, DNS, load balancing, and API gateways
    • Containers and serverless workloads
    • Logs, metrics, traces, alerts, and production dashboards
    • Secrets management and least-privilege access
    • Backups, disaster recovery, and production readiness
    • Database migrations and backward-compatible schema changes
    • Connection pooling, capacity planning, retries, idempotency, and failure recovery
  • Experience introducing staged deployments, feature flags, canary releases, or blue-green deployments.
  • Ability to troubleshoot across application, infrastructure, network, and database layers.
  • Experience working on incremental modernization where legacy and modern systems must run in parallel.
  • Strong written and spoken English with the ability to communicate risk and recommendations clearly.
  • Ability to work independently and deliver senior-level ownership within a part-time schedule.

Preferred Qualifications
