title: Web Application Specialist
company: McGill Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences
description:
Position summary:

At Canadian Centre for Computational Genomics (C3G) at McGill University, we build open-source Research Data Management (RDM) solutions that support every stage of the genomics and health data lifecycle. Our portals, APIs, databases and tools are the infrastructure behind national genomics and health data sharing in Canada. If you want your work to matter beyond the sprint, this is that role.

Projects:

  • The Pan-Canadian Genome Library (PCGL)
  • The Terry Fox Marathon of Hope Cancer Centre Network (MoHCCN)
  • The International Human Epigenome Consortium (IHEC)
  • The Quebec COVID-19 Biobank (BQC19)

We also provide bioinformatics analysis software and high-performance computing services to the life sciences research community, including widely used analysis pipelines. A Web Application Specialist will engage in the development of online data sharing solutions, notably the Bento Platform (https://github.com/bento-platform), which supports the Pan-Canadian Genome Library (https://genomelibrary.ca/), and many other projects in the fields of genomics, epigenomics, and life science. Under the supervision of the Data Team Lead, the Web Application Specialist will implement and maintain client-side and server-side applications, extending the tools and technologies already in place using JavaScript (React/TypeScript), Python, PostgreSQL, Docker and more. Short development cycles will involve small but frequent releases, and constant interactions with the bioinformatics platform team members.

Primary responsibilities:

  • Design, build, test, deploy, monitor and maintain high-quality interactive web applications using TypeScript with React
  • Develop server-side applications (APIs) and scripts, such as back-end data services and quality control pipelines, using Python
  • Focus on user experience, intuitive interfaces and interaction layers to create user-friendly web pages and applications
  • Ensure implementation is done using the best coding practices, including documentation, unit testing, etc.
  • Contribute in technological research and the prototyping of new clinical/genomics data services
  • Setup and maintain automation tools for testing, continuous integration & delivery
  • Optimise code when needed while making use of good software practices
  • Use an issue tracking system to document tasks, issues and bugs, and their resolution status throughout sprints
  • Ensure that all finished solutions work within a variety of browser types and screen settings along with the constraints set by development and design
  • Contribute to the code review process

Other Qualifying Skills and/or Abilities:

Hard skills: Experience with a JavaScript framework (e.g., React, Vue) in developing full-scale web applications is mandatory. Providing links to examples of web applications the applicant has worked on, either live or on GitHub, is highly recommended. Experience with server-side programming/scripting, such as with Python or Node.js. Experience with relational databases (RDBMS), such as PostgreSQL or MySQL. Experience with applications containerization technologies (e.g. Docker, Podman, Kubernetes). Undergraduate degree in computer science, software engineering or related field.

Soft skills: Demonstrated sound intuition in making efficient and simple-to-use browser-based interactive tools and interfaces. Interest in developing fully open-source solutions. Having an open mind towards new technologies, with at least basic knowledge of the various layers involved in web application development (full-stack). Attention to detail, good communication and organisational skills and ability to work in a highly interactive group. Capable of getting multiple tasks assigned at once, and making them all progress steadily.

Strong Assets:

  • Experience with Python frameworks like Flask, Django, or FastAPI.
  • Experience with the Kubernetes container orchestration system.
  • Experience with Extract-Transform-Load (ETL) or Extract-Load-Transform (ELT) pipelines.
  • Experience with CI/CD workflow orchestration systems (e.g. GitHub Actions, GitLab Workflows)

title: Seniorproduktionsleder til tømrerafdelingen i Søborg
description:

Vi søger en erfaren seniorproduktionsleder til styring af egenproduktion i vores tømrerafdeling. Du bliver tilknyttet vores kontor i Søborg og refererer direkte til produktionschefen.

Hos MT Højgaard Danmark sætter vi projektet først. Det betyder, at vi arbejder ud fra en stærk projektkultur, hvor høj faglighed, ansvarlighed og samarbejde er afgørende for vores succes. Tømrerafdelingen er kendetegnet ved et stærkt fællesskab, dygtige kolleger og mange års erfaring med at gennemføre projekter til aftalt tid, kvalitet og økonomi. Du bliver en del af et fagligt dygtigt team, hvor der er gode muligheder for både faglig- og personlig udvikling.

En udfordrende og alsidig hverdag

Som seniorproduktionsleder får du ansvaret for den daglige ledelse af fagprojektet:

  • Produktionsledelse og mandskabsstyring
  • Projektøkonomi og opfølgning
  • Tids- og ressourceplanlægning
  • Ledelse af formænd og timelønnede medarbejdere
  • Akkordaftaler med timelønnede
  • Koordinering med bygherre, rådgivere, arkitekter og øvrige samarbejdspartnere
  • Sikring af fremdrift, kvalitet og arbejdsmiljø

Du bliver en central del af projektteamet og vil arbejde med projekter i forskellige entrepriseformer. Har du solid erfaring med egenproduktion, planlægning og projektstyring, vil der også være mulighed for at få ansvar på hovedentrepriser. Tømrerafdelingen gennemfører projekter i størrelsesordenen 5-200 mio. kr.

Om dig

Vi forestiller os, at du har en håndværksmæssig baggrund som tømrer, snedker eller lignende, kombineret med en uddannelse som bygningskonstruktør, ingeniør eller tilsvarende. Det vigtigste er dog, at du har opbygget stærke kompetencer gennem praktisk erfaring og besidder et godt købmandskab.

Derudover forventer vi, at du:

  • har minimum 4 års erfaring med entrepriseledelse inden for fag-, stor- og hovedentrepriser
  • har dokumenteret erfaring med egenproduktion og ledelse af større projekter
  • er en stærk og synlig leder, der formår at motivere og udvikle medarbejdere
  • har solid økonomisk forståelse og et naturligt fokus på projektets samlede resultat
  • kan skabe tillidsfulde relationer til kunder, samarbejdspartnere og medarbejdere

For at få succes i stillingen skal du kunne balancere rollen som købmand, forhandler og leder. Du arbejder professionelt, træffer klare beslutninger og formår samtidig at bevare stærke og langvarige relationer til både kunder og samarbejdspartnere.

Kan du se dig selv i vores værdier?

Hos MT Højgaard Danmark arbejder vi hver dag for at levere projekter til aftalt tid, i den rette kvalitet og inden for den økonomiske ramme. Det kræver stærkt samarbejde, høj faglighed og fokus på det fælles mål. Hvis du deler disse værdier, vil du passe godt ind hos os.

Vi tilbyder

Du bliver en del af en af Danmarks førende entreprenørvirksomheder med mange spændende projekter. Vi tilbyder bl.a.:

  • et stærkt fagligt miljø med kompetente kolleger
  • masser af ansvar på komplekse projekter
  • efteruddannelse og kompetenceudvikling, både faglig og personlig
  • en individuel udviklingsplan, der understøtter dine ambitioner

Ansøgning

Vil du vide mere om stillingen, er du velkommen til at kontakte produktionsdirektør Tomas Rosentoft på tlf. +45 2270 9337.

Vi ser frem til at modtage dit CV og indkalder løbende til samtaler med henblik på snarlig tiltrædelse.

Om MT Højgaard Danmark

Hos MT Højgaard Danmark arbejder vi med balance mellem høj faglighed og høj trivsel. Mellem handlekraft og omtanke. Mellem frihed til at udvikle sig og ansvar for at få tingene til at ske. Balance mellem det at have travlt, men samtidig have det sjovt og godt. Det, at være et individ, men samtidig kunne samarbejde i et team. Mød os på mth.dk

title: Asset Protection Detective, Salinas Northridge - Full Time
description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Overview

As an Asset Protection Detective, you will help protect company assets, reduce shortage, and support a safe, customer-focused shopping environment. Using surveillance, investigative tools, and strong partnerships with store teams and law enforcement, you will identify and respond to theft, recover merchandise, and help protect our customers, colleagues, and business.

Why This Role Matters

Asset Protection Detectives play an important role in reducing loss while maintaining a safe and welcoming store environment. Through training, observation, investigation, and de-escalation, this role helps protect company assets, support colleagues, and ensure customers can shop with confidence.

How Our Asset Protection Colleagues Spend Their Day…

  • Our colleagues begin each day energized and ready to make an impact. They greet teammates with a warm hello. Before they get started, they review updates and department information so they're fully informed and ready to engage with confidence.

  • We believe service starts with each other - supporting one another with honesty, care, and collaboration so we can better serve our customers and communities.

  • And we know that excellence is a journey - we strive to improve every day, take pride in our work, achieve sales goals and learn from each other to deliver individual and store results.

Full-time colleagues are typically scheduled to work 30 or more hours per week, while part-time colleagues are typically scheduled 12-24 hours per week. All schedules contain weekend shifts as part of the requirements. Hours are dependent on business needs and colleague availability. Information regarding hours per week needed for benefit eligibility purposes can be found here.

What To Expect

  • Use surveillance techniques, investigative tools, and reporting systems to help identify theft, dishonest activity, and shortage trends.

  • Partner with Asset Protection leaders, store teams, and law enforcement to support investigations and protect company assets.

  • Apply de-escalation tools and sound judgment to help maintain a safe environment for customers and colleagues.

  • Prepare clear documentation, statements, and evidence to support investigations, audits, and legal proceedings.

  • Support team readiness by training colleagues on protocols that help protect company assets.

How You’ll Make an Impact

  • Help protect customers, colleagues, and company assets by identifying, investigating, and responding to theft and dishonest activity.

  • Use surveillance techniques to support the apprehension of shoplifters and dishonest employees, while following company policies and legal requirements.

  • Recover stolen merchandise and provide statements, evidence, and documentation to support investigations.

  • Prepare timely and accurate reports related to theft incidents, investigations, audits, and assigned activities.

  • Build strong partnerships with store colleagues, Asset Protection leaders, and law enforcement to support investigations and shortage reduction.

  • Maintain compliance with company policies and legal standards related to apprehensions, searches, and evidence preservation.

  • Testify in court for criminal and civil cases, as needed.

  • Respond to alarm calls, support special assignments, and facilitate first aid for customers and colleagues when needed.

  • Foster an environment of acceptance and respect that strengthens relationships with colleagues, customers, and communities.

Skills That Matter

Must Have

  • Ability to observe, identify, and respond to suspicious activity in a retail environment.

  • Strong communication skills with the ability to partner effectively with customers, colleagues, leaders, and law enforcement.

  • Ability to use sound judgment, de-escalation tools, and company procedures to support a safe environment.

  • Ability to handle proprietary, sensitive, and confidential information with discretion and integrity.

  • For jobs in New York, a current New York State Security Guard License is required.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in retail, customer service, asset protection, security, investigations, or law enforcement.

  • Ability to prepare accurate reports, statements, and documentation related to incidents and investigations.

  • Experience using surveillance systems, reporting tools, or investigative technology.

  • Ability to train or coach colleagues on asset protection protocols, shortage reduction, or safety practices.

Physical Activities You Will Perform

  • This role involves performing essential job functions such as communication, collaboration, and use of office and computer systems. Responsibilities include the ability to access and review written and electronic information, and to move within the work environment and interact with workplace materials as needed to carry out job responsibilities.

  • Position requires prolonged periods of standing/walking around store or department.

  • May occasionally involve reaching above eye level, stooping, kneeling, or crouching.

  • Must be able to apprehend shoplifters.

  • Ability to sustain long periods of time enclosed in surveillance areas.

  • Frequently lift/move up to 30lbs.

  • Requires close vision, color vision, and ability to adjust focus.

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Merchandise discounts
  • Performance-based incentives
  • Annual merit review
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice

Access the full menu of benefits offerings here.

About Us

This is a great time to join Macy’s! Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

Join us and help write the next chapter in our story - Apply Today!

title: Donated Goods Supervisor Full Time
description:
JOB SUMMARY

Under the supervision of the Donated Goods Manager, Donated Goods Manager in Training, or Donated Goods Assistant Manager, the Donated Goods Supervisor is responsible for maintaining activities to ensure maximum revenues and effectiveness. The Donated Goods Supervisor may be responsible for their location in the absence of the Donated Goods Manager or Donated Goods Assistant Manager.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES

Responsible for coaching, training, safety, monitoring daily use of POS and WMS systems, equipment, and supervision of all location personnel in accordance with Agency policies, procedures, and work instructions.

Responsible for ensuring a safe working environment. Instilling proper attitudes towards safety and ensuring work is performed in a safe manner. Constantly watches for and corrects unsafe conditions.

Assist in achieving daily sales and processing goals.

Assist in maintaining merchandising standards and merchandise rotation (i.e., pull schedule).

Sets example for all staff. Leads by example. Enforces the work schedule, break schedule and Agency policies in the absence of Management.

Demonstrate and promote superior customer service both internally and externally. Leads by example and expects the highest level of customer service from all employees. Handles employee/customer/donor complaints in a fair and impartial manner.

In the absence of Management, responsible for timely submission/updating of all required reports including daily/monthly sales recap, transportation needs, labor planner, safety, and personnel-related forms.

Ensure the effective and secure handling of all products, from the point of receipt through the process of warehousing and distribution to stores. Assist with cycle counts and inventory to ensure the DC remains within guidelines of error/shrink.

May assist the Warehouse Manager in overseeing, monitoring, and meeting salvage and recycling monthly revenue goals, including but not limited to, textiles, metal, cardboard, and electronic waste. Ensuring all recordkeeping is timely and accurate. Report emerging trends, issues and needs in an accurate and timely manner.

May perform opening/mid/closing functions as assigned. Accurately handle money involved in the store operations, including daily register balancing, banking, and change.

Work to reduce the possibility of pilferage and burglary.

Ability to train all entry level positions up to Supervisor positions.

Ability to perform and support as needed in all areas of operation.

Support the Agency’s Work Services program and volunteer programs in accordance with Goodwill’s Mission.

Travel needed for coverage of alternative locations, training, and reasonable suspicion process.

Regular attendance is required to perform essential functions of the job.

SECONDARY DUTIES

Performs other duties as assigned by Management.

Support in other store locations as assigned by Director of Donated Goods.

title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer, Platform
description:
About the Role

Join the Platform team at an early-stage AI and manufacturing supply chain company. You will build the backend services, data pipelines, and integrations that support AI-powered agents and reliable movement of goods through complex manufacturing workflows.

What You'll Do

  • Design and scale backend services using Next.js API routes, background jobs, and serverless functions for high-throughput order processing.

  • Build and productionize LLM-based agents, AI/ML infrastructure, and RAG patterns for quote analysis and supplier recommendations.

  • Design PostgreSQL schemas, migrations, and complex queries for materials, quotes, orders, and supplier relationships.

  • Build event-driven pipelines for order state management, notifications, and synchronization across systems.

  • Implement caching, rate limiting, and reliability patterns for external API integrations.

  • Establish monitoring, alerting, and observability practices, and own backend incident response.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong experience with transactional guarantees, ACID semantics, exactly-once processing, and idempotent APIs.

  • Experience scaling PostgreSQL or other relational databases, and building event-driven systems or reliable data pipelines.

  • Experience integrating ERP systems and third-party APIs, including legacy or poorly documented interfaces.

  • Background in manufacturing supply chain, procurement, or logistics, with strong computer science fundamentals.

Compensation & Benefits

Annual salary range: $160,000 to $250,000 USD. Visa sponsorship is available.

Location

Remote. Primary location: San Francisco, California, United States.

title: Investigator 3 (PCN 082095)
description:
Job Description

The Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing is recruiting for an Investigator 3 to join our team.

Investigators serve to ensure competent, professional, and regulated services are delivered to the community by investigating alleged violations of statutes and regulations governing 43 different licensed professions in the State of Alaska. Investigators review complaints concerning violations which may include fraud, malpractice, negligence, misconduct, unethical conduct, unlicensed practice and noncompliance of various licensing provisions.

Your routine duties would include independently conducting investigations of alleged violations of Title 08 statutes and 12 AAC regulations, conducting interviews, invoking disciplinary actions, and when appropriate, preparing and participating in cases for administrative hearing. You also will be working with the Alaska State Medical Board, reviewing cases with medical board members, and attending board meetings.

Our organization, mission and culture:
The mission of the Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing (CBPL) is to ensure that competent, professional and regulated commercial services are available to Alaska consumers. The investigation unit supports this mission by investigating allegations against Alaska's licensed professionals who violate the laws governing their licenses.

The benefits of joining our team:
We offer flexible work schedules where employees in good standing can choose their work hours and/or alternative workweek schedules. We maintain a supportive and collaborative team atmosphere, training opportunities outside of Alaska, and have a comprehensive employee benefits package to include retirement, health insurance, and 13 paid holidays.

You will have the opportunity to utilize and acquire a wide range of investigative skills. Investigators work in collaboration with a multitude of agencies to protect Alaskan consumers and uphold industry and licensing standards. The incumbent will join a team of professionals, committed to public service.

Where you will be working:
Our office is located in downtown Anchorage inside the Atwood Building on the 15th floor; with free employee parking located across the street in the Linny Pacillo parking garage. This position has the possibility of telework.

To be successful in this position a candidate will need the following core competencies:
  • Reasoning: Identifies rules, principles, or relationships that explain facts, data, or other information; analyzes information and makes correct inferences or draws accurate conclusions.
  • Technological Competency: Competency with standard office equipment. Computer literacy and fluency with Microsoft Office software is essential. Administering a large volume of digital documents, information, and evidence in cases. Utilization of the digital case management system and other investigative software.
  • Interpersonal Skills: Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations; is sensitive to cultural diversity, race, gender, disabilities, and other individual differences.
  • Manages and Organizes Information: Identifies a need; gathers, organizes, and maintains both confidential and non-confidential information; determines its importance and accuracy, and clearly communicates it by both written and verbal methods.
  • Independent Worker: displays a high level of initiative, effort, confidentiality, and commitment towards completing assignments in a timely manner; works with minimal supervision; is motivated to achieve; demonstrates responsible behavior.

Minimum Qualifications

Any combination of education and/or experience that provides the applicant with competencies in

  • Accountability: Holds self and others accountable for measurable high-quality, timely, and cost-effective results. Determines objectives, sets priorities, and delegates work. Accepts responsibility for own actions and decisions. Complies with established control systems and rules.

  • Analytical Thinking/Problem Solving: uses a logical, systematic, sequential approach to address problems or opportunities or manage a situation by drawing on one’s knowledge and experience base and calling on other references and resources as necessary.

  • Integrity/Honesty: Contributes to maintaining the integrity of the organization; displays high standards of ethical conduct and understands the impact of violating these standards on an organization, self, and others; is trustworthy.

  • Investigation: Knowledge of the guidelines, regulations, and procedures associated with investigation, including interviewing, evidence detection, locating, gathering, and handling, and drawing appropriate factual inferences and conclusions. Provide oral or written reports of findings. Presenting evidence and providing testimony.

  • Law: Knowledge of State and federal laws, including legal and court procedures, regulations, guidelines, precedents, admissibility of evidence, case preparation, and/or settlements for applicable areas of law practiced or supported.

Equivalent to those typically gained by:
Any combination of preparatory post-secondary education and/or progressively responsible investigative work experience performing duties such as locating and gathering information, evidence and/or testimony to be used in civil or criminal proceedings, administrative actions, or governmentally regulated activities which included preparing reports in support of attorneys or agencies engaged in administrative adjudication, and/or detecting and verify suspected fraud, licensing violations, and other violations of state law.

Definitions:
“Competencies” means a combination of interrelated knowledge, skills, abilities, and behaviors that enable a person to act effectively in a job or situation.

“Typically gained by” means the prevalent, usual method of gaining the competencies expected for entry into the job.

“Training” and “education” in this guidance are synonyms for the process of acquiring knowledge and skills through instruction. It includes instruction through
formal and informal methods (such as classroom, on-line, self-study, and on-the-job), from accredited and unaccredited sources, and long-duration (such as a post-secondary degree) and short-duration (such as a seminar) programs.

“Progressively responsible” means indicating growth and/or advancement in complexity, difficulty, or level of responsibility.

Special Note:
Some positions in this class may require eligibility for commission as a Special Officer with the State of Alaska as a condition of hire.

Some positions require applicants pass a background investigation, which includes a criminal record check for conviction of felony or misdemeanor crimes, as a prerequisite to employment.

Some positions require incumbents possess an Alaska driver's license and operate a motor vehicle.

Additional Required Information

Special Notice: This position requires a valid driver's license.

Cover letter instructions (to be attached to your application):
The cover letter must address (in detail) each of the position-specific competencies to determine if the applicant has the requisite experience. The position requires extensive communication skills, both verbal and written. The incumbent must demonstrate the ability to write in a manner indicating their ability to clearly communicate ideas, intent, and direction.

A successful cover letter will give specific examples demonstrating your experience in an area, in which you assert professional competency. The cover letter should be formatted in the traditional letter style complete with date, inside address, subject line, salutation, body of letter, complimentary close, and signature block. Applicants are advised to pay particular attention to spelling, punctuation and grammar as the cover letter will also be used as a professional writing sample.

Documents needed at the time of interview, unless indicated otherwise:
If you are selected to advance to the interview phase of the recruitment process, you must provide the following at the time of the interview (if not already attached to your application):
  • Three (3) supervisory references; and
  • Last two (2) performance evaluations.
Education:
If post-secondary education is required to meet the minimum qualifications, you must fill in the Education section of the application. If you have not obtained a degree, please indicate the number of units completed. Copies of transcripts are required to verify educational credentials if used to meet the minimum qualifications for a position. Transcripts must be attached at the time the application is submitted.

Work Experience:
If using work experience in order to meet the minimum qualifications of the position and it is not already documented in your application, also provide the employer's name, your job title, dates of employment, and whether full-or part-time. Applications will be reviewed to determine if the responses are supported and minimum qualifications are clearly met. If they are not, the applicant may not advance to the interview and selection phase of the recruitment.

Multiple Vacancies:
This recruitment may be used for more than one (1) vacancy. The applicant pool acquired during this recruitment may be used for future vacancies for up to ninety (90) days after this recruitment closes. Interested applicants are encouraged to apply to each recruitment notice to ensure consideration for all vacancies.

EEO Statement:

title: Interior Solutions Specialist
description:
Job Title
Interior Solutions Specialist

Location
Brantford, ON (On-Site)

Employment Type
New, Full-Time Permanent position

About Stevans Commercial Interiors
Stevans is a Canadian supplier serving long-term care, retirement, healthcare, and commercial environments across Canada for more than 30 years. Our customers include more than 1,000 communities from Vancouver to St. John’s. We provide furniture, window coverings, fabrics, and interior solutions designed to meet the demands of senior living and healthcare environments—from product selection and quoting through procurement and installation support.

Stevans offers a collaborative environment where motivated individuals can build long-term careers (our average employee tenure is 10+ years!). We provide a competitive base salary and bonus structure, a flexible vacation and time off program, and comprehensive benefit coverage.

The Opportunity
In this role, you will build the quotes and proposals that win our projects, covering furniture, window coverings and blinds for long-term care, retirement, healthcare, and commercial clients. You will work with the largest operators across Canada on projects large and small, from a single reorder to complete new builds and full renovations.

This is a mission-critical sales role at the centre of our business. It is a fast-paced, multifaceted position where no two projects will look exactly the same. You will take opportunities from a variety of sources, including online RFPs and tenders, architectural drawings and specifications, bid packages, customer emails, previous order history, and requests handed off from our field sales team. Your job is to turn that information into an accurate, well-thought-out solution for the customer.

The position is based out of our Brantford office and is primarily in-office, with occasional travel as required. This is a full-time salaried position with a competitive bonus structure that rewards performance and contribution.

What We Offer:
  • Competitive salary with bonus opportunities
  • Comprehensive health benefits and flexible vacation policy
  • Commitment to professional growth
  • A mission-driven culture focused on excellence and client satisfaction
Key Responsibilities
  • Prepare accurate quotes and proposals for FF&E projects large and small, including furniture, window coverings, blinds, and soft goods, with the opportunity to expand into new product categories as we grow.
  • Take opportunities from a variety of sources, including online RFPs and tenders, architectural drawings and specifications, bid packages, customer emails, field sales handoffs, and existing customer order history, and turn them into complete solutions.
  • Read and interpret architectural drawings, floor plans, and specifications to complete accurate take-offs, product counts, and room-by-room breakdowns.
  • Become an expert in the Stevans product portfolio and our vendor lines. Understand our products inside and out so you can confidently recommend the right products, fabrics, finishes, specifications, and alternates for each customer's needs, budget, and environment.
  • Develop product recommendations suited to senior care environments, considering durability, infection control, safety, functionality, appearance, and overall value.
  • Own the customer relationship after handoff from our field sales team. Answer questions, solve problems, and help move the project from initial request through to a successful order.
  • Build and maintain detailed pricing, including vendor costs, discounting, freight, installation, and margin. Accuracy and attention to detail are critical to this role.
  • Act as the link between our customers, field sales team, vendors, and internal operations.
  • Source products, confirm specifications, pricing and lead times, chase down answers, and make sure proposals go out complete and on time.
  • Respond to BIDs, RFQs, RFPs, and tender packages for projects of all sizes, while managing the smaller day-to-day customer requests that keep our business moving.
  • Work with customers, designers, architects, and head office contacts to align product selections with project requirements, budgets, and healthcare durability standards.
You are a great fit for the role if:
You are relentless about solving problems - You leave no stone unturned to deliver solutions to customers on time, “The Stevans Way”. When a product is discontinued, a lead time slips, or a budget is tight, you find the path forward.

You are comfortable with ambiguity – You want responsibility early, move with urgency, and measure yourself by what you get done. You are comfortable navigating changing priorities and imperfect information, and you push the agenda to help the company continuously improve.

You are very comfortable with numbers - You are strong in Excel and precise with accuracy. You have exceptionally high attention to detail and build accuracy checks into your work.

You are a team player – “We before me”. You value collaboration, share credit, and listen to other perspectives. We celebrate wins and learn from losses together. Your contributions make the team stronger.

You act like an owner - You take initiative, own outcomes, and operate with accountability. You will help set the standards this team runs on for years.

Qualifications
Required
  • Experience in estimating, quoting, specification, or inside sales, in furniture, FF&E, interiors, building products, construction or related industry.
  • Ability to read and interpret architectural drawings and specification documents.
  • Strong Excel skills and a high comfort level with numbers, pricing, and margin math.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; comfortable communicating directly with customers and vendors.
  • Organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple quotes and deadlines at once.
Asset
  • A diploma or degree in interior design, architectural technology, or a related field.
  • Experience with bids, RFQs, and tender submissions.
  • Familiarity with design, specification, or takeoff software such as AutoCAD, Revit, CET Designer, SketchUp, 2020, and Bluebeam.
  • Experience with material and finish selection.
Interested in being a part of Stevans Commercial Interiors? We look forward to your application!
Stevans Commercial Interiors is committed to meeting the accessibility needs of all applicants throughout the recruiting and selection process. Please let us know about any accommodation and/or support requirements. Please note that only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

Please note we are only accepting applications from those authorized to work in Canada and we are not currently sponsoring any temporary or permanent work visas.

Stevans Commercial Interiors is working in partnership with HR à la carte for our recruitment efforts.

Use of AI in Hiring: Some stages of our recruitment process may use AI-assisted tools to support recruitment efforts; however, all applications are screened and assessed by human reviewers. In addition, all final hiring decisions are made by humans.

title: Studio Production Coordinator
description:
MEISON is a collection of high-end and luxury women’s apparel brands including Jones New York, Misook, Ming Wang, Masai Copenhagen, and Kasper. We focus on elevated, timeless workwear and fashions that are easy to mix-and-match and designed to help build an effortless and reusable wardrobe. Our brands are found online, through specialty boutiques, and in stores with our various retail partners such as Neiman Marcus, Saks 5th Avenue, Nordstrom, Bloomingdale’s and Dillard’s.

Position Summary:

The Studio Production Coordinator will manage day-to-day photo and lifestyle shoot logistics, studio operations, and vendor partnerships to ensure smooth, high-quality creative output. This role acts as a central operational liaison, partnering closely with brand marketing and merchant teams to manage shot lists, handle end-to-end sample inventory, and organize studio space and prop management. The ideal candidate is proactive, highly organized, and thrives in a fast-paced environment supporting photo teams both on set and behind the scenes.

Work Location: Grapevine, Texas

Compensation & Benefits

  • Salary Range: $45,000 to $50,000
  • 100% Employer-covered Medical, Dental & Vision
  • 401(k)
  • PTO
  • 10 Paid Holidays
  • 75% Employee Discount across all brands

Responsibilities

  • Studio Planning & Logistics: Coordinate studio production planning, scheduling shoot timelines, and managing vendor partnerships.
  • Cross-Functional Alignment: Partner closely with the brand marketing and merchant teams to align on shot lists and creative expectations.
  • Sample Management: Oversee end-to-end sample management, including tracking, receiving, organizing, and preparing product inventory for shoots.
  • Prop & Set Management: Source, fulfill, organize, and manage props for studio and lifestyle shoots. Set up, break down, and maintain studio staging, equipment, and production spaces.
  • On-Set & Shoot Support: Assist with staging, preparing, and packing before and after shoots. Support photo teams during shoots with logistics, setup, set changes, and general onsite problem-solving.
  • Workflow & File Management: Organize, track, and manage studio files and operational workflows.
  • Post-Production Support: Perform image retouching and color accuracy adjustments as needed

Qualifications & Experience

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Visual Communication, Photography, Marketing, Operations, or a related field preferred.
  • Experience: 0-1 year of experience in production coordination, creative planning, or commercial studio operations; previous experience in retail production is a plus.
  • Vendor & Workflow Management: Experience working with multiple vendors simultaneously and familiarity with creative workflows, shot list planning, and collaborating with marketing and creative teams.
  • Technical Skills: Basic technical knowledge of photo studio workflows, Capture One, or Adobe Photoshop (retouching skills a major plus).
  • Core Competencies: Strong organizational skills, excellent interpersonal communication, detail-oriented mindset, continuous drive to learn, and strong multitasking and proactive problem-solving abilities.
  • Execution: Ability to work independently and collaboratively across multidisciplinary teams.
  • Physical Requirements: Comfortable lifting up to 50 lbs. and standing for extended periods during studio shoots.

More about Meison

We are a family owned and operated company, and our core values help shape our company culture. These core values are the foundation that we use to build our team, collaborate with each other, and how we approach our work. We are committed to understanding our customers, solving problems by finding and applying solutions, speaking up when we need help all while valuing our time, money and resources.

As we continue to grow and bring new brands into our portfolio, we strive to become one of the preeminent providers of women's high-end luxury apparel in the US. Our goal through all of our efforts is to create a welcoming, inspiring environment that makes it easy for our customers to build a quality wardrobe that works for their style and their lives. They should not have to worry about what to wear or buy next — we do the thinking for them through our passionate understanding of their wants and needs when it comes to getting dressed. Not only do our collections delight the imagination, they also teach our customers how to dress, offering value beyond the aesthetic of a well-designed wardrobe.

title: Electronics Technician
description:
**Join our Chipset team and help bring the next generation of hearing technology to life

**Are you passionate about electronics and practical problem-solving? Do you enjoy working hands-on with hardware, supporting users, and helping turn ideas into working solutions? If so, we encourage you to apply.

At Demant, we develop state-of-the-art chipsets that power our hearing healthcare products used by millions of people worldwide. We are looking for a Junior Chipset Engineer to support our development teams by maintaining and troubleshooting chipset platforms, supporting internal users, and contributing to the development of new chipset test solutions.

**Welcome to Chipset

**Chipset is a key division within our Research & Development organization. We design and develop advanced integrated circuits and chipset platforms that power our world-leading hearing instruments and accessories.

Our commitment to technological excellence drives us to deliver professional-grade solutions in DSP processing, audio quality, connectivity, AI integration, and rechargeability, all in compact form factors with extremely low power consumption.

You will become part of a team of highly skilled engineers working across analog IC design, digital IC design, verification, test development, and system integration. Together, we create the technologies used in products from Oticon, Philips, Bernafon, and other leading hearing healthcare brands.

**The Role

**As a Junior Chipset Engineer, you will play an important role in both supporting our chipset development activities and contributing to the development of the next generation of chipset test platforms.

You will act as a key point of contact for internal users of our chipset development platforms while also participating in hardware development activities under the guidance of experienced engineers.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Provide support for chipset hardware platforms and development boards.
  • Prepare, maintain, and improve chipset boards and lab setups.
  • Assist with schematic design and PCB layout of test boards.
  • Contribute to the development of chipset test systems.
  • Bring up, test, debug, new hardware designs.
  • Perform soldering and rework of prototype hardware.
  • Document solutions, procedures, and designs in compliance with quality requirements.
  • Collaborate with verification teams, as well as external suppliers.

This role offers a unique opportunity to gain broad exposure to chipset development, from practical laboratory work and user support to hardware design and test system development.

**About You

**You may have a background as an Electronics Technician, Laboratory Technician, Electrical Engineering Technician, or a recently graduated Electronics Engineer.

We imagine that you have:

  • a solid understanding of electronics and electronic measurement techniques
  • hands-on experience with laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies, and logic analyzers
  • an interest in hardware development, troubleshooting, and practical problem solving
  • good documentation and communication skills
  • a structured and service-minded approach to your work

Experience with any of the following would be an advantage:

  • schematic capture and PCB layout tools such as Cadence or OrCAD
  • prototype hardware debugging and bring-up
  • soldering and rework of electronic assemblies
  • automated test systems
  • scripting or automation using Python
  • Quality Management Systems (QMS)

**The Ideal Candidate

**We are looking for someone who:

  • enjoys combining practical hands-on work with engineering activities
  • likes helping colleagues solve technical challenges
  • is curious and eager to develop new technical skills
  • can communicate effectively with engineers and stakeholders across multiple disciplines
  • takes ownership of tasks and follows them through to completion
  • thrives in a collaborative team environment

**Why Join Us?

**At Demant, you will become part of a world-class technology organization developing products that improve the lives of millions of people with hearing loss.

We offer:

  • a friendly and highly collaborative engineering environment
  • access to advanced development laboratories and state-of-the-art technology
  • opportunities to learn from experts across ASIC design, firmware, verification, and system development
  • a thorough onboarding process and mentoring from experienced colleagues
  • flexibility, professional development, and excellent employee benefits

Most importantly, you will play a central role in supporting the teams that create the technology behind some of the world's most advanced hearing solutions.

**Do You Want to Join the Team?

**Then please send your CV and application letter as soon as possible and no later than Sunday, October 25, 2026.

For any questions, please contact Peter Siegumfeldt, Senior Manager Chipset, at psie@demant.com.

_At Demant we value diversity, equity and inclusion (DE&I) and we are committed to creating an inclusive working environment. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of ethnic background, personality, age, gender, and education. Diversity is part of our cultural DNA. Women in STEM areas are particularly encouraged to apply, as Demant supports United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 5 on gender equality.

title: Infrastructure Technician II
description:
Infrastructure Technician II

Ready to grow your technical career and take on more advanced responsibilities? As an Infrastructure Technician II, you will be a core part of the team that builds, maintains, and optimizes the structured cabling systems powering world-class data centers.

This role is ideal for experienced technicians who want to sharpen their fiber and copper cabling skills, gain exposure to complex infrastructure builds, and contribute to high impact, high visibility projects. You’ll work in fast paced environments, collaborate with skilled professionals, and help deliver the reliable connectivity that drives today’s digital world.

If you’re looking for hands-on work, technical development, and the chance to grow with an industry leader — this is your opportunity.

Position Details:

  • Hourly position based upon experience & skill level

  • Contract with possible contract extension or hire

  • Standard Work Schedule: up to 6 days a week days and evening shifts available (all shifts are subject to change upon business demands)

  • Location: Customer Site - Abilene, TX

What You’ll Do

Deliver High Quality Structured Cabling Work

  • Install, test, splice, service, and decommission structured cabling systems including fiber optics, copper, communications, and other low voltage systems.

  • Build and remove cabinets, racks, cable trays, pathways, and related data center infrastructure.

  • Perform physical installations and removals with precision, safety, and attention to detail.

Champion Safety & Quality

  • Follow all Company and customer safety standards to ensure an Accident-Free Everyday environment.

  • Uphold quality, production, and industry best practices in every installation.

  • Maintain a clean, organized, and hazard-free work area to support efficient and safe operations.

Interpret and Execute Technical Plans

  • Read and follow project drawings, specifications, and manufacturer guidelines.

  • Apply broad understanding of structured cabling installation, routing, labeling, and commissioning.

  • Ensure installations meet design intent, customer requirements, and industry standards.

Support the Team & Mentor Others

  • Work as a proactive member of the team, supporting less experienced technicians and sharing knowledge.

  • Help plan materials, tools, and tasks to keep projects moving smoothly.

  • Communicate clearly with supervisors, teammates, and customer representatives.

What Helps You Succeed

  • Ability to follow instructions carefully while working with strong independence.

  • Comfortable teaching and learning from peers; contributes positively to team culture.

  • Able to distinguish color for cable identification.

  • Proficient with telecom and construction hand tools, safely and effectively.

  • Thrives in a fast paced, changing environment while maintaining a positive, professional attitude.

  • Highly reliable — shows up on time, prepared, and ready to work.

  • Strong attention to detail and pride in workmanship.

  • Willingness to workdays, nights, weekends, or overtime based on project needs.

  • Excellent work ethics, integrity, and self-motivation.

  • Reads, writes, and understands English; reliable daily transportation required.

What You Bring

  • High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent.

  • 3–5 years of telecom/structured cabling experience (data center experience a strong plus).

  • OSHA10 preferred (must obtain within 90 days).

  • First Aid/CPR certification within 90 days.

  • FOA certifications, BICSI cabling certifications, or similar credentials preferred.

  • Proficient experience installing, terminating, and testing fiber (single-mode/multi-mode connections)

  • Proficiency with various testers - Fluke, OTDR, and VFL

  • Highly preferred - experience splicing fiber

Work Environment & Physical Demands

This is an active, hands-on role inside data centers and technology rich environments.

You will:

  • Work primarily indoors, with occasional outdoor tasks.

  • Experience moderate noise levels typical of construction and data center settings.

  • Regularly sit, kneel, stoop, climb, crawl, reach, talk, and hear during tasks.

  • Frequently stand and walk for extended periods.

  • Regularly lift and/or move up to 50 lbs and frequently lift up to 25 lbs.

  • Work in tight or confined spaces, raised floors, and sometimes at heights using ladders or lifts.

  • Wear PPE and follow all safety protocols.

Reasonable accommodations may be made for qualified individuals with disabilities.

Work Location & Travel

  • Onsite daily at customer or data center locations.

  • Minimal overnight travel (≈5%), but flexibility is required when project needs shift.

Required Tools

  • Candidates must bring and maintain a professional tool kit including (but not limited to):
    Notepad, tool pouch, cable sheath stripper, punch tools, scissors, screwdrivers, pliers, utility knife, tape measure, torpedo level, channel locks, hammer, wrench sets, socket sets, nut drivers, flashlight/headlamp, cordless drill, cordless impact, VFL, toner set, and cable tester.

This job description is designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, and responsibilities that are required of the employee; it is not meant to be all-inclusive for any one position. Job responsibilities and requirements are subject to change at any time due to business conditions or any other reason.

Black Box is a leading global technology solutions provider with 2,500+ team members across 24 countries. We value innovation, ownership, transparency, and continuous growth—both in our business and our people. title: Member of Technical Staff, Agents

What We're Looking For

Compensation & Benefits

title: Director, Cloud Platform Engineering
description:
We made history and now we work to transform the future – for our customers, our communities and our families. You'll see your work on the road every day, helping people move freely and pursue their dreams. At Ford, you can build more than vehicles. Come build what matters.

Enterprise Technology plays a critical part in shaping the future of mobility. If you’re looking for the chance to leverage advanced technology to redefine the transportation landscape, enhance the customer experience and improve people’s lives, this is the opportunity for you. Join us and challenge your IT expertise and analytical skills to help create vehicles that are as smart as you are.

In this position...

Ford is seeking a visionary Director, Cloud Platform Engineering – Data, Analytics & Agentic Data Cloud to own strategy, architecture, and engineering of Ford's cloud database and analytics platforms — built on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) services including Cloud SQL, Spanner, AlloyDB, BigTable, Firestore, and BigQuery. This leader will bring a product-minded, automation-first, Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) platform engineering discipline to every layer of Ford's data estate, own Database-as-a-Service (DBaaS) and fit-for-purpose database architecture patterns for Product Development Organizations (PDO), drive consolidation and cost optimization of SaaS database products, and define Ford's Agentic Data Cloud patterns — including database MCP servers, Knowledge Catalog, and Conversational Analytics — for consumption by application teams.

What you'll do...

Platform Engineering Vision & Leadership

  • Serve as Ford's visionary platform engineering leader for cloud databases and analytics — setting a multi-year strategic roadmap that anticipates future AI, security, and scale requirements.
  • Instill a platform engineering mindset across the data estate — treating databases and analytics systems as internal products with self-service APIs, golden paths, paved roads, and clear SLOs rather than ticket-driven infrastructure.
  • Drive all platform services through an Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) mindset — defining, provisioning, and managing database and analytics infrastructure as version-controlled, testable, and repeatable code rather than manual configuration.
  • Continue to deepen partnerships with cloud and SaaS vendors, co-building rich, differentiated capabilities within their platforms so Ford operates as a strategic technical partner rather than a passive consumer.
  • Build, mentor, and lead a global, high-performing team of platform engineers, architects, and SREs; foster a culture of innovation through hackathons, ideathons, and DevSecOps community events.

Cloud Database & Analytics Platform Engineering

  • Architect and operate GCP-native database platforms (Cloud SQL, Spanner, AlloyDB, BigTable, Firestore) with consistent, reusable, IaC-driven platform engineering patterns across provisioning, security, and observability.
  • Own platform engineering for BigQuery and the broader analytics stack — building governed, self-service data pipelines and reusable analytics tooling for product and data science teams.
  • Build golden-path templates, service APIs, and IaC-based paved-road automation that let engineering teams provision and operate database and analytics resources safely and consistently at scale.

Database-as-a-Service & Fit-for-Purpose Architecture

  • Own Ford's Cloud Database-as-a-Service (DBaaS) strategy, enabling self-service provisioning across GCP-native and SaaS database platforms with automated, golden-path IaC pipelines.
  • Define and evangelize database architecture patterns that guide Product Development Organizations (PDO) toward fit-for-purpose database selection — matching workload characteristics to the right relational, NoSQL, graph, or in-memory technology rather than defaulting to a single platform.
  • Partner with PDO application and engineering teams to embed these architecture patterns into design reviews, reference architectures, and reusable templates.
  • SaaS Consolidation & Cost Optimization
  • Lead enterprise-wide consolidation of SaaS database products (e.g., MongoDB, Neo4J, Redis), reducing platform sprawl, redundant licensing, and support overhead.
  • Own full lifecycle management of database, analytics, and SaaS platforms — versioning, patching, upgrade planning, end-of-life tracking, and decommissioning of unused resources — to proactively eliminate unnecessary and duplicate cost.
  • Own full lifecycle management of database, analytics, and SaaS platforms — versioning, patching, upgrade planning, end-of-life tracking, and decommissioning of unused resources — to proactively eliminate unnecessary and duplicate cost.
  • Own cost-optimization strategy and cloud-cost mindsets (rightsizing, usage governance, cost recommenders) across the data platform portfolio; manage vendor contracts and negotiate enterprise agreements.

Agentic Data Cloud

  • Define and evangelize Ford's Agentic Data Cloud strategy, shifting the enterprise from a passive system of intelligence to an agent-centric system of action.
  • Provide application teams with standardized, reusable patterns for database MCP (Model Context Protocol) Servers, enabling AI agents to safely discover, reason over, and act on enterprise data.
  • Lead deployment of Knowledge Catalog capabilities for AI-context governance and data discoverability, and roll out Conversational Analytics patterns for natural-language data interaction across Ford's applications.
  • Define guardrails and human-in-the-loop controls aligned to Ford's Agentic AI Rubric; partner with Google product and engineering teams (GDIA, Enterprise Architecture) on POC design and service launch frameworks.

You'll have...

  • 15+ years in software engineering, cloud architecture, and data platform services, including significant leadership experience.
  • Proven platform engineering ownership of large-scale database and analytics environments on GCP (Cloud SQL, Spanner, AlloyDB, BigTable, Firestore, BigQuery).
  • Strong hands-on experience with Infrastructure-as-Code tooling and practices, driving platform services through code-defined, version-controlled automation rather than manual provisioning.
  • Direct experience with SaaS database platforms (MongoDB, Neo4J, Elastic, Redis), including consolidation and cost-optimization initiatives at enterprise scale.
  • Demonstrated success owning DBaaS and defining fit-for-purpose database architecture patterns adopted by application/product teams.
  • Demonstrated experience with agentic AI and data platform concepts — MCP servers, Knowledge Catalog, Conversational Analytics, and AI governance frameworks.
  • Strong background in DevOps/SRE practices, automation, CI/CD, and observability.
  • Bachelor's degree required

Even better, you may have...

  • Excellent executive communication skills and ability to lead through influence;
  • Master's degree preferred

You may not check every box, or your experience may look a little different from what we've outlined, but if you think you can bring value to Ford Motor Company, we encourage you to apply!

As an established global company, we offer the benefit of choice. You can choose what your Ford future will look like: will your story span the globe, or keep you close to home? Will your career be a deep dive into what you love, or a series of new teams and new skills? Will you be a leader, a changemaker, a technical expert, a culture builder…or all of the above? No matter what you choose, we offer a work life that works for you, including:

title: Supply Specialist
description:
Supply Specialist – USARCENT G4

Location: Shaw Air Force Base, South Carolina (On-site)
Security Clearance: Active SECRET Clearance Required
Employment Type: Full-Time

Position Summary

UpSlope is seeking an experienced Supply Specialist to support U.S. Army Central (USARCENT) G4 logistics operations at Shaw Air Force Base, South Carolina.

The Supply Specialist will provide supply chain management, inventory accountability, logistics coordination, and operational support to help ensure equipment, supplies, and materials are properly managed and available to support mission requirements.

The ideal candidate will have experience supporting Army or Department of Defense (DoD) supply operations, a strong understanding of military logistics procedures, and the ability to maintain accurate supply records in a fast-paced operational environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support USARCENT G4 supply and logistics operations, ensuring effective management and accountability of supplies, equipment, and organizational property.
  • Assist with tracking, coordinating, and maintaining supply requirements across supported units and staff sections.
  • Maintain accurate inventory records, supply documentation, equipment accountability reports, and related logistics data.
  • Support requisitioning, receiving, issuing, transferring, and tracking supplies and equipment.
  • Monitor supply requests, shipment status, shortages, and backorders to help ensure operational readiness.
  • Assist with property accountability, hand receipts, inventory reconciliations, and equipment inspections.
  • Coordinate with military personnel, supply representatives, logistics staff, and other stakeholders to resolve supply-related issues.
  • Prepare supply status reports, inventory summaries, spreadsheets, and briefings for G4 leadership.
  • Identify supply discrepancies, shortages, and potential logistical challenges and recommend corrective actions.
  • Support supply planning activities related to exercises, operational requirements, and mission readiness.
  • Ensure supply records and processes align with applicable Army and DoD policies and procedures.
  • Assist with improving supply tracking, reporting, and accountability processes.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Previous experience in military supply operations, logistics, inventory management, property accountability, or a closely related field.
  • Working knowledge of Army or DoD supply procedures, logistics operations, and equipment accountability practices.
  • Experience maintaining inventory records, supply documentation, or property accountability systems.
  • Ability to track supply requirements, identify discrepancies, and coordinate resolutions.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to communicate and coordinate effectively with military, civilian, and contractor personnel.
  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple logistical requirements.
  • Active SECRET security clearance required.
  • Ability to work full-time on-site at Shaw Air Force Base, South Carolina.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous experience supporting an Army G4, S4, sustainment command, or military logistics organization.
  • Experience with Army supply and property accountability systems, such as Global Combat Support System–Army (GCSS-Army).
  • Familiarity with Army supply regulations, including AR 710-2 and AR 735-5.
  • Experience with cyclic inventories, hand receipts, property book management, and supply reconciliation.
  • Experience supporting military exercises, deployments, or operational logistics activities.
  • Familiarity with supply readiness reporting and logistics information management.
  • Prior military service or civilian experience supporting Army supply operations.

Work Environment

This position supports USARCENT Headquarters at Shaw Air Force Base, South Carolina.

  • Full-time, on-site position.
  • Standard working hours are generally Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM–4:30 PM, including a 30-minute unpaid lunch.
  • Work involves coordination with Army personnel, DoD civilians, and contractor support staff.
  • Occasional travel may be required depending on mission needs.

Security Requirements

Candidates must possess and maintain an active SECRET security clearance and meet applicable installation and government systems access requirements.

About UpSlope

UpSlope delivers mission-focused professional services and operational support to federal government clients. Our team works alongside military and civilian organizations to provide reliable, innovative solutions that strengthen operational efficiency, readiness, and mission success.

title: Challenge Course Instructor
description:
Application Instructions

  • Application closes November 29
  • Instead of a cover letter, the application will ask some scheduling questions and "what about this position interests you?"
  • Interviews will start the week of December 1

Position Description

Come join our close-knit community of passionate outdoor educators as a challenge Course Instructor. You will facilitate day programs at our Challenge Course in McLaren Park, San Francisco with Bay Area youth (grades 6-12) and community members. You’ll plan the flow of the day, set up and break down the challenge course, and safely facilitate students through high & low ropes elements, ground games, and team-building activities. We’ll teach you how to deliver programs that instill courage, teamwork, confidence, and self-awareness in our participants. Make a difference in the Bay Area as we get folks outside and build community together!


Compensation & Schedule (Part-Time)

  • Starting wage is $24.25/hr with opportunities to promote to lead positions (up to $29.80/hr).
  • This is a part-time, non-exempt, hourly position, typically 2.5-3 days a week (~20 hrs/week).
  • Staff meet to prepare for the week for a half day on most Mondays, with a full-day meeting about once a month. Student programs run Tuesday-Friday (with occasional Saturdays). Staff shifts vary depending on the group’s timing, but are most often 8am-4pm.
  • Our season begins in late January with two weeks of required paid training. Our season ends in November with opportunities to return for the following season.
  • Paid Training: 8 hrs/day, 4 days per week between Mon-Fri, Jan 25 - Feb 5, 2027.
  • Program Season: Mon-Sat, Feb 9 - Nov 18, 2027.
  • There is an unpaid summer break of programs from June 7-11 & July 26-30, 2027.
  • Availability of work is dependent on the number of booked programs.

Benefits (Part-Time)

  • Paid Time Off - Accrue 1 hour for every 13 hrs worked.
  • Unpaid Time Off - Employees can accrue up to 80 hours of unpaid time off each year.
  • 401K after 1-year of employment.
  • Pro Deals (the opportunity to purchase outdoor gear at discounted rates)
  • Free youth development training, professional development funds, and recertification reimbursements.
  • Access to Employee Assistance Program (EAP), free of charge for staff and family members.
  • All required training is paid.

Location

Most program days take place at the McLaren Park Ropes Course in southeast San Francisco.


Who We Are

At Outward Bound California (OBCA) we use challenging outdoor experiences to teach social-emotional skills like teamwork, leadership, and compassion. We offer a wide range of programs, including high/low ropes activities at our San Francisco Challenge Course and multi-day rock climbing/backpacking trips in the High Sierra and Joshua Tree. Our programs encourage our participants (ages 12+, including adults and veterans) to embrace challenges and reflect on how they want to contribute to their communities and the world. To learn more about our ropes course elements, check out the video tour.


We are a part of the Outward Bound USA network with a 65-year history in the US as a leading provider of outdoor education. OBCA is a non-profit and is committed to increasing access for those who have traditionally been excluded from outdoor spaces. We work towards this goal with our 40 community partners and by offering scholarships to more than half of our students.


OBCA strives to create an equitable and inclusive culture where our staff feel respected for their identities and lived experiences. We are looking for team members who can actively join us in the process of furthering our vision for equity and belonging. We recognize that the outdoor industry has historically excluded those with non-dominant identities and know that has led to underrepresentation in this line of work. We strongly encourage those who more significantly face the impacts of exclusion and oppression to apply.

title: Technical Trainer
description:
About Parsec

Parsec Automation, LLC (Parsec) is a trailblazing creator and provider of manufacturing operations management software. Consistently recognized by organizations like Gartner and IDC and a winner of numerous awards, including the Data Breakthrough Awards, American Business, and Best in Biz, Parsec exemplifies leadership in the dynamic, fast-paced manufacturing sector. With major companies such as Johnson & Johnson, Merck, Toyota, Proctor & Gamble, Eli Lilly, Hershey, Siemens, and DuPont leveraging its innovative TrakSYS™ platform to tackle even the most complex manufacturing challenges, Parsec's solutions are actively optimizing efficiency, quality, and compliance at over 11,000 plants in more than 140 countries. Committed to customer success and driven by innovation, Parsec continues to fulfill its mission of making the management of manufacturing operations as simple as possible.

Parsec is backed by BVP Forge, a $780M fund in partnership with the $20B Bessemer platform that has backed industry-defining businesses such as LinkedIn, MindBody, Procore, Shopify, and Toast. BVP Forge combines Bessemer's front-line industry insights, proven growth IP, and robust executive network with tailored resources for self-sustaining companies and the ForgeEdge™ operational program.

The Role

Parsec is hiring a Technical Trainer to join the Technical Enablement team, reporting to the Director of Technical Enablement.

This role facilitates instructor-led TrakSYS™ bootcamps for internal staff, partners, and customers. Delivery begins virtually and will expand to in-person sessions as the program grows. Approximately 70% of the role is facilitation and learner support; the remaining 30% is revising and developing the content the bootcamps run on.

The role requires both facilitation skill and technical fluency. You will be expected to learn the bootcamp's technical simulations thoroughly and handle unscripted questions and live troubleshooting in front of a technical audience.

You will work closely with TrakSYS™ subject matter experts to support learners and keep training content accurate as the product evolves.

Key Responsibilities

  • Facilitate virtual instructor-led TrakSYS™ bootcamp sessions, expanding to in-person delivery as the program grows.
  • Learn the bootcamp's technical simulations and scenarios in depth and guide learners through the simulated plant experience, including unscripted questions and live troubleshooting.
  • Manage the learner experience across each cohort, including pre-work, session pacing, hands-on lab support, and follow-through on open items.
  • Support trainees between sessions through office hours and live Q&A, with assistance from a TrakSYS™ SME.
  • Conduct train-the-trainer sessions to certify additional internal and partner facilitators as the program scales.
  • Revise existing modules based on delivery experience, learner feedback, and product releases.
  • Coordinate peer reviews with SMEs to confirm technical accuracy and clarity.
  • Assist in creating and maintaining instructor-led content, including presentations, facilitator guides, simulated storylines, and lab exercises.
  • Continue developing knowledge of the TrakSYS™ platform, adult learning practice, and the manufacturing sector.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Education, Instructional Design, Engineering, Information Technology, Business, or a related field.
  • 5-8 years of experience facilitating technical training for adult professional learners.
  • Demonstrated experience facilitating technical training both virtually and in person.
  • Technical fluency sufficient to configure and troubleshoot within an enterprise application.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to stay composed and lead a session in front of a technical audience.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team, with strong initiative and follow-through.
  • Willingness to travel (up to 20%) domestically and internationally for in-person delivery.

Preferred / Nice to Have

  • Domain knowledge of manufacturing, MES, ERP, or related enterprise applications.
  • Experience creating content for and/or conducting train-the-trainer sessions.
  • Experience supporting a partner channel.

Compensation / Benefits

  • $90,000 – $100,000 annual base salary
  • Variable bonus based on company and individual performance
  • 100% company-paid health insurance premiums for employee
  • Flexible vacation time
  • Outstanding team environment

Job Summary:

The Engineer III is a highly skilled maintenance professional responsible for ensuring the safe, efficient, and uninterrupted operation of all hotel facilities, building systems, and equipment while delivering exceptional guest experiences. This position performs advanced preventive and corrective maintenance, serves as a technical resource within their primary trade expertise, and provides guidance and support to junior engineering team members. The Engineer III responds to maintenance requests throughout guest rooms, meeting spaces, food and beverage outlets, public areas, and back-of-house facilities, while helping ensure compliance with all safety standards and regulatory requirements. Success in this role requires strong technical expertise, hospitality experience, exceptional troubleshooting skills, and a commitment to maintaining the luxury standards of Regent Santa Monica Beach.

A little bit about your day:

Reporting to the Assistant Director of Engineering every day is different, but you’ll mostly:

  • Perform advanced preventive and corrective maintenance, troubleshooting, and repairs involving electrical, plumbing, HVAC, refrigeration, carpentry, painting, locksmith, fire life safety, lighting, communication, and other building systems while serving as the primary resource within your designated trade expertise.
  • Respond to maintenance requests, guest concerns, and emergency situations throughout guest rooms, meeting spaces, food and beverage outlets, public areas, and back-of-house facilities while maintaining luxury service standards.
  • Review complaint logs, maintenance requests, and work order systems daily, completing assignments dispatched through HotSOS, Espresso, or similar platforms.
  • Provide training, guidance, and technical support to junior engineering team members while promoting teamwork and operational excellence.
  • Monitor, maintain, and help optimize the safe, efficient, and economical operation of all hotel equipment and building systems.
  • Assist the Chief Engineer and Assistant Director of Engineering with room inspections, facility inspections, regulatory compliance efforts, and preventative maintenance programs.
  • Complete documentation related to maintenance activities, communicate assignment status to supervisors and dispatchers, and promptly report significant repair concerns or unusual operating conditions.
  • Perform minor function and event setups, equipment repairs, guest assistance requests, and maintenance support activities throughout the property.
  • Maintain inventories of tools, equipment, supplies, and replacement materials while ensuring engineering shops, storage areas, and workspaces remain clean, organized, and operationally ready.
  • Safely operate tools, equipment, materials, and chemicals in accordance with hotel standards, manufacturer guidelines, and safety procedures.
  • Execute hotel emergency procedures, support sustainability initiatives, comply with all safety regulations, policies, and grooming standards, and remain current on hotel updates and operational changes.
  • Perform other duties and special projects as assigned by hotel leadership.

Requirements:

  • High school diploma, vocational training, or post-secondary education in Engineering, Maintenance, Facilities Management, or a related discipline preferred.
  • Minimum three (3) years of hands-on maintenance experience required, preferably within a luxury hotel, resort, or commercial facility environment; previous hospitality experience required.
  • Ability to read, write, and speak English fluently and communicate effectively with guests, colleagues, and leadership.
  • Advanced knowledge of plumbing, electrical, HVAC, refrigeration, boilers, pumps, lighting, fire life safety, communication systems, and preventative maintenance practices.
  • Experience using maintenance management and building systems software such as HotSOS, Espresso, Opera, Lutron, Bartech, Inncom, Microsoft Office, or similar platforms preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot complex maintenance issues, safely operate hand and power tools, and mentor junior engineering team members.
  • Must be guest-focused with exceptional hospitality, organizational, problem-solving, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to bend, stoop, kneel, climb, and lift up to 75 pounds, and work a flexible schedule including weekends, holidays, and varied shifts.

What you can expect from us:

The hourly pay rate for this role is $24.65 - $30.82. This rate is only applicable for jobs to be performed at Regent Santa Monica Beach. This is the lowest to highest pay scale we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. A colleague’s pay position within the pay range will be based on several factors including, but limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, shift, travel requirements, sales or revenue-based metrics, and business or organizational needs.
