title: Spécialiste principal(e) DevOps | Senior DevOps Specialist
description:
Raison d'être du poste

À titre de spécialiste principal(e) DevOps, vous jouerez un rôle clé dans la conception, le maintien et l'évolution des infrastructures, des systèmes d'automatisation et des mécanismes de déploiement qui soutiennent notre vision de Créer des moments qui touchent les gens.

Vous concevrez et mettrez en œuvre de façon autonome des solutions d'infrastructure, améliorerez les capacités d'automatisation soutenant l'ensemble du cycle de livraison logicielle et contribuerez à maintenir des plateformes fiables, évolutives et sécuritaires.

Grâce à votre capacité à résoudre des problèmes complexes et à votre collaboration avec les équipes d'ingénierie, vous contribuerez au renforcement des pratiques DevOps, au mentorat de collègues moins expérimentés et à l'orientation des décisions relatives à l'infrastructure.

Responsabilités principales

Le ou la spécialiste principal(e) DevOps est responsable de la livraison de solutions d'infrastructure et d'automatisation fiables, sécuritaires et évolutives soutenant nos produits, projets et plateformes logicielles.

La personne titulaire du poste devra :

  • Collaborer étroitement avec les architectes DevOps et logiciels afin de concevoir, mettre en œuvre et maintenir l'infrastructure conformément à la stratégie produit et technique.
  • Concevoir, mettre en œuvre et maintenir l'infrastructure en tant que code (Infrastructure as Code), les pipelines d'intégration et de livraison continues (CI/CD) ainsi que les mécanismes d'automatisation des déploiements dans des environnements infonuagiques et locaux.
  • Configurer, maintenir et dépanner les environnements de développement, de test et de production, y compris les configurations systèmes et la gestion des dépendances.
  • Prendre en charge les initiatives d'infrastructure et d'automatisation de la conception jusqu'à la validation finale.
  • Surveiller la santé et la performance des systèmes et intervenir lors d'incidents afin d'assurer leur disponibilité et leur fiabilité.
  • Identifier et résoudre des enjeux complexes d'infrastructure dans des environnements de développement, de préproduction et de production, tant dans le nuage que sur du matériel local.
  • Gérer les dépendances logicielles, les versions et la cohérence des environnements de développement et de déploiement, tout en assurant la conformité des licences et l'identification des vulnérabilités.
  • Collaborer avec les équipes d'ingénierie logicielle afin d'intégrer les pratiques d'infrastructure et de déploiement à leurs processus de développement.
  • Contribuer à l'amélioration des outils, méthodes de travail et standards DevOps.
  • Encadrer et soutenir les spécialistes DevOps moins expérimentés dans leur développement professionnel.
  • Maintenir une documentation claire de la configuration des infrastructures et des processus opérationnels.
  • Participer à l'évaluation et à l'intégration de nouvelles technologies favorisant l'automatisation et la fiabilité.
  • Explorer et adopter de façon proactive des outils et flux de travail fondés sur l'intelligence artificielle afin d'améliorer votre efficacité personnelle ainsi que les activités d'automatisation, de dépannage et de gestion des infrastructures.
  • Effectuer toute autre tâche requise afin de répondre aux besoins de l'entreprise.

Qualifications et expérience

Formation

  • Baccalauréat, DEC ou DEP en informatique, en technologies de l'information ou expérience pertinente équivalente.


Expérience, connaissances et compétences

  • Minimum de 6 années d'expérience professionnelle en génie logiciel, infrastructure, ingénierie de plateforme ou environnements DevOps, dont au moins 4 années consacrées aux pratiques DevOps, à l'automatisation de l'infrastructure, aux pipelines CI/CD, aux déploiements infonuagiques ou locaux, ou à des responsabilités connexes.
  • Expérience pratique de la gestion de configuration des environnements (approvisionnement et préparation des environnements), tant dans le nuage que sur du matériel local.
  • Solide expertise en gestion des dépendances et des paquets logiciels dans plusieurs langages et technologies ainsi qu'en maintien de la cohérence des environnements.
  • Capacité démontrée à concevoir, mettre en œuvre et maintenir des infrastructures avec un minimum de supervision.
  • Une expérience en conteneurisation et en orchestration constitue un atout.
  • Connaissance des meilleures pratiques en matière de surveillance, de journalisation et de gestion des incidents.
  • Excellentes capacités d'analyse et de résolution de problèmes, y compris dans des contextes techniques peu familiers.
  • Bonnes compétences en communication et capacité à documenter et présenter clairement des solutions techniques.
  • Aisance dans un environnement dynamique et en constante évolution.
  • Désir d'identifier de façon proactive les possibilités d'amélioration des systèmes, outils et processus.

Une connaissance fonctionnelle de l’anglais, tant à l’oral qu’à l’écrit, est requise pour ce poste. Cette exigence est nécessaire puisque la personne titulaire du poste devra :

  • collaborer régulièrement avec des collègues, équipes et partenaires situés à l’extérieur du Québec dont la langue de travail est l’anglais;
  • participer à des réunions techniques, des revues de code et des discussions de conception tenues en anglais;
  • consulter, analyser et utiliser de la documentation technique, des outils de développement, des cadres logiciels (frameworks) et des ressources spécialisées principalement disponibles en anglais;
  • rédiger ou réviser de la documentation technique, des commentaires de code et des communications destinées à des équipes anglophones;
  • contribuer à des projets logiciels mondiaux nécessitant des échanges fréquents en anglais.

ENGLISH


Position Purpose

As a Senior DevOps Specialist, you will play a key role in building and maintaining the infrastructure, automation, and deployment systems that power our vision to Create Moments that Move People. You will independently design and implement infrastructure solutions, improve automation to support all aspects of software delivery, and help ensure our platforms remain reliable, scalable, and secure.

Through proactive problem-solving and close collaboration with engineering teams, you will strengthen our DevOps practices, mentor less experienced engineers and influence infrastructure decisions.

Responsibilities

The Senior DevOps Specialist is responsible for delivering reliable, secure, and scalable infrastructure and automation solutions that support our software products, projects and platform.

The Senior DevOps Specialist will:

  • Work closely alongside DevOps and software architects to design, implement, and maintain infrastructure in alignment with product and technical strategy.
  • Design, implement, and maintain infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD pipelines, and deployment automation across cloud and on-premises environments.
  • Configure, maintain, and troubleshoot build, test, and production infrastructure, including OS-level configuration and dependency management.
  • Take ownership of infrastructure and automation tasks from design through implementation and validation.
  • Monitor system health and performance, and respond to incidents to maintain reliability and uptime.
  • Identify and resolve complex infrastructure issues across development, staging and production environments spanning cloud and local hardware.
  • Manage software dependencies, versioning, and environment consistency across development and deployment targets, ensuring license compliance and identification of vulnerabilities.
  • Collaborate with software engineering teams to integrate infrastructure and deployment practices into their development process.

title: Senior Director, Development & Communications
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, the Senior Director, Development & Communications serves as a member of SDRI's Executive Leadership Team and leads all fundraising, development operations, marketing, communications, donor engagement, community relations, and external affairs activities.

This role is both strategic and hands-on, responsible for advancing philanthropic support, strengthening organizational visibility, expanding community engagement, and supporting the long-term sustainability of the organization. The Senior Director works collaboratively with executive leadership, the Board of Trustees, donors, foundations, corporate partners, volunteers, community leaders, and external stakeholders to advance SDRI's mission and achieve annual fundraising and organizational goals.

The Senior Director serves as a key member of SDRI's Executive Leadership Team and provides strategic leadership across fundraising, communications, community engagement, and organizational growth initiatives.

The title and level of the position will be determined based on the selected candidate's qualifications, experience, leadership background, and demonstrated development and fundraising expertise.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES



Major Gifts & Philanthropy

  • Develop and execute comprehensive fundraising and advancement strategies that support SDRI's strategic priorities, annual operating needs, and long-term sustainability, while achieving revenue goals established by leadership and the Board.
  • Manage a portfolio of major donors and prospects through identification, cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and retention activities, partnering closely with the CEO, Board of Trustees, and volunteer leaders to advance philanthropic investments.
  • Oversee all philanthropic revenue streams, including major gifts, foundations, grants, corporate partnerships, sponsorships, institutional funding, and planned and legacy giving programs.
  • Direct donor stewardship, recognition, moves management, fundraising forecasting, analytics, and reporting to strengthen donor engagement and support informed decision-making.
  • Establish and monitor fundraising performance metrics, pipeline activity, and revenue projections, and lead special fundraising campaigns and strategic initiatives as assigned.


Marketing, Communications & Community Engagement

  • Lead SDRI's marketing, communications, public relations, and community engagement strategies to strengthen organizational visibility, enhance stakeholder engagement, increase public awareness, and support fundraising objectives.
  • Partner with the CEO to communicate SDRI's mission, impact, research and clinical advancements, strategic priorities, and community benefit through compelling and consistent messaging across all channels.
  • Oversee brand management, donor communications, annual reports, fundraising campaigns, newsletters, website content, social media, digital marketing, media relations, storytelling initiatives, and public awareness efforts.
  • Cultivate and maintain relationships with donors, community leaders, healthcare organizations, civic groups, elected officials, media representatives, strategic partners, and other key stakeholders while serving as a visible ambassador for the organization.
  • Manage external marketing, public relations, graphic design, digital media, and creative services providers, while monitoring performance metrics and identifying opportunities to expand community partnerships and organizational reach.


Signature Fundraising Events

  • Provide strategic leadership and oversight for Taste of the Vine and other fundraising events, ensuring alignment with organizational objectives and annual revenue goals.
  • Direct all aspects of event fundraising, including sponsorship development, donor cultivation, auction activities, volunteer engagement, and revenue-generating initiatives.
  • Partner with sponsors, committees, volunteers, donors, and community stakeholders to maximize participation, visibility, fundraising performance, and attendee experience.
  • Oversee event planning, budgeting, execution, and post-event evaluation to ensure operational excellence and achievement of financial objectives.
  • Analyze event outcomes and implement continuous improvements to strengthen revenue generation, donor engagement, and long-term event sustainability.


Development Operations

  • Provide leadership and oversight of development operations, including donor database administration, gift processing, prospect management, stewardship systems, fundraising reporting, and CRM optimization.
  • Ensure the accuracy, integrity, security, and confidentiality of donor and fundraising data while maintaining compliance with applicable regulations, reporting requirements, and privacy standards.
  • Develop and monitor departmental budgets, revenue forecasts, key performance indicators, fundraising dashboards, and operational goals to support strategic decision-making.
  • Establish and maintain efficient systems, policies, and procedures that support fundraising effectiveness, donor stewardship, and organizational accountability.
  • Continuously evaluate and enhance processes, reporting capabilities, and technology platforms to improve operational efficiency and fundraising performance.


Leadership & Organizational Management

  • Serve as a member of the Executive Leadership Team, contributing to organizational strategy, long-range planning, growth initiatives, decision-making, and sustainability efforts.
  • Act as a strategic advisor to the CEO and Board of Trustees on fundraising, communications, community engagement, external relations, and organizational visibility.
  • Lead departmental planning, budgeting, goal setting, performance measurement, resource allocation, and strategic initiatives to ensure alignment with organizational priorities.
  • Supervise and develop staff, consultants, volunteers, and vendors while fostering collaboration, accountability, professional growth, and operational excellence.
  • Present fundraising, communications, and organizational performance data to executive leadership and the Board, while supporting Board engagement in fundraising, stewardship, advocacy, and ambassador activities.


QUALIFICATIONS

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform the essential functions of the position satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills, abilities, education, and experience necessary to perform the essential functions of the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Training and support may be provided as appropriate to facilitate successful job performance.



  • Demonstrated leadership and strategic expertise in philanthropy, fundraising, communications, communications, external relations, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Demonstrated success securing, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding major gifts of $100,000 or more, as well as grants and institutional funding from individuals, corporations, foundations, and philanthropic partners.
  • Exceptional relationship-building skills with executive leaders, board members, donors, community stakeholders, grant funders, and strategic partners.
  • Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and public speaking skills.
  • Strong strategic planning, organizational, analytical, and project management skills.
  • Experience developing and monitoring departmental budgets, fundraising forecasts, performance metrics, and operational goals.
  • Experience leading fundraising campaigns, donor stewardship initiatives, and community engagement programs.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications, including Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Teams, and SharePoint.
  • Experience using donor database and CRM systems, preferably Raiser's Edge NXT.
  • Demonstrated professionalism, sound judgment, discretion, and commitment to maintaining confidentiality.
  • Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends and travel as needed for donor, community, and organizational activities.



EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Nonprofit Management, Communications, Marketing, Public Relations, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and professional experience, required.
  • Master's degree in a related discipline and/or Certified Fund Raising Executive (CFRE) credential preferred.
  • Minimum seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience in nonprofit development, philanthropy, advancement, fundraising, communications, or related fields.
  • Strong preference for candidates with ten (10) or more years of relevant fundraising and development leadership experience.
  • Demonstrated success leading comprehensive fundraising programs, including major gifts, foundation relations, planned giving, donor stewardship, corporate partnerships, and revenue growth initiatives.
  • Experience partnering with executive leadership and governing boards to advance organizational priorities, fundraising objectives, and community engagement efforts.
  • Experience within healthcare, medical research, academic medicine, public health, higher education, or other mission-driven nonprofit organizations preferred.

LANGUAGE SKILLS



Ability to read, write, understand, and communicate effectively in English, both verbally and in writing, as necessary to perform the essential functions of the position.



PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

The employee is regularly required to communicate effectively, remain stationary for extended periods, and operate a computer and other standard office equipment. Frequent use of hands and fingers for computer keyboarding, document preparation, and other administrative functions is required. The employee must be able to work at a computer and view a computer monitor for extended periods.

The employee may occasionally be required to stand, walk, reach, bend, and climb stairs while performing job duties, attending meetings, or participating in organizational events. Movement between offices and facility areas located on separate floors may be required. The employee must occasionally lift, carry, push, or move items weighing up to 25 pounds.

This position requires the ability to communicate effectively in person, by telephone, and through virtual communication platforms. Attendance at meetings, fundraising events, community activities, and donor engagements may require prolonged periods of standing or walking.

The employee must be able to perform the essential functions of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment is primarily an office setting. The employee may be required to move throughout SDRI facilities, including administrative, clinical care, and clinical research areas located on separate floors, in the performance of their job responsibilities. Attendance at meetings, community events, fundraising activities, and donor engagements may require occasional evening or weekend work. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position. The noise level in the work environment is typically moderate, and lighting is primarily artificial office lighting.

This job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed by individuals assigned to this position. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications. Management reserves the right to modify, assign, or remove duties and responsibilities as organizational needs change. Other duties may be assigned as required.

title: Head of Sport Science
description:
About Strava

Strava is the app for active people. With over 200 million athletes in more than 185 countries, it’s more than tracking workouts—it’s where people make progress together, from new habits to new personal bests. No matter your sport or how you track it, Strava’s got you covered. Find your crew, crush your goals, and make every effort count. Start your journey with Strava today.

Our mission is simple: to motivate people to live their best active lives. We believe in the power of movement to connect and drive people forward.

About This Role

Sport Science sits outside Product, Tech, and Runna, reporting directly to the CEO. The team is responsible for the ongoing scientific validation and safety of Strava's and Runna's fitness products, and for the applied research agenda that pushes forward the science of sport and fitness.

As Head of Sport Science, you'll own two things at once: the ongoing scientific validation and safety review of Runna's and Strava's fitness products, and the applied research agenda behind them. You'll manage and grow academic partnerships, define the data and benchmarks needed to make our models' insights scientifically defensible, and grow a team over time. You'll work closely with the coaching team, AI/ML, Data Science, Product, Public Policy, and Legal.

We follow a flexible hybrid model that translates to more than half of your time on-site in our San Francisco office, three days per week.

What You'll Do:

  • Own the ongoing scientific validation and safety review of Runna's and Strava's fitness products, starting with the open items in an active academic audit

  • Manage and grow academic partnerships with Stanford University and Loughborough University, and scope new partnerships as needed

  • Define the data and label strategy, such as perceived exertion, injury history, and sleep, that makes our models' insights scientifically defensible, partnering closely with Data Science and AI/ML

  • Partner with Runna's coaching team on a recurring review cadence, serving as the scientific authority on disputed questions about the application of science in coaching

  • Build out the Sport Science team, plus an external academic advisory council, over time

  • Represent Strava's scientific credibility in external settings, from published research to occasional conference talks.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • An MD, PhD, or equivalent applied track record in exercise physiology, sports science, biomechanics, sports medicine, or a closely related field

  • Substantial experience combining peer-reviewed research with applied work in industry, elite sport, or a research-focused sports medicine setting, translating science into product decisions

  • A track record of managing external academic or clinical partnerships, including agreements, multi-institution collaborations, and ethics-related governance

  • Comfort partnering with data science and ML teams to translate research questions into model and data requirements is a plus, though you won't need to write code yourself

  • Experience building a team or function from its first hire is a plus

  • A track record of representing scientific work externally, such as a paper, a conference talk, or a podcast, is a plus

  • Endurance or running-specific research experience is a plus, though not required

Why Join Us?

Movement brings us together. At Strava, we’re building the world’s largest community of active people, helping them stay motivated and achieve their goals.

Our global team is passionate about making movement fun, meaningful, and accessible to everyone. Whether you’re shaping the technology, growing our community, or driving innovation, your work at Strava makes an impact.

When you join Strava, you’re not just joining a company—you’re joining a movement. If you’re ready to bring your energy, ideas, and drive, let’s build something incredible together.

Strava builds software that makes the best part of our athletes’ days even better. Just as we’re deeply committed to unlocking their potential, we’re dedicated to providing a world-class, inclusive workplace where our employees can grow and thrive, too. We’re backed by Sequoia Capital, TCV, Madrone Partners and Jackson Square Ventures, and we’re expanding in order to exceed the needs of our growing community of global athletes. Our culture reflects our community. We are continuously striving to hire and engage teammates from all backgrounds, experiences and perspectives because we know we are a stronger team together.

Strava is an equal opportunity employer. In keeping with the values of Strava, we make all employment decisions including hiring, evaluation, termination, promotional and training opportunities, without regard to race, religion, color, sex, age, national origin, ancestry, sexual orientation, physical handicap, mental disability, medical condition, disability, gender or identity or expression, pregnancy or pregnancy-related condition, marital status, height and/or weight.

We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

title: Director, Maintenance
description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Overview

The Director, Maintenance manages and oversees maintenance activities across single or multiple Macy's Supply Chain network distribution centers. They lead and mentor facility maintenance teams.

What You Will Do

  • Lead and develop a team of executive and front-line colleagues to maintain all facility, site, and material handling equipment in a fast-paced, large-scale distribution environment.
  • Provide oversight and act as the facility subject matter expert for mechanical systems, fire protection, electrical, plumbing, automation equipment, material handling equipment, conveyor systems, and control systems.

  • Implement a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) methodology to support preventative and predictive practices. Maintain thorough documentation across all maintenance activities and asset histories.
  • Support the network's Root Cause Analysis procedure for equipment failures and communicate findings to benefit distribution centers across the network.
  • Develop cost-effective maintenance, energy consumption, and operational improvement opportunities for the facility and equipment.
  • Act as the Macy's representative for interactions with regulatory agencies, consultants, and local authorities at the facility level.
  • Evaluate the material readiness of assets effectively and reflect them appropriately in a capital and equipment obsolescence replacement schedule.
  • Prepare scope documents and solicit proposals for repair and construction services from third-party service providers.
  • Generate innovative, cost-effective ideas for improving existing material handling systems and optimizing product flow.
  • Serve as an advisor to the corporate engineering team for Mechanical Handling Equipment (MHE) mechanical controls regarding design, installation, and long-term maintenance plans during large-scale capital projects.
  • Collaborate closely with vendors during the installation of material handling equipment to ensure adherence to design specifications and Macy's/OSHA safety requirements.
  • Support and lead the facility in corporate initiatives surrounding Energy, Recycling, and Sustainability.
  • Foster an environment of acceptance and respect that strengthens relationships, and ensures authentic connections with colleagues, customers, and communities.

Skills You Will Need

Leadership: Demonstrated ability to lead and develop executive and front-line colleagues, as well as mentor maintenance teams.

Technical Expertise: Proficiency in mechanical systems, fire protection, electrical, plumbing, automation equipment, material handling equipment, conveyor systems, and control systems.

Financial Management: Experience in executing maintenance and housekeeping budgetary planning, with a focus on efficient financial controls.

Strategic Collaboration: Ability to collaborate with operational teams to plan and execute supply chain strategies, recommending improvements through the utilization of material handling systems and equipment.

Process Improvement: Proven track record in promoting functional procedures and methodologies that enhance building and equipment reliability, safety, and efficiency.

Project Management: Ability to evaluate asset readiness, prepare scope documents, solicit proposals, and oversee repair and construction projects.

Innovation: Capacity to generate innovative, cost-effective ideas for improving material handling systems and optimizing product flow.

Communication: Open and continuous communication skills, effectively presenting information to various stakeholders.

Decision-Making: Sound decision-making ability in managing multiple processes within a fast-paced environment.

Technical Proficiency: Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite, Computerized Maintenance Management Systems, and AutoCAD (a plus).

Sense of Urgency: Ability to prioritize tasks and act with a sense of urgency.

Analytical Skills: Strong analytical troubleshooting skills and attention to detail.

Contractor Management: Leadership experience in providing direction to contractors and collaborating effectively with building senior-level executives to support day-to-day operations.

Who You Are

  • Candidates with a High School Diploma or equivalent are encouraged to apply.
  • This position requires heavy lifting, constant moving, standing, and reaching with arms and hands.
    • Involves standing for at least two consecutive hours, lifting at least 50lbs. stooping, kneeling, crouching, and climbing ladders
    • May involve reaching above eye level
  • Requires close vision, color vision, depth perception, and focus adjustment.
  • Able to work a flexible schedule, including days, evenings, weekends, and holidays based on department and company needs.

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Merchandise discounts
  • Performance-based incentives
  • Annual merit review
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice
  • Tuition reimbursement

Access the full menu of benefits offerings here.

About Us

This is a great time to join Macy’s! Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

Join us and help write the next chapter in our story - apply today!

title: Systems Engineering Intern - Summer 2027
description:
Idaho National Laboratory is seeking a motivated intern to support our Systems Engineering team. This internship offers hands‑on experience in System of Systems development, requirements engineering, architecture design, and verification and validation activities that support innovative research and national mission needs. Interns will work alongside experienced engineers to contribute to projects that span clean energy, national security, and advanced research programs.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Support the development of System of Systems architectures, including identifying system interactions, dependencies, and integration points.
  • Assist in requirements elicitation, decomposition, and management, working with multidisciplinary teams to capture functional and performance needs.
  • Participate in architecture modeling and analysis, using established SE tools and frameworks to evaluate system behavior, interfaces, and design alternatives.
  • Support verification and validation (V&V) planning and execution, helping ensure system requirements are testable, traceable, and met by design solutions.
  • Contribute to creation of systems engineering artifacts, such as interface definitions, functional flow diagrams, requirements traceability matrices, and system behavior models.
  • Collaborate with engineers, researchers, and project managers to apply systems thinking to real‑world problems in energy, national security, robotics, and advanced technologies.
  • Participate in team discussions, design reviews, and technical evaluations to gain visibility into the full systems lifecycle.

This team works a 9x80 schedule onsite at our Idaho Falls campus. Start date and duration of internship vary based on project and student's availability.

  • Enrolled full time in an Undergraduate Degree Program majoring in Engineering, Computer Science, Applied Science, or a related technical field.
  • Interest in systems thinking, integrated systems development, or multidisciplinary engineering.
  • Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills, with the ability to think at both the component and system levels.
  • Familiarity with systems engineering concepts such as requirements, architectures, interfaces, and V&V (coursework is acceptable).
  • Experience with modeling or diagramming tools is a plus.
  • Demonstrated ability to work in teams and communicate technical concepts effectively.
  • Curiosity, adaptability, and enthusiasm for tackling complex technical challenges.

title: Infrastructure Technician III

  • Standard Work Schedule: up to 6 days a week days and evening shifts available (all shifts are subject to change upon business demands)

What You’ll Do

Lead Advanced Structured Cabling & ICT Infrastructure Work

  • Install, service, upgrade, and decommission complex structured cabling systems, including Cat5e/Cat6/Cat6A, fiber optic systems, and low voltage technologies.

  • Execute high skill work such as fusion splicing high strand ribbon fiber, terminating and testing copper and fiber, and performing advanced troubleshooting.

  • Install and remove infrastructure components including racks, cable trays, cabinets, pathways, and network devices.

Be the Subject Matter Expert Onsite

  • Apply deep knowledge of TIA/BICSI standards, building codes, and life safety requirements.

  • Conduct Fluke DSX8000 testing, OTDR testing, inspection, documentation, and remediation.

  • Install servers, rack and stack equipment, patch panels, bonding, firestopping, and cable channeling.

Lead Teams & Set the Standard

  • Mentor and guide Technicians I & II, leading by example in workmanship, professionalism, and customer service.

Deliver an Outstanding Client Experience

Ensure World-class Documentation & Project Execution

Technical Skills That Make You Stand Out

  • Deep knowledge of TIA/BICSI standards and ICT best practices

  • Patch panel installation, rack and stack, and network device mounting

  • Reading/creating port maps and technical documentation

Soft Skills That Elevate You

  • Positive “can do” attitude and strong team leadership mindset

  • Punctual, professional, and reliable

  • Exceptional client facing communication skills

  • Strong collaboration and conflict resolution abilities

  • High attention to detail and pride in workmanship

  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision

What You Bring

  • Associate degree or technical certification or equivalent work experience

  • 5+ years installing, maintaining, and troubleshooting low voltage cabling systems

  • Proven ability to install, terminate, test, and certify copper and fiber systems

  • Experience with major manufacturers (Panduit, CommScope, Corning, Leviton, etc.) preferred

  • Understanding of NEC, ANSI, TIA, EIA, and BICSI standards

  • Ability to read blueprints and construction drawings

  • Valid driver’s license and clean driving record

  • BICSI Technician Certification highly desired

  • Proficient experience installing, terminating, and testing fiber (single-mode/multi-mode connections)

  • Proficiency with various testers - Fluke, OTDR, and VFL

  • Required experience splicing fiber

Supervisory Responsibility

  • Tech III is the first level of field leadership at Black Box.

  • Leads small teams, mentors junior techs, and ensures safe, quality focused execution.

Work Environment & Physical Demands

  • Primarily indoors, occasionally outdoors

Required Tools

Snips, basic hand tools, steel/composite toe boots, VFL (preferred), cordless drill/impact, pliers, testers, punch tools, tape measure, level, flashlight/headlamp, and more.

title: Investment Analyst Intern
description:
Investment Analyst Intern

Who we are and what we’re about:

KU Endowment is an independent, nonprofit organization and the official fundraising foundation for the University of Kansas. We partner with donors in providing philanthropic support to build a greater KU.


As an employee of KU Endowment, you’ll witness firsthand the power of our donors’ generosity. You will join a talented and fun group of people who are inspired to help KU through the support of loyal alumni and friends. The Spring 2027 investment internship at KU Endowment provides an opportunity for the successful candidate to interact with some of the world’s leading institutional investment managers and work across asset classes to gain experience in portfolio construction, manager selection, risk management, and investment operations.

The KU Endowment provides a permanent source of capital to support current and future generations of Jayhawks. KU Endowment’s investment assets are divided among two pools of capital: a $2.8 billion long-term portfolio and a $500m short-term portfolio. These portfolios utilize external managers and are managed by an eight-person team located at KU Endowment’s offices on West Campus. The long-term portfolio is invested globally in a diversified set of traditional equities and fixed-income securities as well as alternatives, including hedge funds, private equity, real estate, natural resources, and alternative credit. title: Data Infrastructure Engineer-Germany
description:
About the role

Doodle is a B2B SaaS platform used by millions of professionals to coordinate meetings and collaborate across teams and companies. We're building the future of scheduling and productivity, working on hard problems where human collaboration meets digital efficiency. We craft elegant solutions to complex problems, and we're looking for passionate problem solvers who share that drive.

Our product, engineering and analytics teams rely on data every day to decide what we build next. As our Data Infrastructure Engineer, you'll bring data engineering and infrastructure together, designing, building and running the platforms that keep our data reliable, secure and easy to use. You'll work closely with our SRE, product, engineering, analytics and security teams to make data simpler for everyone.

Why join us

  • Real impact: your commits change how the world meets.

What you'll do

  • Build the platform: design, build and operate scalable infrastructure for data ingestion, transformation, storage and serving. Run streaming flows with Kafka and Avro, orchestrate batch workflows in Airflow, and keep Redshift performant, well-modeled and cost-effective.

  • Keep it reliable and secure: own SLOs, runbooks and alerts for critical data systems. Protect sensitive data through access controls, encryption, secrets management and retention policies.

  • Fix problems at the root: investigate incidents, lead root-cause analysis and implement preventative improvements.

  • Make data easy to use: improve discoverability through cataloging, lineage, ownership and quality testing, and build documentation, tooling and self-service workflows so analytics and engineering teams can work independently.

What you bring

  • 2+ years in data platform engineering or scalable software systems

  • Kafka and Avro: schema design, serialization and evolution

  • Redshift and production Airflow: data modeling and performance tuning

  • Cloud and DevOps: CI/CD, infrastructure as code and Kubernetes, plus data lakes and open table formats

  • Reliability and security: observability, incident response and debugging pipeline failures, with a security-conscious approach to data access, privacy and secrets

  • Clear communication with both technical and non-technical stakeholders

  • dbt: experience with it is a plus

Our commitment

At Doodle, we're committed to an environment of mutual trust and respect, where equal employment opportunities are available to all applicants and teammates without regard to age, race, ethnic origin, colour, disability, religion or belief, gender, gender identity or sexual orientation. Diversity and inclusion are of utmost importance to us. We're committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives and skills. title: System Engineer
description:
System Engineer – Levels I, II, III, IV, and Senior


Come join us at Bandera Electric Cooperative (BEC) and BEC Fiber, where we are lighting the grid to empower our members!

Help us Reimagine Rural America!

Established in 1938, Bandera Electric Cooperative (BEC) is a member-owned cooperative dedicated to providing exceptional service and innovative solutions to its members. BEC serves more than 30,000 members and delivers electric service to 42,000 active meters across a seven-county territory in the Texas Hill Country, with more than 140 employees. Since 2017, BEC has also offered fiber-optic broadband internet to its rural communities, and it provides behind-the-meter energy solutions, including Apolloware, an advanced real-time energy management platform, solar power installations, and energy storage systems.

Why work for BEC?

We offer Highly Competitive Wages and a Generous Benefit Package!!

Pay range: $84,400 to $227,100 annually, depending on level and experience (see level ranges under Experience below)


Health, Life and Disability Benefits (no waiting period – benefits start on first day)

  • Medical, Dental and Vision plans
  • Health Savings Account (HSA) with a generous employer contribution of $3,250 for Individual medical coverage and $6,500 for Family medical coverage
  • Company-paid Employee Life insurance and Business Travel insurance
  • Short- and Long-term disability plans
  • Supplemental Life and AD&D insurance options

Retirement Benefits

  • 401(k) employer match
  • Pension plan

Additional Benefits

  • PTO – Accrue 180 hours/4.5 weeks of PTO per year to start
  • 10 Paid holidays
  • Tuition reimbursement
  • Gym reimbursement for you and your spouse


We are looking for System Engineers to join the BEC Engineering team and help plan, protect, and build the distribution, substation, and transmission system that serves our members. Our engineers complete system planning studies, perform protection and coordination analysis, develop construction and material standards, and support engineering and project management for construction and upgrade projects, working with technicians and other engineers to ensure safe, reliable, and economical service. This posting covers five levels – System Engineer I, II, III, IV, and Senior System Engineer – and candidates will be considered for the level that matches their education, licensure, and experience. All positions report to the Engineering Director.


Duties and Responsibilities (scope, independence, and leadership increase with each level)

  • Complete planning studies, including load flows, motor starts, system planning, DG additions, capacitor/power factor, load forecast, and power quality studies, to ensure the system can adequately, reliably, and economically serve existing and future load.
  • Perform system protection analysis and coordination to ensure protective devices perform as designed, and investigate protective device mis-operations or improper coordination.
  • Prepare construction and material specifications and develop and modify standards that provide for a safe, reliable, and economic system.
  • Perform engineering and project management duties to construct and upgrade distribution, substation, and transmission facilities.
  • Work with technicians and other engineers to ensure safe operating conditions, and provide annual reports and updates on system reliability.
  • Make recommendations to management on initiatives such as distribution automation, advanced metering, SCADA, and grid resiliency plans.
  • Provide safe, efficient, and dependable service to BEC members at the lowest possible cost.
  • Provide direction, training, and guidance to coworkers and other engineers as experience level allows.
  • Stay informed of all company policies and procedures and participate in all safety and training meetings.
  • Use all personal protective equipment provided.


Qualifications and Requirements

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering (B.S.E.E.) is required for all levels.
  • Professional Engineering (PE) license is required for System Engineer IV and Senior System Engineer, and is one of the qualifying options for System Engineer III (see below).


Experience

Placement at a level is based on the candidate’s education, licensure, and experience. Pay is listed for each level; placement within a range depends on experience.

  • System Engineer I – No experience required. Entry-level position assisting with planning studies, protection analysis, and specifications under the direction of senior engineers. Pay range: $84,400 to $99,500 annually.
  • System Engineer II – Minimum of 18 months of related engineering experience and Engineer In Training (EIT) certification, or 4 years of related engineering experience. Independently completes planning studies and specifications on routine projects. Pay range: $103,000 to $125,200 annually.
  • System Engineer III – Minimum of 4 years of related work experience, and one of the following: a Professional Engineering (PE) license; 10 years of related work experience; or 8 years of related work experience and a postgraduate engineering degree. Leads moderately complex projects and owns protection and standards work. Pay range: $117,400 to $146,000 annually.
  • System Engineer IV – PE license and a minimum of 4 years of related work experience as a Professional Engineer (2 years with a postgraduate engineering degree). Leads complex projects and serves as the technical authority in a specialty area. Pay range: $140,700 to $173,600 annually.
  • Senior System Engineer – PE license and a minimum of 10 years of related work experience as a Professional Engineer (8 years with a postgraduate engineering degree). Sets engineering standards, advises management on strategy, and mentors engineers. Pay range: $162,700 to $227,100 annually.


Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Strong technical knowledge and skills in electrical engineering; depth of knowledge expected increases with level.
  • Knowledge of distribution planning studies, processes, and modeling software.
  • Knowledge of substation and transmission facilities.
  • Knowledge of protective relaying systems and the protective devices used to ensure grid resiliency.
  • Knowledge of overhead (OH) and underground (UG) design and construction specifications.
  • Familiarity with smart grid initiatives, AMI and MDM systems, GIS, OMS, distribution automation, and distributed energy resources.
  • Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills with sound engineering judgment.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, organizational, and time-management skills.
  • Strong attention to detail.
  • Ability to work with increasing independence, managing engineering projects with minimal supervision at higher levels.
  • Ability to provide direction, guidance, and mentoring to other engineers at higher levels.
  • Must have valid Texas driver’s license and related insurance.
  • Must pass background check and drug screening.


Working Conditions

The working conditions for this position involve a fast-paced environment with tight deadlines and a focus on multiple tasks and projects, including complex or varied tasks. The work environment is primarily an office setting, with a focus on computer work and analysis using engineering software and tools; when needed, this position requires working outdoors in all weather conditions. The position may require occasional travel, including overnight travel, to other locations within the Cooperative. Tobacco free, professional office environment.


Physical Requirements

Sit for prolonged periods; reach and extend the arms, with a focus on chest-to-shoulder movements; and perform wrist flexion and extension. Occasional walking and standing are required. Sensory demands include hearing, speech, near vision, and far vision.


BEC is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Sygeplejerske til vores endoskopiteam i sammedagskirurgisk afsnit
description:
Drømmer du om en sygeplejestilling, hvor faglighed, teknik og nærværende patientpleje mødes? Så har du nu muligheden for at blive en del af vores velfungerende endoskopiteam.

Sammedagskirurgisk afsnit i Næstved er en del af en stor anæstesiologisk afdeling og arbejder udelukkende med elektive ambulante forløb.

Vores afsnit består af fire endoskopiske undersøgelsesstuer og en tilhørende opvågningsstue, som vi selv bemanter. Vi assisterer til koloskopier og gastroskopier på en bred patientgruppe, hvoraf en stor del er henvist i pakkeforløb på mistanke om cancer. Derudover anlægges PEG-sonder, og vi har en stue om ugen, hvor patienterne skoperes i fuld anæstesi samt et tilbud om skopi i NAPS.

Vi har desuden to operationsstuer, hvor vi arbejder inden for det ortopædkirurgiske speciale med blandt andet hånd- og fodkirurgi, knæartroskopier, korsbånds- og skulderoperationer og hofteskopier.

Vi søger dig, der

  • er uddannet sygeplejerske og har minimum 2 års erfaring fra endoskopi, operation- eller somatisk sengeafsnit.
  • har lyst til at udvikle dine kompetencer inden for endoskopi
  • trives med at arbejde med avanceret teknisk udstyr
  • har blik for både patienten, proceduren og det gode samarbejde
  • kan bevare overblikket og handle sikkert, også når situationen ændrer sig
  • har lyst til at være en aktiv del af et stærkt fagligt fællesskab.

Du skal blandt andet

  • modtage, informere og udskrive patienter
  • observere og reagere på patientens tilstand før, under og efter proceduren og i forbindelse med sedation
  • assistere aktivt under endoskopiske undersøgelser
  • medvirke til høj kvalitet, patientsikkerhed og god hygiejne
  • være med til at skabe trygge, sikre og sammenhængende patientforløb – fra patienten møder os til de går hjem. Også selvom patientens kontakt med os er kort og fokuseret.

Vi tilbyder dig

  • et stærkt fagligt miljø med erfarne sygeplejekolleger
  • at du aldrig står alene med en opgave
  • en grundig introduktion og et oplæringsforløb tilpasset din erfaring og kompetenceprofil
  • en mulighed for at udvikle dine kompetencer inden for endoskopi
  • en synlig og nærværende daglig ledelse
  • en struktureret hverdag med fokus på den enkelte patient

Vi arbejder kontinuerligt med arbejdsmiljø, psykologisk tryghed og trivsel. Det har skabt en kultur, hvor vi hjælper hinanden, spørger hinanden til råds og løfter opgaverne sammen. Vi tror på, at et godt arbejdsmiljø skaber vi sammen – gennem respekt, faglig nysgerrighed, samarbejde og ikke mindst godt humør i hverdagen.

Afsnittet har åbent mandag–fredag kl. 07.30–16.00. Stillingen er pt. vagtfri og som udgangspunkt på fuld tid. Dog kan et ønske om 32 til 36 timer ugentligt drøftes.

Har du lyst til at blive en del af vores team?

Ansættelsessamtaler forventes afholdt 19/11 og 23/11.

Du er meget velkommen til at kontakte os for yderligere oplysninger eller en rundvisning.

Ansættelsen er betinget af modtagelse af tilfredsstillende børneattest

Ansættelsesområde

Region Sjælland og Region Hovedstaden bliver den 1. januar 2027 til Region Østdanmark som følge af sundhedsreformen. Dit ansættelsesområde vil være Region Østdanmark med alle tilhørende organisatoriske enheder.
Læs mere om betydningen af ansættelsesområdet på Region Østdanmarks hjemmeside.

Startløn for overenskomstansatte

Regionen er forpligtet til at oplyse dig om startlønnen for stillingen. Du får oplyst grundløn, centralt fastsatte tillæg og pension i den relevante overenskomst. Udover startlønnen, kan lønnen indeholde eventuelt forhandlede tillæg afhængigt af stillingen, dine erfaringer og kvalifikationer.
Se startlønnen på regionens hjemmeside

Om Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital

På Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital arbejder vi hver dag for at fremme det sunde liv ved at forebygge og behandle i en sammenhængende sundhedsindsats. Som hospital forener vi psykiatri og somatik. Vores mål er, at patienter og borgere oplever gode og trygge forløb af høj kvalitet.

Som medarbejder bliver du en del af et nytænkende, fagligt og organisatorisk robust hospital, hvor vi gør en forskel for de mennesker, der har brug for os. Læring og udvikling er en del af hverdagen og sker i fagligt forpligtende fællesskaber. Også på tværs af afdelinger.

Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital dækker et opland på ca. 230.000 borgere. Vi har 766 sengepladser og er omkring 5.000 ansatte fordelt på 20 afdelinger, herunder 16 somatiske og psykiatriske specialer.

Vi tilbyder et solidt forskningsmiljø med 13 professorer og et stærkt fagligt uddannelsesmiljø, hvor vi hvert år byder cirka 2.700 studerende, elever og læger i videreuddannelsesforløb velkommen.

title: Patient Services Representative, Psychiatry, Full time, First Shift
description:
At UC Health, we're proud to have the best and brightest teams and clinicians collaborating toward our common purpose: to advance healing and reduce suffering.

As the region's adult academic health system, we strive for innovation and provide world-class care for not only our community, but patients from all over the world. Join our team and you'll be able to develop your skills, grow your career, build relationships with your peers and patients, and help us be a source of hope for our friends and neighbors.

UC Health is committed to providing an inclusive, equitable and diverse place of employment.

The patient services representative will serve as the main point of contact for all patients. This position will interact with all patients as they enter, leave, or request assistance within any of our facilities. The patient services representative will exemplify customer service while ensuring each patient interaction is handled with care.

Engages in population appropriate communication. Has knowledge of growth and development milestones and tasks. Gives clear instructions to patients/family regarding treatment. Involves family/guardian in the assessment, initial treatment and continuing care of the patient. Identifies any physical limitations of the patient and deploys intervention when necessary. Recognizes and responds appropriately to patients/families with behavioral health problems. Interprets population related data and plans care appropriately. Identifies and responds appropriately to different needs resulting from, unique psychological needs or those associated with religious / cultural norms. Performs treatments, administers medication or operates equipment safely. Recognizes and responds to signs/symptoms of abuse or neglect.

Front Office Flow:

  • Warmly greet patients with eye contact and a smile as they enter and leave the clinic. Answer any questions patient may have. Coordinate day of patient scheduling changes or adjustments. title: Assembly Technician
description:
About Us

South Bay Solutions is a high-precision machine shop, making parts for semiconductor, medical devices, and advanced tech hardware. Our tolerances are measured in microns, our equipment is top-of-the-line, and our team is passionate about quality craftsmanship.


Assembly Technician

South Bay Solutions is committed to achieving 100% customer satisfaction through exceptional attention to detail, teamwork, and a strong dedication to quality. We are currently seeking an experienced and dependable Assembly Technician to join our team. The Assembly Technician will be responsible for assembling parts and components in accordance with manufacturing documentation and ensuring that all completed assemblies meet customer quality requirements and company standards.


Openings : 2

Schedule

Day Shift: Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–4:30 PM


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Assemble parts and components by following applicable manufacturing documentation, work instructions, and assembly procedures.
  • Perform basic mechanical assembly operations, including the installation of Helicoils, Dowel Pins, and other related components.
  • Inspect completed parts and assemblies to ensure they meet specified requirements, tolerances, and quality standards.
  • Use precision measuring instruments, including calipers and height gauges, to verify dimensions and specifications.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment at all times.
  • Properly maintain assembly equipment, tools, and workstations to ensure they remain in good working condition.
  • Collaborate closely with the Quality Control Department to ensure all assemblies meet customer and company quality requirements.
  • Accurately complete and maintain Job Traveler documentation throughout the assembly process.
  • Identify and report equipment malfunctions, unsafe conditions, defects, or other hazardous conditions to the appropriate supervisor.
  • Follow all applicable safety procedures, manufacturing requirements, and company policies.
  • Perform other job-related duties and responsibilities as assigned.



Qualifications and Skills

The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience in a manufacturing or machine shop environment and possess the following qualifications:

  • 1–2 years of experience in machine shop assembly, with specific experience installing Helicoils and Dowel Pins.
  • Ability to read, understand, and interpret simple blueprints, drawings, and assembly documentation.
  • Ability to accurately follow written assembly instructions and manufacturing procedures.
  • Proficiency in using calipers, height gauges, hand tools, box cutters, and other common assembly tools.
  • Excellent hand-eye coordination and manual dexterity, particularly when working with small components in a controlled manufacturing environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing high-quality work.
  • Basic mathematical skills, including the ability to perform measurements and basic calculations.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
  • Strong commitment to workplace safety, quality, accuracy, and productivity.



Education and Experience

  • High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent required.

title: Head of Catastrophe and Emergency Response
description:
Why Join Stand: At Stand, you’ll help build a new class of global property protection. We use advanced physics and AI to model catastrophic risk at the asset level, then automate underwriting and mitigation before loss occurs. Insurance is simply the current delivery mechanism. The real product is a scalable risk engine, our Stand World Model.

We stay when traditional insurers exit. We model what others approximate. And we build systems that change outcomes, not just prices.

Our leadership team includes former successful founders and CEOs from Metromile, PolicyGenius, WePay, and HotelTonight, bringing deep experience in building and scaling high-growth companies.

Background: The property insurance industry is built to price loss after it happens. It relies on coarse proxies, backward-looking data, and manual processes, then accepts damage as unavoidable.

Stand takes a different approach. We simulate how real-world catastrophes affect individual properties, translate that into actionable decisions, and automate the business around it. The result is a platform that can underwrite what others can’t and operate with far less friction.

The role

Stand is a homeowners insurance carrier for people who live where wildfire and hurricanes are a fact of life. The promise we make them is unusual: we try to reach you before the loss and get you help, and we handle the claim fast when it comes. This role owns both ends of that promise.

Right now there is no single person who owns catastrophe readiness and response across Stand. Someone has to build the plan before a season, hold our claims partners to a real standard every day, and then run the whole thing when an event is bearing down on our customers. Without that, the promise is a slogan; with it, it's something a homeowner can count on.

Concretely, the job is three things. You build and keep current the catastrophe plan, covering activation levels, who does what, vendor capacity, regulatory reporting, and how we reach customers and brokers. You manage the third-party administrators who handle our claims, day to day and against their service standards. And you own the Emergency Response Program: the work that finds policyholders in the path of an event and gets them help, increasingly automated, with people kept in the loop for the judgment calls.

You report to the Head of Claims and Client Experience and work across the company. You'd partner with Product and Engineering on the automation, with Underwriting and the market teams on where our exposure sits, and with our TPAs and field vendors every week. When an event hits, you lead the response and brief leadership. This is an in-office role in Austin.

What you'll do

  • Own the catastrophe plan across every peril and state we write, including activation levels, roles, vendor capacity, regulatory reporting, and customer and broker outreach. Keep it current and tested with a tabletop before each season.

  • Run the response when an event hits: call the activation level, lead the daily team call, direct the TPAs and field vendors, brief leadership, and put Stand people on the ground at insurance villages and with our hardest-hit customers.

  • Manage our claims TPAs day to day, including staffing, open inventory, escalations, large losses, and payment approvals within your authority. Hold them to their service standards with a regular scorecard, closed-file audits, and remedies when they slip.

  • Own the Emergency Response Program end to end: watch active events, decide when a property needs monitoring, outreach, or a vendor deployment, and direct it remotely.

  • Work with Product and Engineering to automate exposure analysis, deployment recommendations, and customer and broker outreach, extending the approach from one peril to the next while keeping the judgment calls with people.

  • Own the vendor bench across field response, mitigation, housing, contents, engineering, and independent adjusting firms. This includes contracts, standby terms, capacity, and performance, reviewed ahead of each season.

  • First 30 days: a read-out on where the current plan, TPA standards, and vendor bench actually stand, with the biggest gaps named.

  • First 3 months: a written catastrophe plan signed off by leadership and a tabletop run with each TPA, with gaps logged and closed.

  • First year: TPA scorecards running on a regular cadence with remedies applied, a vendor bench with standby terms across every active peril and state, automated exposure analysis and outreach live for the lead peril, and a response you've run cleanly through a live event or exercise.

What we're looking for

  • You've led property claims through real catastrophe events, calling the response, directing adjusters, and holding quality steady while everything is moving fast. Hurricane experience is a strong plus.

  • You've managed TPAs or independent adjusting firms: set and enforced service standards, watched capacity and pricing, and run scorecards that actually changed behavior.

  • You know state catastrophe reporting requirements and claim-handling deadlines well enough to keep a carrier compliant across several states.

  • You can run a live response from both the office and the field, and make fast, sound calls when the information in front of you is incomplete.

  • You're comfortable building from a blank page in a small, fast-moving company. There's no playbook handed to you, no large team under you yet.

Nice to have

  • Wildfire experience.

  • You've scoped automation with product and engineering teams and held them to a timeline.

  • Underwriting, inspection, or mitigation experience alongside claims.

  • Florida or high-net-worth property experience.

  • You've built or run an emergency response program before.

You're probably not a fit if

  • You want a mature playbook and a built-out team to step into. Most of this you'll build yourself.

  • You'd rather stay at the desk; this role goes to the ground when an event hits.

  • You're looking for predictable hours. Catastrophe season has no rhyme or reason.

Benefits:

  • Above-market Health, Dental, and Vision coverage

  • Weekly lunch stipend

  • Flexible time off + holidays

  • 401(k) plan

  • Commuter benefits

  • PAT & MAT Leave

  • Short-Term and Long-Term Disability

  • Monthly team gatherings

  • In-office perks

AI in the Interview Process

Thoughtful use of AI tools is expected and valued at Stand. Candidates should be prepared to discuss how they use AI, how they evaluate its output, and how it informs their work. Strong communication, sound judgment, and the ability to clearly articulate experience and decision-making remain core requirements.

Some parts of the interview process are designed to assess independent thinking, communication, and problem-solving. If you plan to use an AI assistant or LLM during any portion of an interview, please discuss it with your interviewer in advance.

Work Authorization

Candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S. Stand does not sponsor new work visas. We can consider candidates on TN visas, O-1A visas, or H-1B transfers with three years or more remaining.

Equal Opportunity Employment

Stand is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. We believe that diversity enriches the workplace, and we are committed to growing our team with the most talented and passionate people from every community.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals. If you require assistance, please contact us at hr@standinsurance.com.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

AI Use in Hiring

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us at hr@standinsurance.com.

title: Software Engineering, Team Manager
description:
Job Title - Software Engineering, Team Manager

Description - Lead engineering teams that support critical assessment services, with two opportunities across Vue Testing Services and Test Delivery in India. You will combine people leadership, delivery oversight, technical judgement and responsible AI adoption to strengthen team performance and customer outcomes. Also known in the market as: Engineering Manager; Software Development Manager; Technology Manager; Software Engineering People Manager.

About the Role

Pearson is hiring two Software Engineering Team Managers in India through one recruitment campaign. The roles share a common leadership profile but support different product areas: Vue Testing Services (VTS) and Test Delivery.

VTS supports services around a candidate’s assessment journey, including registration, payment and score reporting. Test Delivery powers the delivery of assessments in test centres and online, in a high-volume environment where quality, reliability and operational readiness matter.

In either opportunity, you will lead through clarity, coaching, accountability and partnership. You will translate priorities into achievable plans, strengthen engineering and delivery practices, develop people, manage risk and help teams adopt AI-assisted development responsibly. This is a management role with minimal hands-on coding expected.

What You’ll Do

  • Hire, onboard, coach, develop and retain engineers and technical professionals.

  • Set clear goals, feedback rhythms, development plans and team operating practices.

  • Translate product and department priorities into achievable team plans, capacity choices and ownership.

  • Track sprint and release progress, dependencies, blockers, defects, quality and immediate delivery risks.

  • Partner with Product, Architecture, Quality Engineering, DevOps, Security, Operations and business stakeholders.

  • Maintain strong standards for design, testing, automation, security, observability, documentation and operational readiness.

  • Use engineering, delivery, quality and team signals to identify patterns and drive improvement.

  • Guide deliberate adoption of AI-assisted development, testing, review and documentation while protecting quality and security.

What We’re Looking For

  • A hands-on technical foundation in software engineering, quality engineering, architecture, technology solutions or a closely related discipline.

  • Demonstrated experience leading, coaching or managing technical professionals and building effective teams.

  • Experience delivering software products, platforms or technology services in Agile or similarly iterative environments.

  • Evidence of leading meaningful change, making sound decisions and improving delivery or team effectiveness.

  • Working knowledge of modern software delivery, cloud, DevOps, CI/CD, automation, security, reliability, observability and operational readiness.

  • Experience making people, capacity, priority and delivery decisions in a cross-functional environment.

  • Experience working across distributed teams, functions or time zones.

  • Practical experience using or introducing AI-assisted engineering tools, with sound judgement about quality and risk.

  • Strong communication, collaboration, problem-solving and stakeholder-influence skills.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Business, or equivalent practical experience.

The Opportunities

VTS Lead teams supporting services around the assessment journey, including registration, payment and score reporting. Product and service-platform leadership experience may be particularly useful.

TEST DELIVERY Lead teams supporting the delivery of assessments in test centres and online. Experience with high-volume, operationally critical or reliability-focused platforms may be particularly useful.

Location & Working Pattern

India. Bangalore is the preferred location and Chennai is an option. Exact hybrid attendance requirements will be shared during the recruitment process.

Why Join Pearson?

This is an opportunity to develop engineering talent, strengthen delivery and quality practices, and help teams adopt emerging AI-assisted ways of working across technology that supports assessment experiences at scale.

title: Data Engineer II
description:
About mPulse: mPulse is the leader in conversational AI and member engagement for healthcare. We partner with the nation's most innovative health plans — Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, and Commercial — to engage members in conversations that close care gaps, improve Stars ratings, and drive better health outcomes. Our platform reaches tens of millions of Americans and is built on the belief that better health starts with better conversations.

Job Summary:

mPulse is seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented Data Engineer II to join our Data Engineering team. In this role, you will design, develop, and maintain scalable data pipelines and platform capabilities that support our analytics, product, and AI/ML initiatives.

Our data platform processes high-volume, high-velocity healthcare data, enabling insights and data-driven solutions for a growing client base. You will work cross-functionally with Data Operations, Product, Analytics, and Data Science teams to ensure data is reliable, performant, and aligned with business needs.

The ideal candidate brings strong experience in SQL, Python, dbt, and Airflow, along with a solid foundation in data warehousing and a passion for solving complex data challenges in a healthcare environment.

Duties/Responsibilities:

  • Design, develop, and maintain scalable data pipelines (ETL/ELT) to support ingestion, transformation, and delivery of high-volume healthcare data.
  • Write, optimize, and maintain complex SQL queries for data transformation, validation, and performance tuning.
  • Develop and manage workflow orchestration using Apache Airflow, including DAG creation, monitoring, and troubleshooting.
  • Enhance and scale data platform capabilities to support analytics, product features, and AI/ML use cases.
  • Build and maintain data quality frameworks, including automated data profiling, validation, and testing processes.
  • Monitor and optimize pipeline performance, reliability, and efficiency in production environments.
  • Analyze complex data issues, identify root causes, and implement scalable solutions, clearly communicating findings to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams (Data Operations, Product, Analytics, Data Science) to gather requirements and deliver high-quality data solutions.
  • Partner with clinical and analytics teams to operationalize data-driven insights and reporting solutions.
  • Contribute to documentation of data pipelines, data models, and engineering processes to support maintainability and knowledge sharing.

Skills/Abilities/Experience:

  • Strong proficiency in SQL, including complex querying, data transformation, and performance optimization.
  • Proficiency in Python for data processing, automation, and integration tasks.
  • Experience designing and building data pipelines (ETL/ELT) to support data ingestion, transformation, and delivery.
  • Hands-on experience with modern data warehousing platforms, such as Snowflake, PostgreSQL, Amazon Redshift, or Microsoft SQL Server.
  • Experience with workflow orchestration tools, particularly Apache Airflow (DAG development, debugging, and maintenance).
  • Experience using dbt (data build tool) to develop, test, and manage modular data transformation workflows.
  • Experience working with cloud platforms, particularly AWS (e.g., S3, RDS, Lambda, Glue, DMS).
  • Experience with version control systems and collaborative development workflows, such as GitHub or Bitbucket.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD practices and tools, such as Jenkins or GitHub Actions.
  • Experience supporting data quality initiatives, including data profiling, validation, or monitoring frameworks.
  • Familiarity with data modeling and data warehousing concepts, including dimensional modeling.
  • Exposure to analytics, reporting, or data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Looker) is a plus.
  • Experience working with healthcare data, including claims or clinical datasets, is a plus.
  • Familiarity with data science or machine learning workflows from a data engineering perspective is a plus.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 3+ years of professional experience in data engineering or a related field.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work with complex datasets and identify root causes.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to effectively communicate technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

description:
