title: Reliability Engineer
description:
Arconic creates breakthrough products that shape industries. Working in close partnership with our customers, we solve complex engineering challenges to transform the way we fly, drive, build and power. Through the ingenuity of our people and cutting-edge advanced manufacturing techniques, we deliver these products at a quality and efficiency that ensure customer success and shareholder value.

Arconic Aluminum Extrusions serves the global aerospace and automotive markets with the most specialized engineering, highest quality, and the greatest breadth and depth of forgings and extrusions. Our vertically integrated capabilities and deep materials science expertise in aluminum and titanium structural casting is taking the industry to new heights. AEX is a business unit of Arconic.

The Reliability Engineer is responsible for developing and implementing asset reliability strategies that improve equipment performance, reduce unplanned downtime, and enhance overall manufacturing effectiveness. This role serves as a technical resource for maintenance and operations teams by utilizing reliability engineering principles, preventative and predictive maintenance technologies, data analysis, and structured problem-solving methodologies to identify and eliminate chronic equipment issues. The Reliability Engineer works closely with production, maintenance, engineering, and leadership teams to improve asset health, optimize maintenance practices, and support long-term business objectives

The Reliability Engineer within AEX requires technical and interpersonal skills essential to teamwork. Major duties include but are not limited to:


• Develop and implement reliability strategies that improve equipment availability and reduce asset-related losses.
• Lead root cause failure analysis (RCFA) investigations and implement corrective actions to eliminate recurring equipment failures.
• Utilize predictive and condition-based maintenance technologies to identify equipment degradation and reduce risk of failure.
• Analyze equipment performance data, maintenance records, and reliability metrics to identify improvement opportunities and drive asset reliability initiatives.
• Support the development and optimization of preventive and predictive maintenance programs.
• Partner with operations, maintenance, and engineering teams to improve equipment performance, reliability, and maintainability.
General duties for the Reliability Engineer include but are not limited to:
• Monitor asset performance and reliability trends to identify chronic losses and prioritize improvement activities.
• Facilitate failure mode and effects analyses (FMEA), asset criticality assessments, and other reliability-centered maintenance processes.
• Develop and maintain equipment standards, maintenance task lists, and reliability documentation.
• Assist in the implementation and sustainment of lubrication excellence, precision maintenance, and asset care programs.
• Implement and track reliability KPIs across the business units that align and support the business objectives
• Develop and continuously improve work management processes, including work identification, prioritization, planning, scheduling, backlog management, and execution practices to enhance workforce efficiency and asset reliability.

Required Qualifications:
• Minimum 3 years of manufacturing maintenance experience
• Bachelor of Engineering degree from an accredited institution
• Employees must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Verification of employment eligibility will be required at the time of hire. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.
• This position requires access to controlled technology, as defined in the Export Administration Regulations (15 C.F.R. §730, et seq.) and/or the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). Qualified candidate must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the relevant government agency. Business demands may require employer to proceed with candidates who are immediately eligible to access controlled technology.


Additional Preferred Qualifications:
• 5-10 years of manufacturing maintenance or engineering experience
• Experience in implementing reliability-focused strategy
• Experienced at blueprint and schematic reading and interpretations
• Experience with data-driven equipment performance monitoring.
• Reliability Certifications (CMRP, CRL, CRE, ASQ, SMRP, Life Cycle Institute Programs, etc.)
• Experience with CMMS systems and maintenance-planning processes (incl. FMEA, Control Plan)
• Ability to implement and drive changes to the plant reliability program.
• Ability to work alone or with a team
• Ability to read and interpret detailed mechanical and electrical drawings
• Strong focus on safety.
• A deep knowledge of industrial equipment (forging, robotics, and CNC equipment are a plus), process controls, maintenance planning systems, condition-based monitoring, and TPM.
• Experience with analytics and predictive technologies for preferred candidates
• An understanding of equipment maintenance actions within the reliability framework from a data perspective
• Strong analytic problem solving by developing and using structured approaches to identify root causes and recommend resolutions
• Project Management skills and ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously to meet objectives and key deadlines
• Good verbal and written communication skills.

title: Event Specialist
description:
Event Specialist EMEA – 6-month Contract Position
Location: London, UK
Schedule: Monday-Friday
Hybrid

CSC is looking for an organized, proactive, and commercially minded Event Specialist to join our Events team in our London office located in Canary Wharf.

This exciting opportunity will support the planning and delivery of a varied portfolio of events across EMEA, ranging from conferences, sponsorships, and industry events to client receptions, networking events, and larger CSC brand experiences. You will play a key role in supporting the delivery of the EMEA event roadmap, ensuring our activities align with broader commercial and brand objectives.

Reporting to the Senior Event Specialist, you will work closely with colleagues across Marketing and the wider organization to deliver a consistent, high-quality approach to events. You will act as a collaborative partner to key stakeholders, while contributing to the development and maintenance of event best practices. Maintaining strong standards across budget management, reporting, and return on investment (ROI) will also be central to the role.

This is a hands-on role suited to someone who is highly organized, confident working with multiple stakeholders and suppliers, and comfortable managing several events and competing deadlines simultaneously. The successful candidate will combine strong attention to detail with a proactive, solutions-focused approach and a genuine interest in creating impactful client experiences.

Key responsibilities
• Manage the end-to-end planning and delivery of assigned events across EMEA, ensuring they are delivered on time, within budget, and to a high standard.
• Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders, acting as a subject matter expert and providing proactive guidance throughout the planning process.
• Manage external venues and suppliers, including sourcing, briefing, negotiation, and ongoing coordination.
• Oversee all key event logistics, including attendee management, branding, production, catering, registration, setup, and onsite delivery.
• Manage event budgets, maintaining accurate forecasts and ensuring spend is commercially responsible and aligned with agreed objectives.
• Maintain accurate event data and reporting, including registrations, attendance, leads, budgets, and post-event results.
• Evaluate event performance against agreed objectives, capturing feedback, key learnings, and opportunities to improve future activity.
• Contribute to the development and implementation of event best practices, processes, and standards across the wider Events team.
• Manage event setup and delivery within Cvent, including registration sites, event communications, and reporting.
• Work proactively with internal stakeholders to support invitation activity, monitor registrations, and drive attendance against agreed event targets.
• Work with Salesforce and internal teams to support contact selection, event tracking, and post-event lead management.
• Provide hands-on operational support across the event portfolio, including preparing, packing, and shipping event collateral and promotional items, coordinating couriers and deliveries, and ensuring materials arrive at and return from events as required.
• Support the wider Events team with administrative and operational tasks as required, particularly during busy event periods.

What we are looking for
• 5 years' experience in events, preferably within a corporate, professional services, financial services, or agency environment.
• Experienced in managing multiple events and deadlines simultaneously, whilst tracking ROI
• Confident taking ownership of events rather than relying on step-by-step direction.
• Outstanding interpersonal and communication skills – must be able to communicate clearly and with authenticity to senior leadership and stakeholders.
• Organized and professional candidate that is confident working independently with guidance, as well as able to work collaboratively in a team environment.
• Collaborative and willing to support the wider team during busy periods.
• Comfortable working in a fast-paced, international environment.
• Proficient in Microsoft Office, particularly PowerPoint, Excel and Outlook.
• Excellent written English, proofreading and research skills.
• Willing and able to travel within the UK and internationally when required, sometimes at short notice.
• Willingness to work outside of 9-5 office hours as required.
• Ideally a Bachelor's degree in Event Management, Marketing, or a related field.

What success looks like
Success in this role means being a proactive, dependable, and collaborative member of the Events team who takes ownership of their work and is willing to get involved in every aspect of event delivery.

You will be a genuine team player with a hands-on approach, equally comfortable managing
stakeholders and suppliers as you are supporting with the practical, behind-the-scenes tasks that contribute to a successful event. You will be adaptable, solutions-focused, and willing to step in and support colleagues when priorities shift or workloads increase.

Ultimately, you will become a trusted member of the team who can independently manage assigned events, communicates proactively, takes pride in delivering work to a high standard, and contributes positively to a supportive and collaborative team culture.

title: Security Watch Center Analyst
description:
Security Watch Center Analyst

Key Responsibilities

  • Incident Management & Response — Assist with the coordination and analysis of security incidents as they occur, verifying that documentation is accurate and complete, response actions are logged in real time, and all required follow-up actions (referrals, notifications, corrective actions) are tracked to closure.

  • Workplace Violence Incident Analysis — Review and help coordinate the handling of workplace violence (WPV) incidents and threat assessments, ensuring proper documentation and routing to HR, Employee Relations, and Security Management per established protocols (e.g., WAVR-21-informed assessment). Identify the safety hazard(s) each incident exposes — physical access, insider threat indicators, gaps in reporting or escalation — and track the corresponding mitigation (post order changes, access control adjustments, training, follow-up monitoring) through to implementation and verification.

  • Everbridge Monitoring & Briefing — Monitor Everbridge mass-notification and situational-awareness feeds, extract information with direct relevance to MWD facilities, staff, or operations, and prepare concise briefs for Watch Center leadership and SEMU management so that external events are translated into MWD-specific operational impact rather than raw alert traffic.

  • Report Writing & Documentation — Prepare incident reports, shift/operational summaries, and performance assessments that support management decision-making and continuous improvement. Maintain consistent reporting standards across shifts so incidents are comparable and searchable over time.

  • Crime & Incident Trend Analysis — Analyze incident and crime-related data across all sources — Watch Center logs, WPV cases, dispatched calls, and technology-generated data — to identify trends, emerging threats, and operational vulnerabilities. Produce recommendations that support security planning and resource allocation.

  • Robodog Deployment Reporting — Review weekly robodog (autonomous patrol) reports from desert facilities and Lake Mathews, verify completeness and flag anomalies or coverage gaps, and roll findings into the broader incident trend analysis so patterns detected by autonomous patrol are addressed with the same rigor as officer-reported incidents. Track how identified trends (e.g., recurring perimeter activity, equipment faults, coverage blind spots) are being attended to — assigned owner, corrective action, and status — until resolved.

  • Operational Decision-Making — Apply analytical and critical-thinking skills to evaluate rapidly evolving situations, synthesize incomplete information, and provide sound recommendations to Watch Center leadership during high-pressure or escalating incidents.

  • Watch Center Staff Support — Assist with daily administrative and operational functions, including resource coordination, scheduling support, performance monitoring, and adherence to established policies, procedures, and post orders.

  • Systems & Process Improvement — Evaluate current Watch Center workflows and recommend improvements, best practices, and efficiencies that increase consistency and service quality, including how incident, robodog, and Everbridge data feed into a single trend-reporting pipeline.

Compliance & Quality Assurance — Monitor that personnel maintain required qualifications, certifications, and training in accordance with contract standards; support staffing-requirement compliance and broader quality assurance efforts

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior exposure to workplace violence threat assessment processes or willingness to be trained in a recognized framework (e.g., WAVR-21).

  • Experience supporting critical infrastructure, utility, or large-campus security operations.

  • Familiarity with contract security operations (post orders, staffing compliance, vendor performance monitoring).

  • Prior training or mentoring responsibilities in a shift-based operations environment.

title: Part-Time Systems Analyst III
description:
Position Title:

Part-Time Systems Analyst III

Job Group:

Professional & Scientific

Bachelor’s degree and 5 years of related experience

Job Description:

The Center for Survey Statistics and Methodology (CSSM) within The College of Liberal Arts and Science is seeking a qualified Part-Time Systems Analyst III. CSSM specializes in the research and practice of sample surveys.

CSSM has functioned as a collaborator for federal and state agencies, nonprofit organizations, and other campus units. Building on the expertise of Iowa State University’s Department of Statistics, CSSM has developed extensive capabilities in the technical and operational aspects of data science and sample survey research. Its cross-disciplinary workforce includes statisticians, data collectors, data analysts, software developers, GIS specialists, IT service and infrastructure personnel, communication specialists, and technical writers, who work across two branches: Data Science Services (DSS) and Survey Research Services (SRS).

DSS primarily collaborates with the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Natural Resources Conservation Service (USDA-NRCS) on projects such as the National Resources Inventory (NRI) and the Conservation Effects Assessment Project (CEAP), as well as with the U.S. Department of the Interior’s Bureau of Land Management on rangeland surveys. SRS conducts data collection for surveys across a range of formats and modes, including the Iowa Farm and Rural Life Poll and the Housing Provider Study.

This is a part-time, fully remote position that requires strong communication, organization, and the ability to work independently.


Example of Duties:

  • Performs QA/QC of NRI imagery and geospatial data received from contractors.
  • Investigates and resolves imagery alignment issues, rectification discrepancies, and spatial anomalies.
  • Supports NRCS imagery processing, calibration, and geospatial workflows.
  • Verifies annual CRP datasets for NRI survey use.
  • Ensures geospatial deliverables meet national accuracy and quality standards.
  • Develops Python scripts, data pipelines, and geospatial tools to improve efficiency.
  • Designs and manages end-to-end geospatial workflows for complex spatial datasets.
  • Develops and maintains the RSL Tracker application to monitor production workflows.
  • Identifies workflow bottlenecks and implements process and technology improvements.
  • Coordinates imagery production, processing, review, and QA for regional projects, including Alaska NRI.
  • Coordinates schedules, milestones, technical specifications, and deliverables with contractors and partners.
  • Monitors contractor compliance with requirements, data standards, and timelines.
  • Serves as a senior technical resource for complex NRI geospatial operations.
  • Provides technical guidance, mentoring, and support to staff and project partners.
  • Collaborates with NRCS, FSA, contractors, and other partners to resolve geospatial issues.
  • Develops SOPs, protocols, and technical documentation for geospatial processes.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with geospatial data, GIS, and remote sensing applications.
  • Experience with Python scripting, ArcGIS, QGIS, or ERDAS.
  • Experience developing and managing geospatial data workflows and automation tools.
  • Experience with data quality assurance/quality control and large, complex datasets.
  • Experience coordinating technical projects and working with contractors or multi-agency partners.

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. on an ongoing basis without sponsorship. Immigration sponsorship is not available for this position.

title: Senior Director of Missionary Discipleship
description:
Senior Director of Missionary Discipleship
Our Lady of the Falls Catholic Community
810 Pearl Street, Chippewa Falls, WI 54729

"To abide together with Jesus and invite others into His family."

To Apply to this Opportunity and view other Open Career Opportunities at Our Lady of the Falls Catholic Community follow this link: https://app.dover.com/jobs/ourladyofthefalls

Reports To: Pastor
Status: Full-time, salaried

Salary: $72,000
Schedule: Variable hours, including evenings and weekends
Location: Our Lady of the Falls Central Office, 810 Pearl Street, Chippewa Falls, and all five parish campuses

Help Five Parishes Move From Maintenance to Mission

Five parishes in Chippewa Falls are walking forward together as Our Lady of the Falls Catholic Community: St. Charles Borromeo, St. Peter, Notre Dame, Holy Ghost, and St. Bridget. Each keeps its own identity and history. All five share one mission.

We're looking for a leader who has been discipled, who disciples others, and who wants to build something that lasts. This is a rare chance to shape how a whole community of parishes forms missionary disciples. That includes faith formation, youth ministry, family life, healing ministry, outreach, and service to the poor. If you've ever thought, "Our parish could do so much more if the ministries worked together," this role was written for you.

Position Summary

The Senior Director of Missionary Discipleship leads the planning and oversight of our parish ministries, both those that serve our own people and those that reach beyond our doors. The work is grounded in three essential habits: Divine Intimacy, Virtuous Friendship, and the Little Way of Evangelization.

You'll work closely with the Pastor to carry his vision for missionary discipleship into every ministry. You'll lead by personal accompaniment. That means walking with and supporting the leaders of Faith Formation, Youth Ministry, Outreach and Evangelization, Healing Ministry, Discipleship, Family Life, and Social Justice.

The goal is simple to say and hard to do: move our parishes from maintenance to mission at every key moment of discipleship. You'll do it by building mentorship teams that care for the whole person at every stage of life.

What You'll Do

Lead the Vision

  • Work with the Pastor and Parish Leadership Team to build, carry out, and track a long-term plan for parish growth and evangelization using the Win, Build, Send model

  • Give direction, accompaniment, and accountability to every parish ministry department, making sure each program is faithful to Catholic teaching and serves the mission of Our Lady of the Falls

  • Lead regular ministry staff meetings that break down silos, share resources, and plan major parish-wide events like parish missions and stewardship campaigns

Form and Support Your Team

  • Supervise, support, and evaluate professional ministry staff and key volunteer coordinators

  • Mentor staff and volunteer leaders in leadership, team building, volunteer recruitment, and pastoral care

  • Serve as the main point of contact for resolving overlaps between programs, volunteer concerns, and day-to-day ministry challenges

Raise Up Lay Leaders

  • Build ways to identify, invite, and match parishioners' gifts to ministry, so people move from sitting in the pew to living as active disciples

  • Create one consistent process across all ministries for onboarding, screening, training, and thanking volunteer leaders

  • Build a lasting pipeline of lay leaders who can run small groups, service committees, and parish organizations on their own

Steward the Work Well

  • Review and combine annual budgets for all ministry departments, and bring recommendations to the Director of Finance and Facilities and the Pastor

  • Review the master parish calendar with the Director of Administration and Communications to make the best use of space and prevent scheduling conflicts between ministries

  • Partner with the Director of Administration and Communications so ministry promotion, bulletins, the website, and social media all share one clear message

Keep Our People Safe

  • Oversee and enforce all diocesan safety requirements, making sure volunteers are cleared before they serve

  • Confirm every active volunteer has completed a criminal background check, fingerprinting when required, and Protect and Heal mandated reporter training

  • Keep accurate, confidential digital records of each volunteer's status, and make sure no one who hasn't been cleared serves in restricted ministries, especially those with youth or vulnerable adults

Who You Are

You love Jesus Christ and His Church, and it shows in how you lead. You know what it's like to be mentored in the faith, and you've walked with others as they grew into missionary disciples. You think in systems and you care about people, and you don't see those as competing. You can hold a long-term vision and still remember to follow up on meeting action items.

Qualifications

  • Practicing Catholic in good standing, devoted to prayer and the sacraments, and passionate about serving the Church and the mission of Our Lady of the Falls

  • Bachelor's or master's degree in pastoral studies, theology, church management, business administration, or organizational leadership highly preferred

  • Five or more years of professional leadership experience, ideally leading teams in a large parish, diocese, or Catholic nonprofit

  • A proven ability to manage people, work through conflict, and lead different kinds of teams toward a shared goal

  • Comfort with Microsoft Office or Microsoft 365, email, calendars, databases, and standard office technology

  • Willingness to learn parish management and church administrative software

  • Successful completion of all diocesan background checks and Protect and Heal training

Catholic Identity and Mission

  • Respect for and commitment to the teachings, mission, and ministry of the Catholic Church

  • Personal experience both being discipled and mentored, and accompanying and forming missionary disciples

  • Support for the spiritual and pastoral mission of our parishes

  • A welcoming, service-minded presence with parishioners and visitors

  • Support for parish policies, diocesan requirements, and appropriate standards of confidentiality and professional conduct

Core Competencies

  • Servant leadership: Builds teams and mentors ministry leaders with generosity, patience, and a willingness to help

  • Collaboration: Works independently while partnering well with clergy, staff, volunteers, and parishioners

  • Adaptability: Manages competing priorities and shifting schedules across a busy five-parish community

  • Executive skill: Brings strong strategic planning, project management, and budget oversight

  • Communication: Writes clearly, speaks well one-on-one, and is confident in front of a group

Physical and Work Requirements

  • Regular work across all five parish campuses

  • Ability to sit, stand, walk, use standard office equipment, and occasionally lift or move office and ministry materials

  • Frequent evening and weekend hours, as the ministry requires

Equal Opportunity and Ministry Statement

Our Lady of the Falls is committed to a professional, respectful, and welcoming workplace. Employment is subject to applicable parish and diocesan policies, the requirements of the Catholic Church, and the expectations of this position as a ministry of the parish.

title: Staff Product Manager
description:
What We Do

We’re on a mission to empower animal healthcare professionals with opportunities to earn more and achieve greater flexibility in their careers and personal lives.

Powered by groundbreaking technology, Roo has built the industry-leading veterinary staffing platform, connecting Veterinarians, Technicians, and Assistants with animal hospitals for relief work and hiring opportunities. Roo empowers the largest network of over 20,000 veterinary professionals to help more than 9,000 animal hospitals provide quality care to more pets.
Together, we’ve provided more than 3 million hours of healthcare, helping Veterinarians earn more than $200 million.

As a Staff Product Manager at Roo, you’ll play a pivotal role in driving company-wide impact by leading high-priority initiatives that map directly to our most critical business goals. You’ll partner with cross-functional teams—including engineering, design, data, marketing, operations, and more—to define strategy, align stakeholders, and deliver measurable outcomes. You’ll set the vision, define the north-star metric, establish clear success criteria, and ensure we’re executing with focus and speed.

Your north-star metric will be directly tied to the “Roo Equation,” our guiding business model, ensuring your impact is visible and meaningful. Operating with significant autonomy, you’ll take a growth-minded, iterative approach—identifying leverage points, shipping improvements quickly, and building scalable systems for our customers and internal users.

This role reports to the VP of Product. While the position is remote, occasional travel to our San Francisco co-working space for key meetings and team events is expected.

Your Responsibilities

  • Own the path from sign-up to first shift which includes identity and license verification, the approval decision, first-run experience, and the flow from browsing to requesting to working. Decide what gets automated and what stays human.
  • Build the product for high-volume relief vets: recurring bookings, multi-shift blocks, durable hospital relationships, and the calendar and earnings tooling that makes Roo their default rather than one of several apps.
  • Turn promotions and incentives from operator-run levers into product such as targeting, automation and guardrails that decide where a dollar goes.
  • Partner with the BU's growth marketer as a pair, not a handoff: shared conversion targets, joint experiments, and a standing argument about where the bottleneck actually is.
  • Fix the instrumentation before the roadmap. Work with the BU analyst on cohort definitions, attribution and holdouts so we ship what we can prove.
  • Co-own the BU strategy with the GM to help decide what we do and don't do, carry the product half, and say out loud when a committed lever isn't working.
  • Keep one marketplace. Your decisions land on hospital screens too; partner with the PMs in the other BUs so users get one product, not our org chart.

Qualifications

  • Marketplace experience or commerce depth. 5+ years working on supply, demand, or core marketplace teams. Ideally in high-growth environments. Strong commerce or consumer-platform backgrounds with equivalent funnel depth are welcome.
  • Funnel depth. You've owned real surfaces across the funnel (e.g. search, recommendations, acquisition, onboarding, activation, retention) and you know where the leverage sits in each.
  • Commercial fluency. You're comfortable in the unit economics of a business (take rate, price, contribution margin, payback, etc) and can hold your own in a conversation about margin, not just engagement.

title: Director, AI Scientist & Product Lead – Drug Discovery
description:
About Us:

Structure Therapeutics develops life‐changing medicines for patients using advanced structure‐based and computational drug discovery technology. The company’s platform combines the latest advancements in visualization of molecular interactions, computational chemistry, and data integration to design orally available, superior small molecule medicines that overcome current limitations of biologic and peptide drugs. We are advancing a clinical‐stage pipeline of differentiated treatments focused on chronic diseases with high unmet need, including cardiovascular, metabolic, and pulmonary conditions.

With offices in California and Shanghai, Structure Therapeutics has the benefit of being at the center of life science innovation in both the US and China and capitalizing on the strengths of each geographic location.



Position Summary:

We are seeking a Director, AI Scientist & Product Lead, Drug Discovery to lead the strategy, development, and adoption of artificial intelligence capabilities for our discovery organization in China. This is a player-coach role for a leader who can move fluently among science, data, technology, and product execution. The role works directly with structural biologists, medicinal and computational chemists, biologists, pharmacologists, and other research colleagues to turn important scientific problems into trusted, usable AI products.

The Director will own the Discovery AI product portfolio from opportunity identification and scientific problem definition through design, prototyping, launch, adoption, and value realization. The role requires sufficient technical depth to engage hands-on in data and modeling strategy, experimental design, evaluation, and prototype development, together with the product judgment and leadership presence to align diverse stakeholders and deliver capabilities that improve research decisions.

This individual will be a senior scientific and product partner to local research teams and a core member of the global AI organization. They will collaborate closely with AI scientists, engineers, product leaders, data specialists, and technology partners in the United States to create secure, scalable, and reusable enterprise AI capabilities. Although drug discovery is the role's primary mandate, the Director will help shape shared platforms and methods that can support translational medicine, preclinical development, CMC, clinical development, medical affairs, and commercialization.



Job Responsibilities:

Lead the Discovery AI Product Strategy

  • Develop and own a multi-year AI product vision, roadmap, and portfolio for drug discovery, aligned with research strategy and measurable scientific and business priorities.
  • Partner with discovery leaders and scientists to identify high-value opportunities across target and mechanism assessment, structural biology, hit identification, lead generation and optimization, compound design, assay interpretation, developability, knowledge management, and portfolio decision-making.
  • Translate scientific needs into clear product hypotheses, user requirements, data requirements, success metrics, validation plans, and delivery roadmaps.
  • Prioritize initiatives based on scientific value, technical feasibility, data readiness, time to evidence, risk, scalability, and potential for adoption; recommend when to build, buy, partner, or stop.
  • Maintain a balanced portfolio of near-term workflow improvements, strategic data and platform capabilities, and scientifically ambitious applications of AI.

Provide Scientific & Technical Leadership

  • Shape AI/ML approaches for small-molecule discovery, including methods that may use molecular representations, sequence and structure information, functional and biochemical assay data, SAR, docking, biophysical evidence, imaging, literature, and internal scientific knowledge.
  • Guide the development and evaluation of predictive, generative, retrieval, and agentic capabilities while selecting methods appropriate to the scientific question and available evidence.
  • Work hands-on where it adds the most value—for example, interrogating data quality, defining modeling cohorts and labels, reviewing analyses and code, prototyping approaches, evaluating model behavior, and interpreting results with scientists.
  • Establish rigorous evaluation strategies, including leakage-resistant and scaffold-aware validation, prospective testing, benchmark comparisons, calibrated uncertainty, applicability-domain assessment, and analysis of failure modes.
  • Ensure that model outputs are scientifically interpretable and traceable, with the supporting evidence needed for researchers to make informed decisions.
  • Promote closed-loop learning by capturing experimental decisions and positive and negative results in forms suitable for governed analysis and model improvement.



Own Products from Discovery Through Adoption

  • Lead cross-functional product teams through discovery, definition, design, build, validation, launch, and continuous improvement.
  • Co-design workflows with end users so AI capabilities fit naturally into scientific practice and complement expert scientific judgment.
  • Define product and scientific success measures such as prospective enrichment, prediction quality and calibration, cycle-time reduction, decision confidence, user adoption, and impact on experimental productivity.
  • Partner with software, data, ML, cloud, security, and enterprise-architecture colleagues to convert prototypes into reliable, supportable products.
  • Drive pilot and validation studies with explicit baselines, preregistered decision criteria where appropriate, and clear paths from proof of concept to scaled use.
  • Lead change management, training, feedback collection, and product iteration to ensure that released capabilities are understood, trusted, and routinely used.

Serve as the AI Partner to China Discovery Research

  • Build trusted working relationships with structural biology, chemistry, pharmacology, DMPK, computational science, and research leadership teams.
  • Facilitate multidisciplinary problem-solving sessions that connect biological hypotheses, chemical design, structural evidence, experimental constraints, and quantitative methods.
  • Surface local scientific needs and data realities early, represent them in global product decisions, and ensure solutions work in the research environment.
  • Act as a translator across scientific, technical, and executive audiences, communicating both the potential and the limitations of AI with clarity.
  • Develop internal AI fluency through coaching, demonstrations, office hours, communities of practice, and hands-on collaboration with project teams.

Connect the Global AI Organization

  • Operate as an integrated member of the global AI team, sharing ownership of architecture, product standards, reusable components, evaluation methods, and delivery practices.
  • Coordinate effectively across multiple time zones, maintaining clear decisions, documentation, interfaces, and accountability.
  • Identify where discovery solutions can benefit from or contribute to shared enterprise capabilities such as scientific knowledge systems, governed data products, model services, agent frameworks, evaluation infrastructure, identity and access controls, observability, and human-review patterns.
  • Contribute discovery expertise to AI initiatives spanning translational medicine, preclinical development, CMC, clinical development, medical affairs, and commercialization while protecting the focus and delivery capacity required for discovery.
  • Build productive relationships with external technology and scientific partners when they provide differentiated value, and support technical and scientific due diligence.

Uphold Responsible AI, Data & Scientific Governance

  • Embed data stewardship, privacy, intellectual-property protection, cybersecurity, reproducibility, and appropriate documentation throughout the product lifecycle.
  • Partner with legal, compliance, quality, IT, and scientific colleagues to determine proportionate controls for each use case.
  • Preserve human accountability for high-consequence scientific decisions and define explicit evidence and governance gates before increasing automation.
  • Monitor product and model performance after launch, including data drift, model limitations, scientific failure modes, adoption barriers, and unintended use.
  • Set a high standard for honest scientific communication, distinguishing exploratory signals from validated findings and avoiding unsupported claims of AI impact.

Leadership

  • Personally contribute hands-on to the hardest scientific and product questions while creating the structure, clarity, and momentum that enable others to succeed by bringing scientists along.
  • Lead multidisciplinary teams through influence and shared purpose, including colleagues who do not report directly to this role.
  • Coach scientists and technical contributors in product thinking, experimental rigor, responsible AI, and effective cross-functional collaboration.
  • Help define the longer-term capability and talent needs for discovery AI and support selective team growth, partnerships, and community building.

Qualifications:

  • PhD in computational chemistry, cheminformatics, computational biology, structural biology, bioinformatics, computer science, statistics, applied mathematics, or a related discipline; or equivalent advanced expertise demonstrated through relevant industry accomplishments.
  • 5 or more years of relevant industry experience, including significant leadership of AI-enabled drug-discovery products or programs; exceptional candidates with a different experience profile will also be considered.
  • Experience integrating chemistry, biological assay, structural, and translational data to support compound design or prioritization.
  • Experience with prospective model validation and design–make–test–analyze cycles, including collaboration with medicinal chemists and experimental scientists.
  • Familiarity with modern molecular ML, generative chemistry, structure-based methods, scientific foundation models, knowledge graphs, retrieval-augmented generation, or agentic scientific workflows.
  • Experience building governed scientific data products and integrating with research platforms such as electronic lab notebooks, compound registration systems, assay repositories, chemical-design platforms, or scientific knowledge bases.
  • Experience converting prototypes into production-grade capabilities in partnership with ML engineering, software engineering, data engineering, and cloud-platform teams.
  • Experience evaluating external vendors, research collaborations, or technology partnerships and managing sensitive scientific data appropriately.

title: Senior GTM Systems & AI Lead
description:
Position Overview

Diligent is the AI leader in governance, risk and compliance (GRC) SaaS solutions, helping more than 1 million users and 700,000 board members to clarify risk and elevate governance.

Diligent’s GTM Systems and AI team owns the systems, data, integrations, and AI capabilities behind how we go to market. We’re strengthening the foundations of our GTM environment while expanding how we use AI to improve work across Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, and Operations.

As a Senior GTM Systems & AI Lead, you’ll lead complex improvements across our GTM systems. You’ll fix foundational issues such as incomplete or unreliable data, broken integrations, disconnected workflows, and overlapping AI agents. You’ll also identify, build, and scale AI- workflows that make our teams more effective.

This is a senior, hands-on individual contributor role. You’ll investigate problems, recommend priorities, design solutions, and lead initiatives from definition through rollout and measurable impact. You won’t need to be a traditional software engineer, but you should be highly technical and comfortable working with APIs, SQL, system integrations, MCP, LLMs, and AI coding tools.

We’re early in building this function, so you’ll have meaningful influence over the roadmap, architecture, standards, and ways of working. You’ll report to the Director, GTM Systems and GTM AI.

This role offers flexible working arrangements, with the option to work on a hybrid or fully remote basis. Applicants must be based in the United States.

Regrettably we are unable to provide visa sponsorship, so you must be eligible to work in the US.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Design and build the systems and AI behind how we go to market: connect our GTM systems, automate processes between them, and use AI to make teams faster and data more reliable
  • Find manual or inefficient GTM processes and design, build, and scale AI-enabled workflows, agents, and automations to fix them, using GTM systems and AI coding tools with metrics, evals, and guardrails
  • Own initiatives end to end, from problem definition through rollout and impact, and build reusable systems and patterns rather than one-off agents
  • Work across Sales, Customer Success, Ops, and Marketing as our lead GTM Systems SME: take a problem, shape it into a clear solution, and build the MVP, working with cross-functional teams as needed
  • Connect GTM systems through APIs, orchestration platforms, webhooks, MCP, and other integration patterns while keeping system-of-record data accurate and consistent
  • Drive adoption of what ships and set the standards for how the team builds
  • Identify fragmented or overlapping agents and automations. Consolidate them into maintainable systems with clear ownership, reusable components, appropriate guardrails, and measurable value

Examples of what you might build

  • The missing orchestration/MCP layer connecting our dozen+ GTM tools without a bespoke integration project each time
  • A self-serve automation marketplace other teams can request and extend without filing a ticket and waiting
  • Signal-scoring automation that doubles down on our highest-converting signals and proves ROI on every tool renewal

What success looks like

  • Built a clear understanding of our GTM systems, data flows, integrations, automations, and existing AI agents
  • Identified and prioritized the foundational issues creating the greatest operational risk or friction
  • Improved the reliability of critical data flows and automations while reducing recurring failures
  • Established clearer ownership and standards for GTM integrations, agents, and automated workflows.
  • Begun shipping AI-enabled solutions that reduce manual work or improve how our GTM teams operate
  • Created a practical roadmap that balances foundational systems work with new AI capabilities

These are the essentials you’ll need to get an interview:

  • Significant experience working across GTM Systems, Revenue Operations, Business Systems, or a related function, typically gained through five or more years of relevant work
  • Hands-on experience building with LLMs and agent frameworks, and fluent with AI coding tools like Claude Code, Codex or any similar tools
  • Deep understanding of GTM systems, data, and processes across functions such as Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, and Operations
  • Technical fluency with APIs, webhooks, integration and orchestration platforms, data flows, and system architecture

Behavioral Skills:

  • Self-starter who can take a business problem from a cross-functional team, define it, and build the AI or automation solution yourself, comfortable in ambiguity
  • Strong systems thinking. You can distinguish symptoms from root causes and design solutions that remain reliable as the business and technology stack evolve
  • Senior-level influence: leads cross-functional initiatives, raises the bar for how others build, and explains tradeoffs to technical and non-technical leaders up to VP level

It would be great if you had these to, but we’ll support you if you don’t:

  • Experience with MCP, RAG, agent evaluation, observability, or governance tooling
  • Experience using Python or JavaScript to troubleshoot, extend, or maintain automations and integrations
  • Experience rationalizing overlapping agents, automations, integrations, or GTM tools
  • Experience establishing standards and reusable patterns for AI-enabled workflows
  • Experience improving systems and data through M&A, rapid growth, or significant organizational change
  • Experience measuring adoption, productivity gains, data-quality improvements, or business outcomes from systems and AI initiatives
  • Experience of working within a B2B SaaS environment

ICUC is creating a new leadership role to own our automation and AI strategy across the business. This is a product and innovation mandate, not a workforce-efficiency one: the Director, Product Automation is responsible for how AI and automation get built into the actual work we do for clients — community management, strategy, insights, monitoring, and social listening, so our teams can work faster, with more precision, and with sharper focus on the client.

Automation & AI Strategy

  • Evaluate, pilot, and select tools and technologies that make our core services - community management, strategy, insights, monitoring, and social listening - faster, more precise, and more scalable, without compromising the quality clients expect.

description:

This is a hands-on, delivery-focused role for someone who already writes solid Java and wants to grow fast in a modern cloud environment. You will build and maintain the services behind our multi-tenant SaaS platform, working shoulder to shoulder with the squad's Digital Architect, who will review your code, guide your technical decisions, and help you level up, and other software developers. We are looking for someone who writes clean, tested code, asks good questions, takes feedback well, and finishes what they start.

Primary mission: Deliver well-tested, production-ready backend features for our cloud-native SaaS products, under the technical guidance of the squad's Digital Architect.

Key stakeholders: Digital Architect (direct manager), Squad Software Developers, Product Manager, Data/AI Engineers.

Employment type: Full-time

Jobs to Be Done: Lead the Frontend Engineering Team: Manage, grow, and set the technical direction for all frontend engineers. Own hiring, code review standards, individual development plans, and the allocation of frontend capacity across squads and platform work. Feature Development: Implement backend features and REST APIs in Java (Spring Boot) for our SaaS products, from a defined ticket through to a running service in production. Testing as Part of the Work: Write unit and integration tests for everything you build. Tests are part of the deliverable, not a separate task to be done later. Code Review Participation: Submit small, reviewable pull requests and act on review feedback quickly. Review your peers' code and learn from theirs. title: Patient Benefits Coordinator
description:
OPENED: 10/09/2026

CLOSE: 10/26/2026


POSITION DESCRIPTION


POSITION: PATIENT BENEFITS COORDINATOR


RESPONSIBLE TO: Patient Services Manager

SALARY: Step Range: 9 ($17.80) - 28 ($31.21); Full Benefits

CLASSIFICATION: Non-Management, Full-Time, State Funded


LOCATION: Klamath Tribal Health & Family Services

Healing Place, Klamath Falls, Oregon and/or

Medicine Place, Chiloquin, Oregon


BACKGROUND: P.L. 101-630 Level


POSITION OBJECTIVES


The primary purpose of this position is to function as an advocate for patients in the effective utilization of alternate resources such as Medicare, Medicaid, Department of Veterans Affairs (DVA), Bureau of Employment Compensation (BEC), Private Insurance Billing (PIB, Children’s Special Health Services, Aid to Families with Dependent Children (AFDC), Oregon Health Plan, etc. The primary responsibility of this position is to ensure that all patients who are eligible for alternate resources are identified, contacted and encouraged to apply for and maintain eligibility for available benefits.


MAJOR DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


1. Determine eligibility of patients referred to by Klamath Tribal Health & Family Services’ staff. Provide a response describing initial action taken to the referring staff within three working days upon receipt of referral. Maintain chart notes within the EHR/PM Patient Benefits Notes section and Alternate Resource Master Log documenting all actions taken regarding referral


2. Work closely with Patient Registration, Third Party Billing, Contract Health Services and other front-line staff to ensure all patient information is current, accurate and that all alternate resources are utilized.


3. This position will provide back up for Patient Registration and assist in maintaining current and accurate patient data in the database being utilized by Klamath Tribal Health. This will involve interviewing and screening new and existing patients and informing Patient Registration staff so that the appropriate changes can be made. The Patient Benefits Coordinator may make the changes with approval from the supervisor.


4. Ensure maximal identification of persons who have or are eligible for alternate resources by effectively implementing screening and interview methods.


5. Work closely with all facility staff in identification and proper utilization of all alternate resources available to all patients who utilize Klamath Tribal Health & Family Services, giving emphasis to those who reside in the Klamath Tribes’ Health Service area (Klamath County). Alternate Resources are those that provide direct health assistance for the client, for example Medicaid and Medicare.


6. Assist patients and their families with processing all applications for alternate resources, for example Medicaid and Medicare. Provide interpretation of the rules and regulations from the organization supplying the benefit, as well as the rules governing Tribal/IHS services. Review with patients what is covered and how to use those services. This may require occasional travel to the patient’s home to acquire documentation, assist with applications or to interview the patient for additional information.


7. Transmit all applications for alternate resources to the appropriate agency; track and monitor the processing of applications. Document all activities within the EHR/PM Patient Benefits Notes section and Alternate Resource Master Log.


8. Track all applications for alternate resources throughout the processing period. Follow up to ensure all required information and documentation have been submitted, monitor application status and renewal/end dates, and take timely action to prevent missed deadlines or lapses in coverage. The Patient Benefits Coordinator will contact the patient following application submission to identify and obtain any additional information or documentation needed to complete the application process. Document all follow-up attempts, communications, and actions taken in accordance with department procedures.


9. Follow up on all pending eligibility claims and work closely with families and agencies to see that patients are not discriminated against because of their dual role as a citizen and as a Tribal Health/IHS recipient.


10. Keep patients and staff up to date on regulatory changes by researching, updating and sharing information on alternate resources.


11. Document all work activities on finding/maintaining/assisting with alternate resources on the “notes page” of the patient’s chart in the current database system being utilized by Klamath Tribal Health.


12. Develop and maintain a network of contacts in local, state and federal agencies to better assist patients in developing other resources, including all agencies and organizations that provide alternate resources for health care. Identify a contact at the agency who can assist the patient with detailed applications for Social Security Administration (SSA), Department of Human Services Tribal programs AFDC, Supplemental Social Security Income (SSI), etc.


13. Responsible for maintaining an accurate daily log of activities; log of visits with patients noting the chart number, the time and what action was taken, (i.e. home visit to complete application, advocate work at the local DHS office, etc.); submit log to Patient Services Manager for review each week.


14. Assist clients with initial applications for disability determination through the Social Security Administration by providing information on how to apply online, by mail or in-person. Staff may also assist the client in making contact with an agency or individual of their choice who specializes in disability assistance.


15. Assist clients in enrolling into health insurance plans through Oregon’s state-based marketplace.


16. Submit monthly and annual reports to the Patient Services Manager. Submit quarterly reports to the Office of Medical Assistance Programs as agreed to by contract

17. Assist patients eligible for KTHFS Tribal Premium Sponsorship Programs with applications for enrollment, relay information regarding program eligibility, and program benefits.


18. Screen upcoming KTHFS appointments (Medical, Dental, YFGC, etc.) daily, as assigned by the Patient Services Manager, to verify active health insurance coverage or potential eligibility for alternate resources for those who are uninsured. Place appropriate alerts in the patient’s chart and make reasonable efforts to screen the uninsured patients for potential alternate resources. Document screening efforts and outcomes in the patient’s EHR/PM notes section.


19. Attend meetings, trainings, and other professional development opportunities hosted by external collaborative entities when requested by Patient Services Manager.


20. Like all employees of the Klamath Tribes, the incumbent will be called upon to accomplish other tasks that may not be directly related to this position, but are integral to the Klamath Tribes’ broader functions, including but not limited to, assisting during Tribal sponsored cultural, traditional, or community events that enable the successful operation of programs and practices of The Klamath Tribes as aligned with The Klamath Tribes’ Mission Statement. Some of these tasks may be scheduled outside of regular work hours, if necessary.


SUPERVISORY CONTROLS


The Patient Benefits Coordinator works under the direct supervision of the Patient Services Manager. Assignments are performed according to various established office procedures using set standards. New assignments are provided in detail, as well as changes in current procedures. Major or new issues are referred to supervisor. Work is checked for accuracy, adequacy, and timeliness.


After initial training, recurring assignments are completed independently. Completed work is spot checked for accuracy, adequacy and timeliness, and compliance with policies and procedures.


KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES


Knowledge of and the ability to maintain strict confidentiality of medical and administrative records adhering to the standards for health record-keeping under HIPAA and Privacy Act requirements.


A working knowledge of Medicare/Medicaid, SSA, DSS and Tribal programs and other related agencies policies and procedures to assist patients in application for alternate resources.


Knowledge of the eligibility requirements for Medicare/Medicaid, SSI, OHP, in order to determine who is eligible for alternate resources.


A working knowledge of sensitivity communication practices and interview techniques in order to speak with and for the patient.


Possess basic knowledge of how to establish registers of eligible patients in various programs to determine who is eligible for alternate resources.

Must be proficient in typing and computer skills. Emphasis will be on accuracy and attention to detail. Ability to use IBM compatible PC, MS Word, MS Excel, MS Office, and ability to learn RPMS program necessary for data tracking.

• REQUIRED to maintain strict patient confidentiality and adhere to the standards for behavioral health record-keeping and HIPAA requirements.

title: Call for CVs: Training Associate
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Internal and external candidates will be considered for this vacancy. For the purposes of this vacancy, internal candidates are defined as staff members holding a regular, fixed-term or short-term graded or ungraded contract, including Junior Professional Officers (JPOs), staff on Special Leave Without Pay (SLWOP), UN Volunteers with at least twelve (12) months of continuous service in IOM, and staff members on secondment/loan released by the Organization, unless otherwise specified in their contract. Staff members holding a regular, fixed-term or short-term graded contract will not retain their contract type if appointed to an ungraded position.

Organizational Context and Scope

IOM Ireland has been operating in Ireland since 2001, currently in following areas of migration management: Assisted Voluntary Return and Reintegration, Resettlement, Family Reunification, Counter-Trafficking, Protection, Integration Support to Beneficiaries of Temporary Protection, Integrated Immigration Governance and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS).

IOM provides mental health and psychosocial support to international protection seekers residing in the Citywest accommodation facility with the aim to improve their psychosocial well-being and to strengthen their overall resilience.

Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission in Ireland, the Head of the MHPSS Unit and in direct supervision of Senior Training Associate, the incumbent will be accountable and responsible for the delivery of Trauma-Informed Practice training (Supportive Spaces initiative) to accommodation centre staff and other personnel working with International Protection Applicants.

  1. Support the implementation of the Supportive Spaces training plan and prepare for the delivery of training sessions in line with the approved curriculum and materials.
  2. Deliver Supportive Spaces training sessions to designated participants in accordance with the approved training methodology and materials.
  3. Collect participant feedback and evaluation data to measure learning outcomes, participant satisfaction, and training effectiveness.
  4. Maintain accurate training records, attendance registers, evaluation results, and other required programme documentation in accordance with project requirements.
  5. Contribute to the preparation of monthly activity reports by providing accurate training statistics, participant data, and narrative updates as required.
  6. Maintain up-to-date knowledge of the Irish international protection system, relevant safeguarding principles, and current policies, standards, and best practices relating to the support and inclusion of International Protection Applicants.
  7. Perform such other duties as may be assigned by the Senior Training Associate.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Development, Psychology, Political or Social Sciences, Law, International Relations or a related field from an accredited academic institution with a minimum three years of relevant professional experience. OR
  • High School degree with five years of relevant professional experience

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • Proven experience designing, facilitating, and evaluating training programmes, including delivery of sensitive or trauma-informed content.
  • Demonstrated experience providing psychosocial support, safeguarding, or wellbeing-focused services to refugees, asylum seekers, migrants, or other vulnerable populations.
  • Experience collaborating with statutory, community, and non-governmental organisations in Ireland; existing knowledge of the refugee protection and integration landscape is desirable.
  • Strong understanding of international protection, displacement, integration, safeguarding, and trauma-informed practice, with the ability to apply relevant standards and best practices in training delivery.
  • Experience in working in a multi-cultural environment is an advantage.
  • Previous experience with international organizations, NGOs, EU Agencies and/or Irish law enforcements or Government’s Departments would be an asset.

Skills

  • Interpersonal skills (i.e. empathy and emotional resilience).
  • Intercultural competence and communication skills.
  • Culture-specific knowledge.
  • Strong organizational, facilitation, and presentations skills.
  • Computer literacy in standard software applications (MS Office, etc.)
  • Strong analytical and documentation skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary and multicultural team.
  • Experience in trauma-informed care or psychosocial support (desirable).
  • Knowledge of community mental health or humanitarian contexts (desirable).

Languages

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 1

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Notes

Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

This post is subject to local recruitment. Only persons holding a valid residence and work permit in Ireland will be eligible for consideration.

As the right to live and work in Ireland is required, the contract issued may be shorter than the period mentioned in the advertisement, in order to align with expiry date of the work permit.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

Establishes, monitors, and maintains productivity and quality benchmarks for CDI staff; initiates corrective action when necessary; keeps leadership informed; and may delegate portions of the CDS performance evaluation content preparation, rounding meetings, and/or audit feedback to appropriate CDI Coordinators.

title: Asset Protection Detective, Palisades Center - Part Time
description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Overview

As an Asset Protection Detective, you will help protect company assets, reduce shortage, and support a safe, customer-focused shopping environment. Using surveillance, investigative tools, and strong partnerships with store teams and law enforcement, you will identify and respond to theft, recover merchandise, and help protect our customers, colleagues, and business.

Why This Role Matters

Asset Protection Detectives play an important role in reducing loss while maintaining a safe and welcoming store environment. Through training, observation, investigation, and de-escalation, this role helps protect company assets, support colleagues, and ensure customers can shop with confidence.

How Our Asset Protection Colleagues Spend Their Day…

  • Our colleagues begin each day energized and ready to make an impact. They greet teammates with a warm hello. Before they get started, they review updates and department information so they're fully informed and ready to engage with confidence.

  • We believe service starts with each other - supporting one another with honesty, care, and collaboration so we can better serve our customers and communities.

  • And we know that excellence is a journey - we strive to improve every day, take pride in our work, achieve sales goals and learn from each other to deliver individual and store results.

Full-time colleagues are typically scheduled to work 30 or more hours per week, while part-time colleagues are typically scheduled 12-24 hours per week. All schedules contain weekend shifts as part of the requirements. Hours are dependent on business needs and colleague availability. Information regarding hours per week needed for benefit eligibility purposes can be found here.

What To Expect

  • Use surveillance techniques, investigative tools, and reporting systems to help identify theft, dishonest activity, and shortage trends.

  • Partner with Asset Protection leaders, store teams, and law enforcement to support investigations and protect company assets.

  • Apply de-escalation tools and sound judgment to help maintain a safe environment for customers and colleagues.

  • Prepare clear documentation, statements, and evidence to support investigations, audits, and legal proceedings.

  • Support team readiness by training colleagues on protocols that help protect company assets.

How You’ll Make an Impact

  • Help protect customers, colleagues, and company assets by identifying, investigating, and responding to theft and dishonest activity.

  • Use surveillance techniques to support the apprehension of shoplifters and dishonest employees, while following company policies and legal requirements.

  • Recover stolen merchandise and provide statements, evidence, and documentation to support investigations.

  • Prepare timely and accurate reports related to theft incidents, investigations, audits, and assigned activities.

  • Build strong partnerships with store colleagues, Asset Protection leaders, and law enforcement to support investigations and shortage reduction.

  • Maintain compliance with company policies and legal standards related to apprehensions, searches, and evidence preservation.

  • Testify in court for criminal and civil cases, as needed.

  • Respond to alarm calls, support special assignments, and facilitate first aid for customers and colleagues when needed.

  • Foster an environment of acceptance and respect that strengthens relationships with colleagues, customers, and communities.

Skills That Matter

Must Have

  • Ability to observe, identify, and respond to suspicious activity in a retail environment.

  • Strong communication skills with the ability to partner effectively with customers, colleagues, leaders, and law enforcement.

  • Ability to use sound judgment, de-escalation tools, and company procedures to support a safe environment.

  • Ability to handle proprietary, sensitive, and confidential information with discretion and integrity.

  • For jobs in New York, a current New York State Security Guard License is required.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in retail, customer service, asset protection, security, investigations, or law enforcement.

  • Ability to prepare accurate reports, statements, and documentation related to incidents and investigations.

  • Experience using surveillance systems, reporting tools, or investigative technology.

  • Ability to train or coach colleagues on asset protection protocols, shortage reduction, or safety practices.

Physical Activities You Will Perform

  • This role involves performing essential job functions such as communication, collaboration, and use of office and computer systems. Responsibilities include the ability to access and review written and electronic information, and to move within the work environment and interact with workplace materials as needed to carry out job responsibilities.

  • Position requires prolonged periods of standing/walking around store or department.

  • May occasionally involve reaching above eye level, stooping, kneeling, or crouching.

  • Must be able to apprehend shoplifters.

  • Ability to sustain long periods of time enclosed in surveillance areas.

  • Frequently lift/move up to 30lbs.

  • Requires close vision, color vision, and ability to adjust focus.

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Merchandise discounts
  • Performance-based incentives
  • Annual merit review
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice

Access the full menu of benefits offerings here.

About Us

This is a great time to join Macy’s! Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

Join us and help write the next chapter in our story - Apply Today!
